Santino: They told me if I said anything to anyone... they'd come back for my mother. Matt: Do you know where they took Claire? Santino: No. Santino: I'm sorry... Matt: Those men are going to hurt her because of me. Matt: No, it's not your fault, Santino. Matt: It's mine. Matt: Is there anything else you heard or saw? Matt: Anything that might help me find her? Santino: I saw them get into a taxi. Santino: But not in the back, in the front. Santino: Like it was theirs. Matt: What was the company? Matt: Did you see a name? Santino: Veles. Veles Taxi. Matt: Yes.

location: Italian restaurant - Fisk and Vanessa's dinner
scene_text: Vanessa: I hope you like it. Fisk: It's delicious. Fisk: I don't know much about wine. Fisk: My assistant, he recommended it. Vanessa: Maybe I should be out with him. Fisk: That was a joke. Vanessa: Yes, of course. Vanessa: A bad one, but... mmm... Vanessa: You don't do this much, do you? Fisk: No. Fisk: I've been preoccupied... for a long time. Fisk: This is nice. Fisk: I didn't even know it was here. Vanessa: Yes, it just opened last month. Vanessa: The city's really changing. Fisk: Not fast enough. Vanessa: I don't know. Vanessa: Be a shame to see all the character scrubbed away. Vanessa: You didn't grow up here, did you? Fisk: What gave it away? Fisk: When I was a kid, I used to dream what it would be like to... to live somewhere far away from Hell's Kitchen. Fisk: Somewhere beautiful. Vanessa: What made you stay? Fisk: I didn't. Fisk: When I was 12 years old, my mother, she sent me to stay with relatives. Fisk: Had a farm, middle of nowhere. Fisk: Those were good years. Vanessa: But you came back. Fisk: Yes. Fisk: Time and distance, they afford a certain clarity. Fisk: I realized that this city was a part of me, that it was in my blood. Fisk: And I would do anything to make it a better place... for people like you. Vanessa: To a better place.

Sergei: You answer, he stops hitting you. Sergei: Everyone is happy. Claire: I told you, I don't know who he is. Sergei: Tell me his name. Claire: I don't know. Claire: He never told me. He never told me! Sergei: Mikhail, check the breaker. Sergei: Check the breaker! Sergei: Mikhail? Sergei: Mikhail! Sergei: No, you aren't. Sergei: I'll blow her brains out! Claire: It hurts, doesn't it? Claire: Being in pain, being afraid. Claire: It's okay. Claire: I'm here. Claire: I have you.

Ben Urich: You bid on anything? Karen Page: Yeah. Karen Page: Some, uh... office equipment from a realtor. Karen Page: Nearly as old as I am. Ben Urich: Win? Karen Page: Yeah, 3,500 I don't have. Karen Page: I charged it to the law firm where I work. Karen Page: Probably just got my ass fired. Ben Urich: Beats the alternative. Waitress: More coffee? Karen Page: Uh, can I have a decaf? Waitress: Oh, sure thing. Karen Page: Thanks. Karen Page: How did you know I was gonna be there? Ben Urich: Wasn't looking for you. Karen Page: I thought you weren't interested. Ben Urich: I said you should move on. Ben Urich: Didn't say anything about me. Karen Page: So I was right. Ben Urich: About the office equipment. Ben Urich: Union Allied or whatever it is that they're calling themselves now, they're buying it back. Ben Urich: I mean, you follow that, maybe you find the guy behind the curtain. Ben Urich: You said you read a bunch of my articles. Ben Urich: Remember the one about the, uh... the runoff? Ben Urich: What that company was dumping into the river? Karen Page: Yeah, sure. Ben Urich: Fished the guy that tipped me off out of that same river a month later. Ben Urich: And that fella trying to clean up the Teachers Union? Ben Urich: Moved out of state... after flyers went up saying he was a pedophile. Ben Urich: They underestimated what people in power will do to stay there. Ben Urich: Didn't think you'd make the same mistake after what happened to you. Karen Page: What about the woman? Karen Page: From your first series of articles about the VA? Karen Page: What happened to her? Ben Urich: She met the worst fate. Ben Urich: Married beneath her... to a workaholic who never appreciated her. Karen Page: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to... Ben Urich: We need to be smart. Ben Urich: Smarter than they are. Ben Urich: Don't visit me at the office anymore, and don't tell anyone else about this. Ben Urich: If that doesn't work for you, get up and get the hell out of my life. Karen Page: That works for me. Ben Urich: Good. Ben Urich: First thing, sign the agreement from the Union Allied lawyer. Karen Page: What? No! Karen Page: No, I sign that, I can't ever talk publicly about this. Ben Urich: Yeah... Ben Urich: ...but I'm not signing it.

Vladimir: Sergei. Vladimir: Sergei... Vladimir: Who did this? Sergei: The man in black... Vladimir: All right. Stay there. Vladimr: That was Piotr. Vladimir: Fisk has come out of hiding. Vladimir: We need his help, brother. Anatoly: I will not bow before that man! Vladimir: Then I will go... Vladimir: And bow for both of us. Anatoly: Go. Anatoly: Make the deal.

Vanessa: Are you sure about dessert? Vanessa: They have an incredible Zuppa Inglese. Fisk: Don't children have that at birthday parties? Vanessa: Yes. Vanessa: When I was a kid, I loved it. Vanessa: Probably loved it a bit too much. Fisk: Well, now I have to know what it tastes like. Fisk: You wanna split one? Vanessa: Yes. Fisk: We'll have a Zuppa. Waiter: Yes, sir. Vanessa: Chocolate was always my downfall. Vanessa: Milk chocolate, not the dark stuff they say is better for you. Fisk: I can order something else. Vanessa: No, no, it's good to try new things. Vanessa: Get out of the comfort zone. Fisk: Yes, we get caught up in what we're doing... who we think we are. Vanessa: So... who are you, Wilson? Fisk: Tonight, I'm just a man... enjoying the company of a captivating woman. Wesley: I told you he's indisposed. Wesley: Sir, I need to speak with you. Fisk: What is this? Wesley: We need to go... now.

Guard: He's here! Vladimir: Who do you think? Vladimir: No, I don't know how he found us. Vladimir: Where's my brother? Vladimir: Listen, shut up! Vladimir: Shut up! Vladimir: I don't care what he told you... Vladimir: ...get him on the phone!
Anatoly: I'm sorry. Anatoly: I want to tell you, my brother and I, we gratefully accept... Fisk: Wesley will take care of you. Driver: Put him in a car. Driver: Understood.

Foggy: Promise you won't get mad. Matt: You bought a fax machine? Foggy: From the early '90s. Foggy: Oh, it's not that old... I think. Foggy: Um, but the rest of the stuff's coming tomorrow. Matt: The rest? Foggy: Yeah, like, a printer and conference phones and a copier and... Foggy: Yeah, there was an auction and, you know, we needed stuff, so I, um... charged it to the office. Foggy: But don't freak out, okay? Foggy: I got a thing, some money coming in from... Foggy: You know what? It doesn't matter. Foggy: You mad? Matt: I ever tell you my mom wanted me to be a butcher? Foggy: A butcher?

Claire: This isn't gonna feel great. Matt: Ow. Claire: You got pretty good hands for a blind guy. Matt: Used to patch up my dad. Claire: He ran around in a mask, too? Matt: He was a boxer. Matt: Took a lot of beatings. Claire: Huh. Claire: So you take after him then. Matt: Ow. Claire: Shit. Claire: I'm sorry. Matt: It's okay. Claire: You've had a lot worse. Claire: I mean, I'm sorry for getting you into this. I... Claire: I never thought that I'd be putting anyone else at risk. Matt: It was my choice. Matt: You didn't ask me to pull you from that dumpster. Claire: No, you did it because you're a good person. Claire: And you almost got killed... because of me. Claire: Tell me it was worth it. Claire: Tell me that you've got a plan... an end game. Matt: Claire... Claire: Anything? Matt: I'm just trying to make my city a better place, that's all. Claire: Ow. I think maybe it's a little more complicated than that now. Claire: Nothing's changing out there. Claire: No matter what I do, I'm just... I'm making things worse. Matt: Tell that to the boy you saved from the Russians. Matt: Or all the other people you've helped. Claire: And what about the people I've gotten hurt? What do I... Claire: What do I tell them? Matt: Feel my heart. Matt: Come on, feel it. Claire: What is it telling you? Matt: That you're scared. Claire: Because I am. Claire: More than I've ever been in my life. Claire: And I am not alone. Claire: But you can do something about it... for all of us, Mike. Matt: Matthew. Matt: My name is Matthew.

Vanessa: Will I see you again? Vanessa: I don't usually date customers. Fisk: You came out with me tonight. Fisk: And here we are, so... Fisk: I can... return the painting, and then I'd no longer be a... Vanessa: I'm not interested in gestures, Wilson, or your money, or... whatever that was all about at the restaurant. Vanessa: I went out with you because... there's something different about you. Vanessa: Not so sure it's a good thing now. Fisk: Like you said... I don't do this much. Fisk: And I'm sorry that our night, it went sideways. Fisk: But... I enjoyed our time together very much, Vanessa. Fisk: If you don't feel the same... even a little bit... just tell me, and I promise you won't see me again. Vanessa: I... don't know how I feel.

Fisk: And even after all that, you didn't even get a name out of the girl? Wesley: No. Wesley: The man in black came before our men had finished. Anatoly: You were right to reach out to us, although... a call would have been more appropriate. Fisk: They say the past is etched in stone, but it isn't. Fisk: It's... smoke trapped in a closed room, swirling... changing. Fisk: Buffeted by the passing of years and wishful thinking. Fisk: But even though our perception of it changes, one thing remains constant. Fisk: The past can... never be completely erased. Fisk: It lingers. Fisk: Like the scent of burning wood. Driver: Sir? Fisk: Yes, passenger side. Wesley: Was that him? Fisk: Mmm. Fisk: He'd like to have a word with you. Fisk: You embarrassed me. Fisk: You embarrassed me in front of her. Fisk: Tell Mr. Potter I'll need a new suit. Fisk: Hmm. Fisk: What about this? Fisk: Take what's left of him and send it to his brother. Wesley: It'll start a war. Fisk: I'm counting on it.

Claire: You've been busy. Matt: Yeah. Ow. Claire: Sorry. Claire: So, how's that working out for you? Matt: You should see the other guys. Claire: I have. Claire: The one you threw off the roof, at my place? Claire: He's in a coma. Do you know that? Matt: Yeah, I heard. Claire: How do you feel about that? Matt: I'll live. Claire: Hey! Claire: Get off the counter! Matt: Wow, you don't like cats. Claire: I'm allergic. Claire: I was supposed to be coming in, feeding this guy twice a day while my friend was out of town, not hiding out here using up all my sick days. Matt: Just a while longer. Matt: Just till I know the Russians aren't looking for you. Claire: I'm not the one that looks like they've been through the grinder. Claire: You really need to get some kind of body armor or something. Matt: It would slow me down too much. Claire: So will a bullet. Claire: You worried about me? Matt: What if I were? Claire: I would tell you I'm a big boy, and not to be. Matt: Right. Matt: That's why you keep ending up here. Claire: Well, maybe I just like the sound of your voice. Claire: Hmm. Claire: So what happens the night you come by... I'm already talking to someone else? Matt: Yeah, it crossed my mind. Claire: Yeah? Matt: Here. Claire: Um, you shouldn't have. Matt: I didn't. The burner's for me. Matt: Memorize the number, put yours in. Matt: Next time I need to come by, I'll call. Claire: By "come by," do you mean stumble in, bleeding half to death? Matt: Yeah, something like that. Claire: You're gonna get yourself killed. Claire: You really gotta ease up. Matt: No, I can't. Not yet. Matt: I can take care of myself, Mike. Claire: You know... Matt: It's not just about you. Matt: It's a little more complicated than that. Matt: You ever heard the name Wilson Fisk? Claire: No... who's that? Matt: Just a name somebody gave me. Matt: But there's no public record. Matt: Nothing on the Internet. Matt: Not one mention of Fisk. Claire: Maybe whoever gave you his name was lying. Matt: I would have known if he was. Claire: How? Matt: Heartbeat. Claire: Right, of course, heartbeat. Claire: So, what, you're just gonna go out there punching whoever you can, hoping to find somebody who knows this Fisk guy? Matt: Well, apply enough pressure, someone will break. Matt: Sooner or later.

Wesley: Oof. Those look like they hurt. Vladimir: I've had worse. Wesley: I know how much your people delight in extolling the amount of pain they can endure, but maybe next time you could try ducking? Wesley: Leland's finalized the paperwork. Wesley: Prohaszka's holdings in Kitchen Cab have been acquired and transferred via third party to Veles Taxi. Wesley: Your distribution infrastructure just doubled. Anatoly: Tell your employer we are grateful. Wesley: Don't think he really cares at the moment. Wesley: You were light again this week. Vladimir: There was a complication. Wesley: One you assured us you were addressing. Anatoly: Do you know what he was asking? Anatoly: This fool who laid hands on my brother? Wesley: Not my concern. Anatoly: It should be. Anatoly: He was asking about your employer, by name. Wesley: All the more reason to settle this. Wesley: You sneeze, we all catch a cold. Wesley: Madame Gao and Mr. Nobu have expressed their disappointment. Vladimir: We have not heard of this. Wesley: Hmm, that's because we've been talking behind your back, about how the Russians can't seem to handle one man running around in a mask. Wesley: I mean, if he had an iron suit or a magic hammer, maybe that would explain why you keep getting your asses handed to you... Vladimir: We're done here. Wesley: He's weakened your operation. Vladimir: You think us weak? Wesley: This isn't personal, Vladimir. Wesley: It's business. Wesley: Distribution of Madame Gao's product has been affected, which in turn is causing delays in other ventures. Wesley: This is not acceptable. Wesley: Fortunately for all parties, my employer has agreed to help return you to solid footing. Vladimir: How? Wesley: By aiding you in certain duties deemed vital to the continuation of service... Anatoly: He wants to take over. Wesley: We value the services you provide, but clearly you need help providing them. Wesley: We'll all profit nicely under the new structure. Vladimir: How nicely? Vladimir: Tell Mr. Fisk... Wesley: We don't say his name. Vladimir: Tell... Mr. Fisk... Vladimir: ...that if he wants a pound of flesh... Vladimir: ...he can come here and carve it himself. Wesley: This is an offer, not an order. Wesley: The choice of how we proceed is yours. Wesley: Talk it over with your brother. Wesley: We'll be in touch.

Ben Urich: Did you look at it? Karen Page: Yeah, I looked at it. Ben Urich: And? Karen Page: And... it's a story I've heard before. Karen Page: Company gets caught up in a scandal, files for bankruptcy, then quietly restructures under a new name. Karen Page: They killed Daniel Fisher. Karen Page: They tried to kill me. Ben Urich: I'm still a little unclear on that point. Ben Urich: You say here Rance assaulted you in your apartment. Ben Urich: And a man in a black mask saved your life? Karen Page: Yes, but he just... Karen Page: He came out of nowhere. Ben Urich: And you'd never seen him before? Karen Page: No. Ben Urich: Stranger things, right? Ben Urich: Well, what about Rance? Ben Urich: Do you really believe that he just up and hung himself in jail? Karen Page: That guard tried to do the same thing to me. Karen Page: Why don't you ask him? Ben Urich: Farnum? Ben Urich: He's dead. Ben Urich: Ate the barrel of his gun in his basement. Ben Urich: And your old boss, McClintock? Ben Urich: Overdosed on pills or some such. Ben Urich: You seeing a pattern here, Miss Page? Karen Page: Then why isn't anyone looking into this? Ben Urich: You don't understand how lucky you are. Ben Urich: Count the angels on the head of a pin, and move on. Karen Page: So they just shuffle some papers and all this disappears? Ben Urich: Wouldn't be the first time. Karen Page: Oh, don't bullshit me. Karen Page: A construction company is brick and mortar, literally. Karen Page: All right, you cannot just shift cranes and trailers and office equipment like you can numbers on a page. Karen Page: There has to be a trail if everything is being liquidated. Ben Urich: Thanks for the coffee. Karen Page: What? Karen Page: So that's it?

Anatoly: Stories like this are built on sources, Miss Page. Ben Urich: Stories like this are built on sources, Miss Page. Ben Urich: Credible sources. Ben Urich: I did some digging into your, uh... past activities. Karen Page: Well, I did some digging, too. Karen Page: I read every big story with your byline. Karen Page: The VA kickbacks, toxic runoff, the Teachers Union scandal. Karen Page: Hell, you pretty much brought down the Italian mob back when I was in diapers. Karen Page: What ever happened to that reporter, Mr. Urich? Ben Urich: He got old. Ben Urich: And a hell of a lot less stupid.

Anatoly: My God. Anatoly: Give me the kit. Vladimir: This could kill him. Anatoly: Semyon's usually the one we send for this sort of work. Anatoly: He'd understand. Vladimir: You hear back from Piotr? Anatoly: Said he'd call when he had something on Fisk's movements. Vladimir: Fisk is cautious. Vladimir: If he suspects... Anatoly: Then what? Anatoly: What are you so afraid of? Anatoly: We were in that hellhole for three years. Anatoly: From princes of Moscow... to shitting in a bucket. Anatoly: I promised myself if we ever got free... we'd never lose what we had again. Anatoly: Especially not to pride. Vladimir: Back when we had nothing, we agreed on everything. Vladimir: We've lost our way... in this land of riches. Anatoly: Then let's find it again... together. Anatoly: You sure... this was epinephrine? Anatoly: Get his tube out. Anatoly: Semyon... Anatoly: It's us... Anatoly: Anatoly and Vladimir. Anatoly: That's it... Anatoly: Breathe... Anatoly: Breathe... Anatoly: And tell us about the man who did this to you. Semyon: The devil. Semyon: The devil. Anatoly: Did you see anything? Anatoly: Semyon? Anatoly: Anything that could help us find him? Semyon: There was a woman... Vladimir: Get Sergei on the phone.

Wesley: Hola. Fisk: Hola. Wesley: Anatoly may be the way in. Wesley: He seems more amenable to the proposition, or at least not quite as... vitriolic as his brother. Fisk: Well, confrontations can be expensive. Fisk: I'd prefer to handle this quietly. Fisk: How are we on the timeline? Wesley: Within a reasonable margin. Wesley: Assuming we can settle with the Russians quickly. Fisk: We will. One way or another. Fisk: What about the masked idiot? Wesley: If the brothers can't handle him, I'll find another solution.
Fisk: No. Fisk: You stay with the car. Wesley: Sir... Fisk: I need to attend to this alone. Fisk: Thank you, Wesley.

Claire: You cook for every girl you bring home? Matt: Nah, just the ones that keep me alive. Claire: You have a job or something to get to? Or are you one of those billionaire playboys I'm always hearing about? Matt: No, I have a job. Claire: Damn, thought I'd lucked out. What do you do? Matt: Lawyer. I have a practice, so my own boss. Claire: Lawyer by day, vigilante by night. The hell does that work? Matt: Yeah, I'll let you know when I figure it out. Claire: Oh, shit. Matt: You just opened one of the cuts on your back. Claire: How do you know that? Matt: I can taste copper in the air. Claire: "Copper in the air." Matt: May I? Claire: Knock yourself out, Houdini. Matt: The swelling's down. Rib fracture's only a hairline. I couldn't tell before. Claire: You have X-ray fingers now? Matt: I can hear your bones shift when you breathe. No grinding means nothing's broken. Claire: What does a hairline fracture sound like? Matt: An old ship. Claire: How do you— I mean, I know that you're blind, but you see so much. How? Matt: I guess you have to think of it as more than just five senses. I can't see, not like everyone else, but I can feel. Things like balance and direction. Micro-changes in air density, vibrations, blankets of temperature variations. Mix all that with what I hear, subtle smells. All of the fragments form a sort of impressionistic painting. Claire: Okay, but what does that look like? Like, what do you actually see? Matt: A world on fire. Claire: If all I saw was fire, I'd probably want to hit people, too. I just wish I knew I was hitting the right ones. Matt: Claire, they know who you are now. And they're not going to stop. I'd like you to stay here, with me— just till I figure something out. Claire: That's a hell of a way to get a girl to move in. Matt: It worked, didn't it? Claire: Hmm. Claire: I was wondering if you were ever gonna do that. Matt: Well, I've been a little busy. I'll get you some clothes while I'm out. Claire: Mmm. Why don't you go to the police? With all that you have on the Russians? Matt: I wear a mask and beat on people. Doesn't exactly mesh with police policy. Claire: You're going to end up in another dumpster, you try to take down the entire Russian mob yourself. Matt: Maybe I only need to take down one man. Claire: Fisk? Matt: Cut off the head of the snake, the body dies. Claire: How do you know he's the head of the snake if you can't find anything on him? Matt: There was a murder in a bowling alley. A man named Prohaszka. Owned a majority in Kitchen Cabs. They were turning those over in the garage they took me to. Right, I think Fisk hired the man that killed Prohaszka. Everything leads back to him but no one will talk. Claire: Maybe you are beating on the wrong people. I heard a name, when they were... The prick with the baseball bat reacted when he heard it. Like a dog when you yank his leash. Matt: What was the name? Claire: Vladimir. Vladimir: It's me again. Call me back. Shithead. Wesley: My employer sends his regards. And his gratitude that his offer was accepted. There are still a few small details we'd like to iron out before— Uh, where's your brother? Vladimir: This is a thing I was going to ask you. Last time I saw him, he was heading to see Mr.— Wesley: Your employer. Vladimir: He practically kissed me when we agreed to terms. He have a girl or a boy he might be celebrating with? Wesley: You try his cell? Vladimir: He does not answer. Wesley: Try again. We need to lock this down and get distribution back to acceptable levels. Goon: We found him. Vladimir: Where? Goon: He was dumped in the lot around the corner. Vladimir: My brother. My brother. We should have returned to Moscow. Like you wanted. Vladimir: The man in the mask. He sends us a message. Put every man we have on the street. Find him. And bring me his head. Leland: Anyone else wondering about this? Nobu: Why aren't we meeting in the usual place? And what's all this? Fisk: An opportunity for those willing to seize it. Wesley: She's happy to see you. Fisk: My apologies for my absence of late. And for calling you here on little notice. Leland: Where are the Smiley Twins? Sleeping off another kidnapping? Fisk: The Ranskahovs are no longer a part of this organization. Leland: Since when? Fisk: Since I removed Anatoly's head with my car door. Wesley: She's upset they weren't consulted. Wesley: He isn't happy either. Leland: Deal me in on that. What the hell happened? Fisk: It was a personal matter. Leland: What? That's— Vladimir isn't exactly a hug-it-out kind of guy. Fisk: The masked vigilante killed his brother. At least that's what Vladimir believes. Leland: And? Fisk: It will distract him until preparations can be made. We all knew that we would need to eliminate the Russians one day. Leland: Why? Fisk: They were too unpredictable. Leland: This from a guy taking heads off with a car door. Wesley: She wants to know how her product is going to be moved now. Fisk: For the moment, you would keep sending your deliveries to the Russians, as though nothing has changed. And when this is all over, I'll assume their responsibility. Leland: And move their share to your column in the ledger? Fisk: A rising tide raises all boats, Leland. Profits will be divided up equally among us. Four shares, instead of five. Fisk: Leland? Leland: What, I'm going against the three of you? I like my head where it's at. Fisk: Then we're in agreement. Nothing changes until I'm ready to move on Vladimir. Nobu: And what if he finds out the truth before that happens? Fisk: That would be unfortunate for all of us. Leland: Masked vigilantes, crazy Russians— I'm getting my stun gun out of storage. Nobu: Remember your promise to me and those I speak for. Fisk: Madame Gao, may I walk you to your car? Wesley: She thinks you want something. Fisk: I want to put this behind us as quickly as possible. Russian Goon: Shut up. Ask him about the man in the mask. Piotr: Let's go. Piotr: Wait. Goon: Huh? Matt: Where's Vladimir? Piotr: No, please! Matt: Vladimir! Where is he? Piotr: Please, I'll tell you what you want! Just don't cut my head off! Matt: What are you talking about? Piotr: Vladimir's brother. Everyone knows you took his head. Cop: On the ground! On the ground! Cop: Be advised two on foot. One en route to the 15th. Karen: No! Oh, my God. You don't make any sense! Foggy: Whoa, be nice to it. You know, for when the machines take over. Karen: I can't get any of this crap I bought to work. Foggy: Bad time to mention the phones? All I hear when I try to dial is a bunch of clicks. Could be the machines plotting, but I don't speak computer overlord. Karen: No, it's the rats. Foggy: The who what now? Karen: They chewed through the main line. Phone guy's working on it now. Exterminator's Monday. Foggy: We have rats now. I'm never sleeping here again. Matt: Then there's an upside. Hey, you guys hear anything on the news about a Russian getting his head cut off? In Hell's Kitchen? Foggy: This city. Bad enough you get mugged, now they chop your melon off. What's next, groping corpses? Mrs. Cardenas: Excuse. Is this, um— Señor Foggy law? Foggy: Bess Mahoney. Brett's mom? Mrs. Cardenas: Sí, she refer me. Karen: Something about cigars? Foggy: You know Spanish? Karen: Oh, just what I remember from high school. Mrs. Cardenas, tell us what happened. Mrs. Cardenas: Mi casa es rent-control. But the landlord, Señor Tully... Foggy: Armand Tully? Sleaze bag owns buildings all over town. Mrs. Cardenas: Sí, y señor Tully— Karen: He wants to convert the apartments to condominiums. And he wants them out. Karen: Men came weeks ago. They said that they were workers. Karen: And they destroyed the apartments with a... I don't know that last word. Matt: Sledgehammers. Foggy: College. You ever have a client that wants to chat in Punjabi, I'm your man. Karen: Um— Do you want to do this? Foggy: No, no. I like listening to your voice. Karen: Go on, Mrs. Cardenas. Mrs. Cardenas: There is damage, en todas partes. Karen: Everywhere. Karen: They have no working sinks or pipes. They don't have water or electricity for days. Mrs. Cardenas: We call policía. We speak to the officer. Karen: The police couldn't help. Mrs. Cardenas: Policía say, "It is a city issue." Karen: They don't know what to do. Foggy: This says Tully offered them 10,000 to give up their rent control and vacate the premises. Maybe we can pressure him into giving a better payout. Mrs. Cardenas: No, Señor Foggy. We do no want money. We want to stay in our homes. Karen: This way, Mrs. Cardenas. Foggy: I heard you say my name. Why'd you say my name? Matt: I told her you're going to talk to Tully's lawyer. Foggy: Tully's lawyer? Do you know who reps him? Matt: Yeah, I know. Foggy: Landman and Zack! Landman and mother-freakin' Zack, man! Karen: Ooh, sounds impressive. Are they looking to hire? Matt: Oh, you wouldn't be happy. We used to intern there. Karen: Oh, right. Foggy: And they offered us a job, a great job. Which we turned down to go off and save the world. Now they hate us. Matt: We'll need to load for bear if we're gonna take them on. I'll hit the precinct to check for complaints against Tully. Foggy: I can't go to L and Z alone. They're gonna shark attack me, Matt. location: NEW YORK CITY - HEAT WAVE - OPENING MONTAGE
scene_text: Reporter: Record temperatures in the New York area as 100-degree weather hits its fifth consecutive day with no end in sight. Man 1: I'll tell you who I want! Man 2: I told you I'll call you later. Man 3: Yeah, you'll get what you want. Man 4: ...lowlife pulls a piece on me. It never worked! Woman: What's wrong with you? I tell you not to touch... Driver: You want to move your car? Huh? Get out of the way! Person: Oh, my God! Move, move! Person 2: They opened fire. Person 3: Move the hell out of the way! Officer: Drop the gun! Drop the gun and get on the ground... Person 4: Out of my way! Move! Move, move, move! Officer 2: You get out of the car! Officer 3: Get out of the way, now! Get out of the car, now! Person 5: Call 911. Man 5: And then he went to... Man 6: You! You! Stay calm! Call the cops. Woman 2: Let me go! Please put me down. Help! Anybody, please help! Man 7: Shut up! Shut up! Officer 4: Stand back, everybody. Woman 3: Okay, please, please.

Brett: Sergeant Mahoney. What do we got? Officer: Looks like the whole Irish mob, Sarge. At least the ones operating in Hell's Kitchen. Brett: How many? Officer: Fifteen, maybe twenty dead. Hard to tell with all the... pieces. Brett: Jesus. Any witnesses? Officer: None that are talking. Brett: Cameras? Officer: Disabled. Whoever did this knew what they were doing. Brett: Get CSU down here. And lock this place down tight.

Karen: Matt! How is he? Matt: Not good. He's lost a lot of blood. Foggy: What happened? Matt: Someone massacred the Irish. Grotto was there. Karen: Massacred? Matt: That's what he said. Doctor: Are you here for Mr. Casagrande? Matt: Yes. How is he? Doctor: Critical but stable. The bullet went clean through. No major organ damage, but he's lost a significant amount of blood. Matt: Can we see him? Doctor: He's being moved to a room. Give us a few minutes.

Brett: Mr. Murdock. Miss Page. Mr. Nelson. Matt: Sergeant Mahoney. Brett: I need to talk to your client. Matt: He's in no condition to answer questions. Brett: Fifteen people are dead. If he knows something... Foggy: Then he can tell you when he's recovered. Brett: This is a crime scene investigation. I don't need permission from his lawyers. Matt: Actually, you do. Unless you're arresting him for something. Brett: Not yet. Karen: Then we're done here. Brett: Look, I'm trying to help. Whatever happened tonight, it's connected to what went down with the Dogs of Hell last week. We're talking about a crew with the training, knowledge and hardware to take out half the city. Matt: What do they want? Brett: That's what's driving the DA nuts. We don't know who they are. We just know who they're not. Foggy: I'd say they're definitely not fond of the Irish. Brett: You think? Officer 2: Where exactly am I gonna put this asshole? The morgue's completely full. Brett: This is worse than what happened to the Dogs of Hell. Now, we got history, so I'll tell you as a friend, you stay out of this shit. If you got a witness, the smart move is to turn him over and walk away. Hell's Kitchen is about to explode. Foggy: You hear that? He called me friend. Matt: What'd you pick up? Foggy: Your hearing's better than mine. Matt: Whatever happened here happened to the Dogs of Hell last week. Foggy: The biker gang? Matt: Yeah. Foggy: What are we stepping into? Matt: I don't know. I think I can rattle some cages, see who talks but, uh... Foggy: Did you even listen to Brett? We're talking about a squad of trained killers loose on the streets. Not the kind of guys you challenge to a fist fight in your underwear. Matt: Hey! It's not underwear, Foggy. Underwear is comfortable. Foggy: You're a lot of things. Bulletproof is not one of them. Matt: I'll see you in the morning. Foggy: You're an asshole. But if I can't stop you, least I can do is help. I have a guy I can talk to. Maybe come back with a few puzzle pieces. Matt: Cool. Just be careful. Foggy: You don't get to say that!

Karen: Okay, okay, okay. You've got multiple lacerations, Steve. All right? The doctor said... Grotto: No! No doctor. Karen: The cut is deep, all right? Into the muscle, but there's no vessel damage. Nothing that a few weeks of physical therapy can't cure. You need to stay here. Grotto: That ain't happening. Karen: No, I'm here to help you. Grotto: By hog-tying me to a hospital with a target on my ass? You wanna wait for a bullet through the window or pull the trigger myself? Karen: You need to listen to me, Steve. Grotto: No, you listen to me, you daft woman! Karen: You can trust me! Grotto: Who, in Christ's name, is Steve? Karen: You are. Your name is Steve Schaffer, and I am your wife, Isabelle. You got into a bar fight defending my honor. And other than the beer that was wasted when that bottle sliced through your flesh, I have got no regrets, because I have loved you since I was 16, hot Irish temper and all. Grotto: It's a nice story, doll. You gotta run home now. You ain't got the balls for what's coming. Karen: Slide into bed, sweetheart, and settle in. Because I am the best chance you've got in the world right now.

Turk: You got your break-action singles, your side-by-side, your over-unders, and the classic pump-action. All guaranteed to supersede every other on the market. Buyer: None of these is semis. Turk: Aw, what do you need semis for, couple bad-asses like you? Whatever this army is, they're planting men by the dozen, Turk. Buyer: No semis, no deal. Turk: Man, I seen you shoot. No semi's gonna magically make you have good aim. Saw these off, spread your blast, and thank me later, 'cause you ain't no deadeye. Buyer: What'd you just say? Turk: Oh, shit. Daredevil: Nice duds. Turk: The Irish had a whole squad massacred tonight. Daredevil: That's a damn shame, 'cause I'm fresh out of sympathy cards. There's talk about an army in town. Military grade firepower, high volume. Turk: Who's the supplier, Turk? Daredevil: You think I know? Shit like that's so high above my pay grade... Turk: I'm telling you the truth, man. That tin in my trunk couldn't kill a rabbit. Daredevil: Okay, okay! Okay, listen. I did hear somethin' from a guy in Rikers. It's got to do with Fisk. Turk: Fisk is gone. Daredevil: Yeah, but once you took care of him, what'd you think was gonna happen? Every gang worth shit's trying to grab up everything fat boy left behind. I even heard the cartel's getting into it. They're bringing up some heavy munitions from Juárez. Military grade. Turk: Where? Daredevil: Warehouse. Meatpacking District, 13th Street and something, I swear I'm telling you all I know. Listen, man. I gave you what you wanted. My hand's busted, I got all this glass I gotta replace now. Maybe, just let a brother go, huh? Come on, D. I'm out on parole, man. I can't go back to jail. Please. Daredevil: I missed Hell's Kitchen. Turk: Yeah. It didn't miss you. Daredevil: Fine. Know what? Be like that. 'Cause we both know I'll be back out by the end of the month... I'll see you then.

Bouncer: Members only, pork chop. Foggy: It's okay, I'm meeting a friend. Bouncer: Get lost or get hurt. Foggy: He's a full-patch member of the Dogs of Hell. I swear, I just need to talk to him. Bouncer: What's this big shot's name? Foggy: Smitty. Bouncer: Don't move. Foggy: Does it look like I'm packing? Bouncer: Gonna wish you were. Come with me. Biker 1: Look at this asshole. Says he's here to see Smitty. Biker 2: Old friend. Foggy: Old friend? Biker 2: Yeah. Third grade. Sister Haney's class? She really had it in for us. Is he around or should I just... Foggy: Ow! No, no, no, no! Holy shit! Biker 2: What's your name? Foggy: Foggy! Franklin Nelson! Biker 2: Never heard of you. Foggy: I've known Smitty for a long time. Biker 2: Oh, yeah? Me, too. Obviously, we went on different career paths along the way... Foggy: Is this funny to you? Biker 2: No. No, sir. Biker 3: 'Cause I'm two seconds away from slitting your throat. Foggy: I'm not a cop, okay? Biker 3: You a fed? Foggy: I'm a lawyer. Look, I just... I just need five minutes with Smitty and then I swear, I'm gone. Biker 3: Yeah, you're gone now. Ever walk back in here again, and you'll leave in pieces. Nod if you understand me. Take him out back, show him how we feel about lawyers. Foggy: No, please, no, no, no, no, no. Foggy: It's okay. I'm gonna get you down. I'm gonna get you down. I'm gonna get you down. It was a mistake coming here, I realize that. Biker: Shut up! Foggy: I just wanted to help people, I swear. Biker: Smitty would understand! Foggy: Smitty's dead, asshole. Foggy: What? Biker: You have to believe me, I... I didn't know that. Foggy: Oh, I believe there's a lot you don't know. Biker: Whoa, okay, look. Smitty was a long time ago. Couple years ago, I helped a guy named Foster. Foggy: He was a biker! Biker: Not one of ours. Foggy: Ricky Wex? Biker: Shut up! Foggy: I helped a guy named Pope! Yeah, the VA said that his injuries weren't sustained during battle, but they were! They just didn't manifest themselves for 20 years. Uh, we got his operation sorted and then, a couple of months later, he was back on his Harley, doing whatever it is you guys do. Which is none of my business! Biker: You helped Pope? Foggy: Get the hell out of here. Biker: Really? Foggy: Now! Biker: What happened to Smitty? Foggy: You serious? Biker: I came here for a reason. I just need answers! Look, if I don't get answers, a lot of innocent blood could be shed. People who both you and I care about are gonna get hurt. And you don't seem like the most sentimental guy, but you're still listening. And that knife isn't in my neck, so I have to believe that right now... maybe you and I are on the same side. Biker: You got guts, Harvard. I'll give you that. Foggy: Columbia, actually, but it's not courage. It's more like sheer adrenaline. Hey, look, I wouldn't be asking, I wouldn't be here doing this if it wasn't important. Biker: Smitty was on a run, I-90 with four brothers, transporting a big score. They were hit by a goddamn army. Their whole crew was cut to pieces. Left there like roadkill. Foggy: Any idea who did it? Biker: Nah. New crew, doesn't matter. Whoever they are, we're gonna find 'em. And when we do, you wanna be very far away from the action. You didn't hear none of this from me. Now go. And don't come back.

Irish Survivor: I always knew the devil would come for me. But I thought I would be dead first. Daredevil: I'm gonna get some help. Irish Survivor: No! No... no... Daredevil: Who did this? Irish Survivor: No one escapes this. No one can get away. Daredevil: Tell me. Tell me who they are. Irish Survivor: No "they." Him. It's one man.

Karen: Hold it right there. Grotto: Oh, my God! Oh, God. Karen: What was that? Grotto: No, no, no, no, no, no, no. Shit. Someone's come to finish the job. Karen: Shh! Don't move. Grotto: No, to hell with that. He's got a gun! Karen: Shit. Come on, come on, come on! Come on! Grotto: Dear God. Shit. Karen: What? You... You don't have the right keys? Grotto: Shut up! Shut up! Karen: Is this even your car? Grotto: Belonged to a friend. Karen: Where's he? Grotto: He's dead. Get in! Karen/Grotto: Bang.

Foggy: You ever wake up in the morning... from the second you get out of bed, it's like... every molecule in your body hurts? Matt: No, never. Foggy: I'm in agony, dude. Matt: What, did you go back to the gym? Foggy: Hell, no. Do I look capable of making healthy life choices? I went out, Matthew. Went out dancing. Matt: I'm choosing not to believe that. Foggy: And yet, it's true. Matt: Mind if I ask you a personal question? Foggy: Go ahead. Matt: Are you insane? Foggy: Yes. Matt: Tell me it was the barista. Barista: Hey, Foggy. Looking good! Foggy: Her name is Bethany and she is very limber. Matt: Oh! You're my hero. Man: Watch it, asshole. Matt: So, uh, when's the next date? Foggy: Well, therein lies the true pain. Matt: No! Foggy: Yes. One and done. End of the night, she hugged me like a cousin and said, "I'll call you." Matt: Oh, that's brutal. Foggy: You know what my problem is? Matt: Well, it ain't the moves. You know I got the moves. Foggy: That's the tragedy of you being blind, you've never seen me dance. Matt: Yeah, but I can cite the legends I heard in law school. Foggy: So come on, what is it? What's the problem? Matt: No wingman. You never come out with me anymore. Foggy: Could you imagine Nelson and Murdock on the dance floor? Matt: I can't deny that does sound epic. Foggy: Then come out with me, Matt. All right. Come on, just one time, me and you. Matt: What is it? Foggy: You're bleeding. Matt: Huh. Where? Foggy: Base of the skull. Matt: Did you get it? Foggy: No one's gonna notice, if that's what you mean. Matt: Thank you. Foggy: I hate this. Matt: We don't need to talk about it. Foggy: Good thinking. Matt: You know, Karen's been asking questions. The cuts, the scrapes, the bruises. Foggy: What do you tell her? Matt: You have a drinking problem. Foggy: That's horrible. Matt: Well, it's more plausible than you put on a devil suit and beat the shit out of strangers. Foggy: You know, this whole thing isn't just your problem anymore. And I'm past worrying about the broken bones, and finding you beaten into a coma. Matt: What about us? Foggy: Nelson and Murdock? You ever stop to think what happens if you get caught? At best, you'll be disbarred. Matt: Then you'll continue to do the good work we started together. Foggy: Do you even hear yourself? You're my partner. I don't wanna continue alone. Matt: Foggy... last week, a client came to our office, Zuly Almeida. Claimed her life was in danger. We had no legal recourse to offer. Foggy: I remember. You recommended an excellent shelter for battered women. Matt: And she went. Foggy: Yeah, she tried. Matt: That night, her husband found out she wanted to leave him, and he followed her to the bus stop with a gut full of beer and a butcher knife in his hand. Foggy: You never told me that. Matt: Well, I'm telling you now. Mr. Almeida walked out of his apartment with the intention to hack Mrs. Almeida into many bloody pieces... starting by taking off her head. Guess what? Never happened. Instead, he woke up in a hospital with two broken arms and a restraining order safety-pinned to his chest. Foggy: Jesus, Matt. Matt: If I take a night off, people get hurt. Foggy: I don't wanna lose you. Matt: You won't. Foggy: Promise me. Matt: You want me to cross my heart? Foggy: Do not make fun of me. Matt: I swear. Come on. Let's get to work. Foggy: Yeah, I gotta get out of this heat.
Irish Thug: Idiots.

Karen: Good morning, guys. You take the scenic route this morning? Matt: Morning to you, too. Foggy: Morning, Karen. Karen: What have we got? Foggy: All right. Well, uh, Mr. Marino's dog was viciously beaten by his neighbor after the dog, um... defiled the neighbor's statue of Saint Francis. Karen: "Defiled"? Foggy: Um... humped repeatedly until completion. Matt: That's a dog I want to defend. Foggy: Oh, he's... he's all yours, cowboy. And, uh, Mr. Maxwell here was attacked in a bar fight last night. Maxwell: He started it. Karen: Oh, I... I called Metro-General and the other guy will recover, but if you are looking at trial, you probably wanna wait until his jaw is unwired. Maxwell: Your girl's a badass. Matt: You've no idea. Karen: Um, and, uh, Miss Jacinto's working papers have been denied for the third time. Her father's gone and she says that factory work is the only way she can support her family. Matt: Well, tell her not to worry. Foggy: Yeah. Karen: I've already pulled her applications from the DOE. Matt: Good, because we're gonna find her something better. Karen: And that's just the appointments for the first hour. You wanna talk about our 10:00 a.m.'s? Foggy: Uh, what's that? Karen: Oh, uh, the bananas are from Mr. Tate. Payment for that fender bender thing. And for you... Strawberry rhubarb. Matt: You will be mine. Karen: Uh, so, um... I installed this free trial of accounting software on my computer. And the good news is that I can re-up it every 30 days with a fake email address. But, um... the bad news is that... we're broke. As in, literally no money. And our income can't cover our bills. Matt: We'll manage. I don't know how, but I know we will. Foggy: All right. Well, in the meantime, I guess we have, um... lots of pastries and... and fruit. Karen: Yeah, and fans. Foggy: Portable, electric fans. Karen: Yes. And, uh... and each other. Matt: Miss Jacinto, will you come in, please? Let's see if we can find you a better way to live in Hell's Kitchen. Karen: Please, sit down.

Nesbitt: Apologies, Mr. Nesbitt. Voice: Blood's still up. Nesbitt: Best you mind him, Thomas. Thomas: You miserable mutt! Where was all that fight 10 minutes ago? Place smells like dog shit! Voice 2: There's a pot calling the kettle. Voice 3: Someone get this poor man a drink. Nesbitt: Grotto, you mangy shite. How's the view up Nesbitt's ass? Nesbitt: Gentlemen, if you'll permit me... a word before we begin. This is a night for celebration. A night to discuss the future of our family... the gratitude we feel for the support of his father. But perhaps as important... it is also... a moment for sober reflection. Irish Man 1: Sober, my ass. Nesbitt: Two hundred years ago, our people were little more than dirt farmers, struggling just to survive. They had nothing but their hopes and their fists, and they brought both of them along when they came to America, many to this very city. Irish Man 2: Think you've had enough, George. Nesbitt: Now some of you are young... so there's no reason you'd remember, but there was a time when the Irish owned Hell's Kitchen. Wasn't a mother's son could make a move without giving us our due, and any sorry shite dull enough to cross us paid a heavy price. We had the cops, judges, councilmen. We had the whole bloody city at our beck and call. But we got complacent. Lost our edge. Just enough for a piece of garbage like Wilson Fisk to steal what was rightfully ours. Irish Man 3: That's right. Nesbitt: Some of us feared Fisk. Some, in fact, ran. A few... maybe even deigned to work for him. Siding against their own kind. But now the Devil's taken him down, and that, gentlemen, has provided us with a singular opportunity. The Russians are dead. The Chinese, they turned tail and ran, leaving the drug trade ripe for the taking. The yakuza have gone silent. Irish Man 4: Piss on 'em! Irish Man 5: Piss on 'em all! Irish Man 6: Piss on 'em all. Nesbitt: 'Cause this is our time! Anyone crosses us, we'll paint the streets red with their blood. And when they're gone, we'll make your father proud, and purge ourselves of the filthy traitors who betrayed their own kind and make Hell's Kitchen ours again!

Karen: See, I don't know, that definitely sounded like cheating to me, Miss Page. Foggy, you sure we're not being hustled here? Foggy: As sure as Josie's AC is busted. Matt: What AC? Karen: At least she brought water. Matt: Oh! Foggy: No, you don't wanna do that. Karen: You can't drink the water here. Matt: Josie's pipes have issues. Rust, mold. Karen: I think I can actually see the bacteria floating in there. Foggy: Oh, ew, ew. Matt: See, that... that's why we, uh, keep our cock neat. Foggy: Pretend you're abroad, on vacation someplace exotic, but no mojitos. Karen: Josie just throws mint in the beer. Matt: Right. Matt: Excuse me. Foggy: You trying to scare me? That's cheating. Karen: How is that cheating? Foggy: You got fangs in your mouth. Karen: You wanna see fangs? Foggy: Yes, I do. Matt: Hello? Grotto: It's me. Grotto. I need help, man. Matt: Slow down. What happened? Grotto: I can't go to the cops. They're gonna k*ll me. Matt: Who's gonna k*ll you, Grotto? Grotto: I need a safe place to hide. I'm bleeding out here, man. Please. Matt: Where are you? Grotto: I got nowhere to go. I'm... I'm at the docks by 12th. Matt: Okay, I'm on my way.

Foggy: Everything okay? Matt: No, I gotta go. That was one of our clients. Karen: Which one? Matt: Grotto. Foggy: The mob guy? Matt: He didn't say much. Just that he needs help. Foggy: All right, well, we'll come with you. Matt: No, it's okay. You guys stay. Finish the game. Karen: Matt... Matt: I'll call you if I need anything.

Matt: Grotto? Grotto! Grotto: Over here. Matt: Jesus. What happened to you? Grotto: Nesbitt. He set up a meet. Some kind of... family dinner or some shit. And then... they came out of nowhere, man. Just started shooting. Everybody. Everybody's dead. Matt: Who? Who did this? Grotto: I don't know. I didn't see. I just ran. Matt: We need to get you to a hospital. Grotto: No! No hospitals. They'll find me there. Matt: You're losing too much blood. If we don't get you help... Grotto: Then I'm dead either way.
Nesbitt: What the... Irish Man: Jesus Christ!

location: HOSPITAL PARKING GARAGE - CONTINUATION FROM PREVIOUS EPISODE
scene_text: Karen: Good. Stay there. Grotto: Matt? Karen: No. I haven't seen him since last night. I'll let him know what's going on. Meet you at the precinct. And don't let anyone talk to Grotto until then.

Grotto: Yo, Brass! It's me, Grotto. Cut the spook act and say something already! Shit, shit. Shit. You don't wanna deal, fine! Find someone else stupid enough to buy H off you! Brass: Good one, asshole. Let's get this done. I got places I gotta be tonight. Officer: We lost visual. Foggy: Mayday! Mayday! Mayday, what do you call it? Abort! Abort! Reyes: I'm a cop, moron. Shut up. Officer: And sound. I can't hear him anymore. Tech: Probably just interference from the metal in the shipping crate. Most likely, ma'am. We'll, uh, try adjusting the gain on it. Brass: Package is delivered. Grotto: What do you mean "package is delivered"? Brass: If I was you, I'd put that on. Grotto: What? Why? Why? Officer: Charlie one is now set. Over. Officer 2: Roger that, Charlie one. Overwatch positions, check in by the numbers. Karen: What exactly is an "overwatch position"? Reyes: Let the police do their job. Officer: Charlie three is set. Clear fields of fire in sectors one and five. Over. Officer 2: Charlie four is set. Clear fields of... Foggy: "Fields of fire" doesn't sound like cop talk to me. That sounds like you're planning an ambush. Karen: Really? You're using my client as bait for the Punisher? Reyes: Probably the first useful thing your client's ever done in his life. Foggy: Oh, I'm gonna have so much fun suing you. Karen: Whatever it is that you have planned here for tonight, it ends now. We're getting Grotto out. Officer: We have a situation taking place on Tac channel one, ma'am! Officer: Target is inbound. Repeat, target is inbound. Reyes: Take him out! Officer: Hold your fire! Move in! Officer 2: Keep your bead! Officer 3: I'll go left! Officer 4: Hands in the air! Now! Reyes: Shit! It's not him, it's a diversion. Target's still out there! The bastard knew it was a trap. Foggy: Shit. Grotto's getting away. We have to go get him. Karen: No, you can't go out there. Foggy: Foggy! Karen: This place is about to become a war zone. Foggy: I don't care. Karen: I know it sucks, but the safest place to be is in this room right now. Foggy: What the hell is that? Reyes: Status report. What's going on out there? Sniper: Target acquired. Reyes: You know what to do. Sniper: Negative. We do not, I repeat, we do not have a clean target. Reyes: Shit! Sniper: You know what to do. Reyes: Take the shot! Sniper: No. Reyes: Ten-four. Take the shot. Repeat, take the shot! Officer: We lost him! Karen: Foggy? Officer 2: Ground floor clear. They're gone. Repeat, they're gone.
Reporter: It was a normal evening at Metro-General when a lone gunman entered and began firing into the crowd. Most of the patients are being moved to other area hospitals. Investigators say...

Officer: The building's clear. Perp is not in the building. Standby to lift lockdown. Dispatcher: All units hold position. We have a report of shots fired earlier on a rooftop up on 10th. Neighbor: Yeah? Foggy: I lost my keys! Neighbor: Your kid locked you out? Foggy: Yeah. Neighbor: You some kind of idiot? Foggy: Yeah. Foggy: Oh, shit. No, no, no, no, no. No! Matt! Come on, Matt, wake up. You okay, Matt? Come on. Get up! Matt! Matt, come on! Wake up. Wake up! Come on! Matt, can you breathe? Matt. Can you get up? Matt: Hey, Foggy, can I get some aspirin? Foggy: You sure you don't want an x-ray? Maybe a psych eval? Matt: An aspirin's fine, buddy. Foggy: You got shot in the head. You're lucky you're not in the morgue. Matt: It was just a dumb mistake, man. Foggy: What? Matt: The gun on his ankle, I... I should've heard it, you know. I should've felt it. Foggy: Are you serious? Matt: Yeah, but he's fast, this guy, Foggy, he's... He's trained. Foggy: He's a lunatic, Matt. I went to the hospital. I saw what he did. Matt: Where's Karen? Foggy: We've been through this. Matt: Oh, yeah, that's right. Yeah, you're sure... you're sure she's okay? Foggy: She got Grotto to the NYPD. We're gonna meet there, make a deal with the DA. Matt: Thanks. Thanks, buddy. I'm gonna put on some pants. Foggy: No. Matt: It's okay. I know we need to get going. Foggy: "We" don't need to do anything. Matt: Foggy, I don't wanna do this right now. Foggy: Karen's safe, you're safe... and our client will be safe within the hour. It's all taken care of. Matt: Except the shooter. He's still walking the streets of Hell's Kitchen. Foggy: He's the cops' problem now. Matt: He's gonna plow right through the cops. I know what you're doing. You saw what he did to the Irish, you didn't see what he did to the Mexican Cartel. He hung them on meat hooks, and he left them there to die. Foggy: You want another round. Matt: Blood is being shed, Foggy. Foggy: And you've donated more than your fair share to the cause. Matt: I need to stop him. Foggy: You need to get rest. Okay? And when you wake up, you need to consider putting that thing back in whatever wacko box it came from. Better yet... Let go. Matt: You first. Foggy: I don't wanna do this again. Matt: Then don't. You know what would've happened if someone caught us stumbling home? You wearing that thing? Foggy: I appreciate it, Foggy. You taking care of me. Matt: You should. But when the cops try to take this guy down, it's gonna be one hell of a fight, lives are gonna be lost. This guy's not gonna go down easy. I need to help. Foggy: You look like shit. Stay here. Get rest. We don't need people asking questions we don't have answers to. I've covered for you enough as it is. And for now, let the NYPD and the DA do their jobs. And trust me to do mine! Okay?

Officer: That window bulletproof? Karen: Twenty cops outside that door. You're safe. Grotto: Where the hell are your boys? Karen: On their way. Detective: Place of birth? Grotto: Queens. Detective: Relatives? Anyone we should place into Witness Protection with you? Grotto: No. I got no one. Detective: You don't seem rattled. A guy tries to blow your head off, you ain't scared? Grotto: I'm terrified. Karen: Sorry. Are you okay? Foggy: Yeah, yeah. Mmm. The paperwork's almost done and Brett's gonna be in in a minute. Karen: Where's Murdock? Foggy: He took a sick day. Detective: You told us the Irish were attacked by a whole gang of guys. I'm pretty sure the word you used was "army." You want to tell me why I'm now hearing this is all being done by one man? Grotto: Look, I didn't know you guys were... Detective: Who does he work for? Grotto: I got no idea! Detective: Well, what do you know? Grotto: I know he's a sociopath, that's what. I mean, yeah, fine... I heard the rumors, okay, but I didn't think... I thought it was ridiculous, okay? Ten, 20 guys could be mowed down at a time. And with precision? You know, tactically.
