Elektra: And now, your mind is racing. You're wondering what you can possibly say or do to keep me on the line, because the last thing you want is to spend the rest of the evening with that scotch and that shaggy-haired friend of yours. Elektra: You know what your problem is? You're pretty. You even work the blind thing. But you're dumb. You lost before you even stepped to the plate. Matt: You get all of that from a pair of old wingtips? Elektra: Quick study. Matt: You wanna know what I think? Elektra: Tell me. Matt: I think the game's just beginning. Matt: Because despite your artisan tequilas and charm-school manners— Despite being richer than God and having the whole world at your fingertips— you're just bored. Elektra: Really? Matt: Bored enough to spend your time studying a stranger's shoes. See, I think you were dying on the vine of this tight-ass party, because Daddy's money can't buy you the one thing you really need. Elektra: And what's that? Matt: The unexpected. Elektra: Maybe you're not so dumb. Elektra Natchios. Matt: Matt Murdock. Let's go, Matthew. Elektra: On your left. Matt: Do you like it? Elektra: Sounds expensive. Matt: You have good ears. Elektra: Is it yours? Matt: It is. Until we get caught.

Karen: Mr. Tower? Tower: Uh, I wish you'd called. I'd have set something up. Karen: Are they in? Tower: Uh, just the Nelson half. Karen: What's the problem? Tower: We need to talk. In private. Tower: You know, it's really not a good idea to piss her off. Foggy: Who? Tower: Reyes. The DA. She's not happy about the Punisher files I leaked to you. Foggy: How does she know? Tower: She has her ways. Look, I'm just saying— watch your back. Both of you. Foggy: We can handle Reyes. Tower: Can you? She's building a case against Castle. A big one. And she doesn't want anyone getting in her way. Foggy: What kind of case? Tower: I don't know all the details. But I know it's personal for her. Something happened. Something she's not talking about. Foggy: What do you mean? Tower: Just— be careful, okay? All of you.

location: FANCY RESTAURANT - MATT AND KAREN'S DATE
scene_text: Karen: Hey. Matt: Hey. Karen: Everything okay? Matt: Yeah, they ran out of wine. Karen: No. Wait, seriously? Matt: Matt— I don't— I don't like this place, you know? Karen: Is it the place? Or is it— Matt: It's definitely not you. Karen: You're sure? Matt: Yeah. I'm positive. Come on. I know where we can go. Karen: Thank you. Matt: Wow, this smells amazing. Matt: What is it? Karen: Um— Who cares? They have wine. Matt: Right. That's— You know, I've always felt more comfortable with the cheap stuff. You know? Karen: Yeah? Matt: Well, here, I'll drink to that. Matt: Cheap stuff. Karen: Cheap stuff. Karen: You know, I never even had Indian food until a few months ago. Matt: How is that possible? Karen: Well, my hometown in Vermont had about 400 people, so the most ethnic food it offered was French fries. Matt: So that's why you, uh, came to New York? For the— for the food? Karen: Uh, no. Although, if I knew places like this existed, I'd have left Vermont ages ago. Matt: You see, that's why I love this city. Karen: Hmm? Matt: I've lived here my whole life, and the place never stops unfolding new secrets. Karen: Hmm. Yeah, you know— despite the crime, and the darkness, every once in a while, New York makes me feel— Like, safe? Matt: Yes, is that weird? Karen: Well— Matt: Huh. Karen: I get it. Matt: I wish you could see this place. Karen: I can, if you describe it to me. Karen: So, anyways, my favorite part is the ceiling. So, it's literally dripping with thousands of lights. They're shaped like chili peppers— which sounds really tacky, I know, but it's, um, it's not. Just— It's magic.

Karen: This is me. Karen: Are you sure you don't— live two more blocks? Matt: Maybe three? Karen: I wish. Matt: We could sit. Karen: Yeah. Matt: All right, I'm gonna kiss ya. Karen: You could come up if you like. Matt: I would love to. Karen: But you won't. Matt: Not tonight. Karen: It's okay. Matt: Can I— Matt: Can I tell you why? Karen: Because I have this incredible ability to bring disaster to the best things in my life— and tonight has been perfect. Karen: Don't you think? Matt: Yes. And if I stop now, then I get to keep this one perfect night. Matt: And also have the chance of keeping it going tomorrow. Karen: And the day after— Matt: And the day after that— Karen: And the— Matt: Exactly. Karen: Then I guess it's good night— Mr. Murdock. Matt: Good night, Ms. Page.

Man 2: Fix me up, man? Fix me up. Man 3: I know who you are, man! I know who you are! Man 4: How much you got, man? How much you got? Roscoe: Oh, Jesus Christ. Roscoe: When I get out of this— Oh, I'll remember your faces. Every single bit of them— I will hunt you! Elektra: Aw— When you get out? Matt: Where did you find him? Elektra: Monte Carlo. I wasn't lying. He's been going by an alias for years now. Al Marino. An ugly name for an ugly man. Roscoe: Oh, you're dead. Both of ya! Couple of kids playing house! Elektra: Hey! Watch your tongue. While it's still attached. He tried to hide. Went underground. But the scum always rises. Al just couldn't stay anonymous. He had to spend his blood money. Make a splash. Be the big man. You made it easy for me. Roscoe: Eat shit. Elektra: Want me to hit you again? Well, I won't. But he will. Roscoe: I don't know him from Christ, but one look and I can tell. Pretty boy ain't got it in him. Matt: You don't remember me? Roscoe: You killed my father. Matt: Well, I hate to break it to you, son— but I killed a lot of guys' dads. Matt: Then let me help you. He hit hard. Like this. Roscoe: You call that hard? Elektra: Let it out. Let it out. Okay? Whatever's inside you. Do it for your father, Matthew. Do it for us. Come on. Roscoe: "Matthew"? Roscoe: You're Battlin' Jack's boy! Oh, you amateur. Now I know your name. Nothing'll stop me from bloodying the street with your corpse. Just like I did to your old man! Elektra: Yes. Elektra: End it. End it now. Matt: What? Elektra: Keep going. Matt: No, that's, uh— No, that's all I got. Elektra: No— He knows your name. Cut his throat. Kill him. Matt: What? Elektra: Kill him. Matt: I can't do that. Elektra: We can do anything together. Remember? Matt: No, I can't. Elektra: I thought you understood me. Matt: Yeah, I thought I did, too. We need to call the police. Operator: 911, what is your emergency? Matt: Um— Yes, I'd like to report the location of a wanted felon. Matt: The name is Roscoe Sweeney. Operator: What is the address?
Yakuza Leader: The hacker is on the ninth floor. Move quickly. Quietly. When we are done, we bring the boss all ten fingers. Yakuza Member: Questions?

Yakuza Boss: We have spent hundreds of millions of dollars, and decades of planning on this operation. And now... our most valuable secrets have been stolen. I'd be very disappointed to learn you aided this theft in any way, Gibson-san. Gibson: I... I had nothing to do with it. Yakuza Boss: We entrusted you with access. Even employed security to protect you and ensure the sanctity of our operation. Gibson: I was in the bathroom. We were attacked. Listen! Listen, I would never betray you! I have nothing but respect for the Yakuza! Yakuza Boss: Who said I was Yakuza? Foggy: Foggy? Matt: You weren't answering your phone. Foggy: Why are you fancy? Matt: What's going on? Foggy: The arraignment. Frank pled not guilty, Matt. Matt: What? Foggy: And it gets worse. Reyes pulled every string she has and fast-tracked the trial. Matt: What... All right. All right, all right, so we, uh... we motion to extend. We, um... maybe streamline our case theory, and not waste time fighting any charges... Foggy: You don't understand, Matt! Frank agreed! He thinks he's stickin' it to Reyes or something. I hope your schedule is clear, buddy. 'Cause The People v. Frank Castle... starts next week.

Elektra: Hungry? Matt: Mmm. Elektra: Come on, that's enough. You've eaten enough. Talk. Waitress: Warm that up for you? Pie? Elektra: Don't tell me you're watching your figure. Matt: We just fought the Yakuza. Elektra: And won! Matt: You might've mentioned the Japanese mafia before butterfly knives started flying. Elektra: I told you I needed help, no? Matt: You said you needed a lawyer. Elektra: I lied. Matt: Yeah, no shit. You've been lying since you got here. And that ends now. I want to know what you're doing back here, what's happening with the Yakuza... And I wanna know how you know... I wanna know how you know about me. Elektra: I know who you are because I watch the news. "The successful apprehension of Wilson Fisk." Matt: I wear a mask. Elektra: Well, you can't mask that ass. I'd know it anywhere. You've been working out, by the way. I appreciate that. Matt: The Yakuza are a powerful organization with powerful enemies. Elektra: Mmm-hmm. Matt: What do they want with you? Elektra: I guess I have a way of pissing people off sometimes. Matt: Yeah, I agree. Elektra: Come on. Don't be angry, Matthew. I told you. My money's planted deeply inside investments with the Roxxon Corporation. And Roxxon has ties to crime. Matt: How long have you known that? Elektra: I didn't. Until last night. I stirred the pot a little on the business side. And when I did, who came knocking on my door but the Yakuza. Their mistake, because now, they're after us. Matt: No. Uh-uh. There is no us. This is your problem. Why can't you just divest your funds from Roxxon and be done with it? Elektra: That's a coward's way out. Someone screwed with me. I don't like that. Matt: Then get a lawyer. Elektra: I thought I did. Matt: Call the police. Elektra: You're one to talk. Devil of Hell's Kitchen... Matt: Would you keep your voice down? What I do is none of your business, all right? Not anymore. Elektra: Matthew... Matt: Let me tell you what's gonna happen now. You're gonna finish your food, you're gonna leave the waitress the biggest tip she's ever seen, then you're gonna get up and leave. You're gonna book yourself on the first available flight out of New York... and get on it, go back to whatever spa, or resort, or five-star hotel you just came from, and stay out of my city. If the Yakuza have their sights set on something bigger than your spoiled little rich ass, then I will take care of them. Elektra: Let me tell you. The Yakuza do have a bigger plan, and I'm not going anywhere. Matt: You can't fight them. Elektra: And you can? Matt: I drove them out of New York once before. Elektra: Oh, no, you didn't. The Yakuza never left. They just hibernated and watched you take out all of their enemies. Now, New York is ripe for the taking, and they plan on getting to the top of the hill first. Matt: Well, I'll scare 'em back into hibernation... Elektra: I came to you. If you don't want to be partners, I'll handle it on my own... Matt: Partners? Waitress: More coffee? Matt: No. I don't need a partner. Elektra: Yes, you do. And so do I. Because you have skills. You fight better than anyone I know. But I have information. I gained access to Roxxon's servers right in front of their little criminal faces. We do it together, we take them down fast and hard. The second it's done, I'm out of your city. Forever. Matt: The last time I saw you, you put a knife in my hand and asked me to slit Roscoe Sweeney's throat. I happen to respect human life. If we do this... If... then I need to know you're at least gonna pretend to feel the same way. Nobody dies. Do you understand? Do you understand? Elektra: Oh, perfectly. Matt: Good. I have a rule of my own. Elektra: Shoot. Matt: No sex. Elektra: Oh, my God. You have a pair on you. Matt: Mmm? Elektra: This may come as a surprise to you, but I've actually moved on in the ten years since you left. I'm seeing someone now, which is only part of the reason why I have zero interest in ever starting anything up with you ever again. Elektra: Of course you do. Check, please. Matt: You're still so arrogant. Elektra: Just realistic. What makes you think every man you meet wants to sleep with you? Matt: Because so far, they have. Elektra: We do this... we work together, we take down the Yakuza, and then you're gone. I don't wanna ever see you again. Matt: Absolutely. Elektra: Fine. One last thing. And this is the deal-breaker. Matt: You have to give me back that pie.

Roth: So, um, Miss Page, I drew this up based on your official statement to the police, about the Metro-General shooting. Karen: You new to New York, Mr. Roth? Roth: Born and raised. Karen: Is this your first case? Roth: Second. I won my first. Domestic violence. I believe in protecting women. Karen: Thanks. From all of us. Roth: Uh, here, this says that Castle pursued me down the stairwell, but I went down, he went up. Karen: Um, okay, that's a change I can make. Roth: Also, I didn't escape on foot, I had a car. I know I told the NYPD about that. Karen: Um... car. Roth: I was also not Castle's only target. That's just flat out wrong. What about Grotto? Where... Where did you get my statement? Karen: Grotto? Roth: Grote. Karen: Oh, Elliot Grote. Yeah, he's on the victim list. Ballistics matched him to one of the many guns connected to Frank Castle. Matt: Early start today? Karen: Matt. Uh, this is Christopher Roth. He's the public defender assigned to the Castle case. I just dropped by to get Miss Page's signature on this statement. Once we've got that, we're all done. Roth: Well, with this meeting. With this case. Matt: How so? Roth: Castle's awake. Soon, he'll plead guilty, then it's open and shut. Matt: Open and shut is good. New York will sleep better knowing Frank Castle's behind bars. I know I will. Roth: Sleep even better when he's dead. Karen: Uh, dead? Roth: Well, lethal injection, probably, although the electric chair is a possibility. Karen: New York doesn't have the death penalty. Roth: Yeah, but Delaware does. Some Dogs of Hell were murdered out there along Interstate 95. DA Reyes just has to link the killings to Castle, and then they'll be well within their rights to extradite him. And... you know... Karen: Are you and DA Reyes friends? Roth: I met her once. Karen: When? Roth: Yesterday, when the judge assigned me to the case. But, look... She's the one who took down the Punisher. She's not going through all these paces so that she can not put the final nail in his coffin. Literally. Karen: I'm sorry, Mr. Roth, I can't sign this yet. Roth: Um... Karen: Are you sure? Matt: Positive. Roth: We'll be in touch, Mr. Roth. Karen: I'm sure we will. Karen: Statement he wanted me to sign? Complete work of fiction. Probably handcrafted by Reyes. Matt: Well, we could write an anonymous letter, and maybe the judge will assign a new public defender. Karen: Yeah, or we could help Castle ourselves. Matt: No way. Karen: Yeah. We don't have to defend him. We could just negotiate a plea deal. Without extradition, or an electric chair. And then, Castle goes away, Reyes gets her ticker-tape parade... everyone wins. Matt: Everyone except us. You see the front door? The "open" sign is up, but nobody's walking in. If we keep messing with Reyes, we'll be shuttered by the end of the month. Karen: Come on, if we stand up to her, we could actually end her incessant bullying. And possibly save this guy's life. Matt: A murderer who shot at you. Karen: For reasons that I don't fully understand yet. Matt: Roth said Castle's gonna plead guilty. So we get in there, we talk to him... Ask him some questions about what really happened to his family, why Reyes wants him dead. Build a fair plea, and show the DA our justice system... still has a backbone. Matt: This is a bad idea, Matt. Foggy: Um... Karen: It's okay, I'll be outside. Foggy: I can't believe we're even discussing this. He chained you to a roof. You, of all people, should know he's a psychopath. Matt: Okay, his methodology is clearly wrong, but... in his own kind of way, he was trying to do something noble. Foggy: Do you hear yourself? Matt: Yeah. He wanted justice, Foggy, like us. Foggy: So we should risk everything... our firm, our reputation, and... and let's be honest, our safety? We should put it all on the line to help him? Matt: Kinda. Yeah. Foggy: Is this about saving a man or saving a vigilante? Matt: He's a person. Like you, Foggy. Like me. And he shouldn't have to die. Matt: Karen, grab your stuff. We're going to the hospital.

Security: You can't have cell phones in this area, sir! Foggy: What's going on? Security: Reporters. Looks like every outlet in town wants a word with Castle. Or a report on who does. Come on. Brett: You press? Foggy: Uh, no, attorneys. Brett: IDs? Foggy: This much spotlight concern anyone else? I mean, we're about to step onto a big proscenium stage here. Matt: And how do I know what proscenium means? Foggy: Because I did theater in summer camp... ...which is exactly the kind of thing that these reporters will find out when they start looking for dirt on us. Matt: Relax, Foggy. They're not gonna look. Karen: Not until we make them.

Brett: Five minutes. Foggy: Mr. Castle, I'm Franklin Nelson, this is Matthew Murdock. We're attorneys. Frank: I know who you are. Got your a*s kicked by the Irish. Good times. Matt: We, uh, we'd like to talk to you about your case. Frank: I already got a lawyer. Foggy: Christopher Roth. He's a public defender. And we have reason to believe he's working with the DA to build a case against you. Frank: So what? Matt: So we'd like to help. Frank: Why? Karen: Because we think what happened to your family... we think there's more to it than what's being reported. Frank: You the girl from the hospital? Karen: Yes. Frank: You got a set of balls on you, lady. Coming back here. Karen: Yeah, well, I wanted to talk to you about what happened. Frank: Nothing to talk about. Matt: Mr. Castle, if you plead guilty, you could face the death penalty. Frank: Good. Foggy: Good? Frank: I got nothing left. My family's gone. I don't give a shit what happens to me. Matt: Then why are you still fighting? Frank: Because I'm not done yet. Karen: Not done with what? Frank: Making them pay. Every single one of them. Matt: Who's "them"? Frank: The ones who took my family from me. Foggy: The Irish? The Dogs of Hell? Frank: All of them. Anyone who had a hand in it. Matt: Mr. Castle, if you let us help you, we can make sure you get a fair trial. We can make sure the truth comes out. Frank: Truth? You want the truth? The truth is my wife and kids are dead. And nothing you do is gonna bring them back. Karen: No. But we can make sure that whoever's responsible is held accountable. Frank: I'm holding them accountable. My way. Matt: Your way gets you killed. Frank: Like I said. I don't give a shit. Foggy: Okay, well, we do. So if you change your mind— Frank: I won't. Brett: Time's up. Foggy: We'll be in touch, Mr. Castle. Foggy: Well, that went well. Karen: He's hurting. He's lost everything. Matt: That doesn't give him the right to kill people. Karen: I know. But maybe... maybe we can help him see that.

Karen: Mr. Castle? Frank: You again. Karen: I wanted to apologize. For earlier. We shouldn't have ambushed you like that. Frank: It's fine. Karen: Can I ask you something? Frank: Depends. Karen: Why did you let me live? At the hospital. You could have killed me. But you didn't. Frank: You want me to say I'm sorry? Is that it? Karen: No. I just... I want to understand. Frank: Look, you got any idea what a scout sniper is? You ever heard of that? No? Karen: No. Frank: Okay, well, you're looking at one. My class in Quantico was class 307. And we had a... a motto. It was a saying, yeah? It was, "One shot, one kill." The point is, if I wanted you dead, you'd be dead. Karen: Why... why am I here? Why did you ask me to stay? Frank: I don't... I guess I worry that... the memories are just gonna go away. Karen: Mr. Castle... Frank: Look, you... You went to... You were in my house. You... You never went back? Karen: After your family was... Frank: No. Karen: Can I just ask you, did you... Were you in the kitchen? Frank: Yes. Karen: The plates, were they... Were they on the table, or did they get into the sink? Frank: Um... Uh... I think, washed. In the rack. Karen: How about in the next room, did you... Did you see that piano that was there? Frank: Yeah. Yeah. Karen: Yeah? Frank: My son, Frank Junior, he... He used to grab a handful of cookies and take 'em and hide 'em in that bench. You know, he'd play soldier. Guard it, protect it. Karen: Oh, yeah? Frank: Then he'd fall asleep down there. We'd find him... He'd be sleeping on a pile of... pile of cookie crumbs. Karen: Yeah, I, um... When I was little girl, I did the same thing. Except ginger snaps and, um, broom closet. Frank: Oh, yeah? Karen: Pretend it was a spaceship. Take me... far away. Frank: Did you? Karen: Yeah. I guess we need that, right? We need to get away sometimes. Karen: I went up into the kids' bedrooms. There were drawings on the walls and, uh, sports trophies on the dressers. Frank: Yeah, I was gone a lot, so I didn't... I missed a lot of that. Karen: There were toys... scattered all over the ground, um... A lot of plastic dinosaurs. Frank: Yeah, those were my little girl's. Those were Lisa's. When she was little, she used to make these little noises when she played with them. Karen: What about the little... the little car? Like a... Like a remote-controlled Jeep. Frank: Yeah, yeah, that, uh... That was Frank Junior's. I got that for him for his seventh birthday. He used to... Yeah, he drove me crazy with that thing. Karen: Look, Frank, it's... It's really not for me to say... but they clearly loved you. Very much. Frank: Yeah... Okay... Here. Karen: Thank you. Frank: Thank you, ma'am. Karen: For what? Frank: You helped... You helped me remember. Karen: You're welcome. If you wanna ask your questions, you can go ahead. Frank: Blind bastard. Elektra: Ugh, could one of you grab me a club soda? Matt: Come on. Elektra: Oh, for Christ's sake.

Security: What the hell? Did the power go out, or did you hit the switch? Elektra: This will erase the recordings and loop the security cameras. Matt: This way. Elektra: One second. Matt: Floor's crawling with security. Come with me. Elektra: It's your lucky day, Mr. Castle.

Foggy: The six Dogs of Hell gang members you wiped out in Delaware? Won't be an issue anymore. Delaware doesn't have the evidence to charge and extradite, so... the death penalty is officially off the table. But Reyes also wanted three life sentences without the possibility of parole. But as the Nelson in Nelson and Murdock, I got her down to one, with the possibility of parole in 25 years. That's the good news. Matt: And the bad? Foggy: She wouldn't budge on protective custody. He's gonna have to be in general pop. Karen: Uh, no, that's bullshit. All right? He'll be... He'll be surrounded by criminals, people out for his blood. Frank: Sounds like a party. Matt: No doubt you can handle yourself, but I think Reyes is betting on the gangs here. Legally, though? I think this is the best possible deal we're gonna make right now. So... I recommend you take it. Frank: Okay. Foggy: Okay, so, when the judge and Reyes come in... all you have to do is say three simple words. "Guilty, Your Honor." And you'll never have to see us again. Frank: Can do. Judge: Case number 4854, The People v. Frank Castle. Do you waive the reading of the charges? Foggy: Yes, Your Honor. Judge: All right, then. How does the defendant plead? Frank: I plead not guilty. You hear that, witch? I'm gonna watch you burn right along with me. Do you hear me? Judge: Counselor, please control your client. Frank: Do you hear me? Foggy: I'm sorry, Your Honor. Judge: The defendant has entered a plea of not guilty. Due to the nature and severity of the crimes he is accused of, bail is denied. A court date will be set upon consultation with the DA's office. We are adjourned. Karen: Holy shit. Foggy: That was not supposed to happen. Reyes: What'd you say to him? Foggy: What? Reyes: Three hours ago, he was pleading guilty. Why did he change his mind? Karen: Maybe he just wants the truth. About Grotto, about his family, about the... ...the cover-up. I mean, if we go to trial, then it all comes out, right? Reyes: There's no "if." This is happening. Trial of the century. Foggy: We need to find Matt before this goes wide. Tell him everything's about to change.

Elektra: Elektra. Elektra. Matt: Not bad, Magoo. Security: Eyes on Gibson? Security 2: He's in the men's room, sir. Matt: It's there. Elektra: It's not there. Matt: It was supposed to be there. Elektra: I take it it's not here. Matt: It was supposed to be there. Elektra: If they find Gibson, we're toast. We have to go. Matt: Matthew! Elektra: Shh. Security: Stop the elevators. We have an intruder on the 13th floor. Yakuza Boss: Pull up security footage. I want to know who got to them. Tech: Quick! Pull up the cameras on the 13th floor. Matt: What? Elektra: There's something behind this wall. There's an electrical current running through it. Matt: Yeah? Where? Elektra: An interruption in the signal... here. Matt: Okay. Okay... Ah. Elektra: I'm a genius. Here, this one. Matt: Books, paper. Tech: Hiro, get in here. They're on a loop. Yakuza Boss: Sir, we found the problem. Security: All security, report to the 13th floor. Elektra: This is it. The Roxxon ledger. Matt: Not now, we gotta go. Elektra: I don't speak Japanese, but I think they know we're here. Matt: It's not working. Elektra: They're gonna see us. Yakuza Boss: Shut the power. Close the gates. Elektra: Shit, they found us. Matt: Let's go. Elektra: They've shut down the floor. They're coming. Now. Security: Don't move! Elektra: Oh! Oh, my goodness! Security: We got something. 11th floor. Elektra: We are so sorry. This is, uh, very embarrassing. We just... thought we could, uh, sneak in here. But we'll be right out of here... Matt: Sir... Elektra: He'll make a big donation. He's very rich. Matt: Oh... Elektra: Please, sweetheart, just... Matt: Ow. Elektra: Very sorry, sir. Security: Shut up! Nothing but a couple drunks. Keep checking the 13th floor. Elektra: Thank you. Security: You need to leave. Elektra: Yes, certainly. Once again, we're so sorry, we didn't... Security: Now! Matt: Would you keep your shit together? Elektra: Calm down. Elektra: Invoices for arms. Matt: Guns, ammunition... Elektra: You read Japanese? Matt: Mmm-hmm. Elektra: Drugs. Designer stuff, mostly. And this looks like people. Laborers of some sort. Sounds like a lot of them. Over the past several months. And all from Japan. Matt: Oh, what is this? Elektra: What is it? Matt: I don't know. This one, I can't read. Elektra: What do you mean? Matt: It's in some kind of code. Elektra: This doesn't make sense. If invoices for drugs and guns and human trafficking aren't encrypted, then what is? Matt: Wow, what are they hiding? Elektra: Same time tomorrow, Matthew?

Judge: Potential juror number 17, please state your name. Juror 1: Richard Day. Prosecutor: Can you state for the court any preexisting opinion, any at all, that you may hold for the defendant, Frank Castle? Juror 1: You mean the Punisher? I think he's an animal... a sick, twisted, venal... Juror 2: Hero. That's what we should be calling him. Doing the things the cops won't do, Frank Castle is a... Juror 3: A grotesque insult to the Second Amendment, a fascist without the authority. If you ask me, people like Frank Castle ought to be... Juror 4: Applauded for putting all the thieves and muggers and rapists in the morgue, where they belong. Let those bastards feel scared walking down the street for a change. Juror 5: It's Son of Sam all over again. It's Bernie Goetz... Juror 6: It's like the only thing protecting us is Frank. Juror 7: I just moved my family to New York, and now we're moving out. If anyone can kill anyone in this town... where does the insanity end? Judge: Counselors, over 400 potential jurors have come through this courtroom. So I should tell you, if you can't agree to move forward with the 12 men and women selected, I will make this trial a living hell for all of you. Foggy: Your Honor, New York hasn't seen a trial this divisive and this public in years. Finding an impartial jury is not easy. Everybody has an opinion about Frank Castle. Judge: It's New York, Mr. Nelson. Everybody has an opinion about everything. Ms. Reyes, is the prosecution satisfied with its jury panel? Reyes: Yes, Your Honor. Judge: And the defense, Mr. Nelson? Foggy: Uh, yes, Your Honor, we are. Judge: Thank Christ. The trial of The People of New York v. Frank Castle is now in session.

Foggy: If I get my hands on the worthless intern who organized these files... Karen: Oh, I'm sure that intern's just following the DA's orders. It's not officially sabotage, just sets it back. I'll tell you. I'm gonna tell you exactly what kind of man you are. You're the kind of man this city needs. Because, ladies and gentlemen of the jury, we all know this city needs help. Needs it now. Not tomorrow, not next week, not when the day comes, when the corruption that Wilson Fisk left in his wake is flushed out for good, and the police force is finally back on its feet. We need it now. 'Cause this city's been sick. And the cops, they can't fix it alone, they need... We all need men and women who are willing to take the fight themselves. The kind of people who risk their lives so that we can walk safe at night in our own neighborhoods. The ones our esteemed District Attorney here is trying so hard to destroy. New York needs these people. We need... heroes. Judge: Order. Matt: The help they offer... ...and the hope that they provide. Frank Castle wanted to help, but he took it too far. He shot people, he killed people. It's against the law. And he broke that law many, many times. Now, I don't like him any more than you do, but here's the thing, he's not a common criminal. He's not malicious in intent. Frank Castle is actually a good man. He just... He doesn't know the difference between right and wrong anymore. And he doesn't need punishment for that. He needs help. Our help. That's the kind of man Frank Castle is. And now, you have to decide what kind of jury you want to be. No further questions, Your Honor. Frank: Your, uh... Your Honor? Can I say something? Judge: You may. Frank: You know those, uh... Those people? The ones I put down, the people I killed? I want you to know that I'd do it all again. This is a circus, all right? It's a charade, it's an act. It's bullshit about how crazy I am. Judge: Language. Frank: I ain't crazy! I'm not crazy. Okay? I know what I did. I know who I am. And I do not need your help. I'm smack-dab in the middle of my right goddamn mind, and any scumbag, any... any lowlife, any maggot piece of shit that I put down, I did it... because I liked it! Judge: Order! Frank: Hell, I loved it! I'm sittin' here, I'm... I'm just itching. I'm itching to do it again. And you think... What, you think you're gonna send me to a nuthouse? Some doctor, they're gonna get me to stop from doing what I want to do? Well, that ain't happening! Not on my watch! You people, you call me the Punisher, ain't that right? The big bad Punisher. Judge: Bailiff. Frank: Well, here I am! Judge: Remove the witness. Frank: You want it, you got it! I am the Punisher! I'm right here! You want it, I'll give it to you. And anybody who came here today to hear me whine, to hear me beg? Well, you can kiss my ass! Do you hear me? I'm guilty. Judge: Come on, please, Judge! Frank: I'm guilty, you hear me? I'm guilty! I'm guilty! I'll kill every one of 'em! I'll kill every single one! Foggy: How the hell did this happen? Karen: That wasn't the Frank I met with yesterday. Matt: Guys... I think somebody got to him. Foggy: Convincing him of what? Yelling his way to multiple life sentences? Karen: You provoked him. Matt: What? I didn't... Foggy: What are you talking... Karen: I had it lined up for you. We could have done this. We could have gotten the charges reduced. All you had to do was get Frank to tell his story. Instead you veer off into vigilante-land! Matt: Foggy, he wasn't cooperating! Foggy: I'm glad we lost. You hear me? I'm glad. Matt: Foggy... Karen: Karen, let him go. Foggy: I don't want to hear it. Karen, can I talk to you for five seconds, please? Karen: I don't want to hear another bullshit excuse! Maybe you are an alcoholic. Maybe you're in a fight club. Maybe you are sleeping with a whole harem of women. I don't care, I'm done. You're right. This city really needs heroes. But you're not one of them.

Elektra: You gotta feel like shit. Matt: Go back to bed. Elektra: I can barely stand. Matt: Then go back to bed. Elektra: No. I don't want to be with you anymore. I want to be with him. Stick: Don't be stupid. Elektra: He needs more training. The Hand is new to him... Stick: Soft. Matt Murdock is soft. He made you soft. You let your guard down. Go back to bed, Ellie. Elektra: I'm not a child. Stick: You can't be with him. Elektra: Why? Stick: You can't change what you are. Elektra: Matthew thinks I can. And I believe him. Stick: Get out... before I get nasty. Elektra: Are you threatening me? Stick: You're damn right, I am. Elektra: Go. Stick: What do you think he'll say... when he finds out... what you are? What you've always been? Haven't told him yet... have ya? Elektra: Get out. Stick: Aside from saving your ass... you have no idea what I've protected you from. Elektra: I can protect myself. Stick: We'll find out. Enough with these amateurs. Time to get the band back together. Head to the Wall.

Matt: Where's Stick? Elektra: I made my choice. He didn't like it. I want to be with you. The only person in this world who believes I'm good. Matt: You lost today. Elektra: It doesn't matter. Matt: You lost more than just the case. Elektra: Yeah. I didn't lose you. Matt: I'm sorry. Elektra: I'm not. Matt: How does this work? You and me? How can we make it work? Elektra: I don't know. But we're gonna figure it out. Not now, though. Right now, you need to rest.

Matt: Who do you work for? Huh? Who sent you? Answer me! Huh? You tell them, whoever they are, I'm gonna find them, and when I do, I'm gonna... No... You're... You're just a kid. Elektra: Elektra, no... No... What did you do? Matt: This is who I am. Do you still want me? Elektra: Matthew. Matthew! Matt: You're okay... You're okay...

Guard 1: I got this one. Guard 2: On whose orders? Guard 1: The warden's. You got a problem with that? Guard 2: No one tells us anything down here. Prisoner: Hey, look at me, Frank! Look at me! I'm gonna stick you! That's a promise! I promise you! Frank: Right through here. Kingpin: I see you got my message.
Guard: All right, watch your head. Inmate 5-5-4-6-7. Fisk, Wilson. Guard 2: Everything off. Clothing and personal items in the bin. Newbies wear white. That's yours.

Ellison: It wasn't just a random gang shootout. It was a sting. Karen: Who knows who's involved? Ellison: Cops, DA's office, obviously. Karen: The mayor? How high does this go? Ellison: I don't know. But I can tell by that look in your eye that you're not gonna get any rest till you figure it out. So if you wanna camp out in here... it's all yours. Start digging. Karen: Are you serious? Ellison: I'm very serious. Ben was the best researcher I've ever known. Karen: I remember. Ellison: Did you... Karen: Read that? Yes. Yeah, I... I read it. Look, Ben didn't care, and I don't, either. Get to work, okay? Go.

Fisk: Are you sure that's a good idea, Mr. Fisk? Guard: Go now! How quickly we turn into savages. As if the moment we walk through these prison doors... Frank: You tried to have me killed. Fisk: Yes, it would've been cleaner that way, but you got what you wanted! Given the condition that he was in, I assume that Dutton admitted to some involvement in your tragedy. Frank: What do you want? Why am I still alive? Fisk: Because plans change. Because if you want to survive, you adapt. Yes! The plan was to kill you. I needed to close that loop. I'd already made a deal with the rest of the guards. I doubled the cut that Dutton was paying them. But that didn't work out, did it? No, I was wrong. That's difficult to admit, but... you have a gift, Mr. Castle. I assumed that the stories that I read in the paper about your attacks on the criminal world were apocryphal. How could one man be capable of such... violence? But then I saw it... with my own two eyes. And when one comes across someone with such talent... with such a gift... well... you don't let that go to waste. No. No, you don't. Frank: How's that? Fisk: Release him. Guard: Mr. Fisk, I... Fisk: Do it now! Frank: What the hell is this? Fisk: I'm in control now. And I've set you free. Frank: What does that mean, "free"? Fisk: I'll show you. Frank: Stay back. 'Cause everyone warned me that prison would be an inhumane environment. It is. But I... I find it refreshing. The perfect microcosm of the animal world. When an animal wants something, when it needs something, other things... need to be stepped on. Fisk: You want me on the outside so I step on every piece of shit I see. That way, nobody gets strong, and we... The city's yours for the taking. Frank: Something like that. Yeah. Fisk: So if you can do that, if you can get me out, why not just do it yourself? Frank: Because I play the long game, Mr. Castle. You see, when I'm finally let out of this cage... it won't be to wage war. It will be to win one. You, sir... you need to focus on now. I've given you a chance to walk free. To put that gift of yours to work, to find... What does Dutton call him? The Blacksmith. Fisk: If I were in your shoes... I would use this opportunity to find your justice, to kill your way to justice! And not for me. Of course not. Not for yourself. For your family. For them. Frank: Fisk. Fisk: Yes? Frank: You know... next time I see you... only one of us walks away. Fisk: Yes, of course. I'm counting on it.

Daredevil: Is someone there? Gibson: Someone... These people... Jesus. What are they doing to you? Prisoner: Daniel. Daniel! Gibson: Daniel. Oh, Daniel! We're gonna get them out. Stan, we're gonna get them all out. Prisoner: Daniel, my boy. Oh, my boy. Oh, my boy. Gibson: Keys. Prisoner: Just hold on, my son. Come here. Thank God. Thank God. God. Daredevil: Get down! Nobu: They weren't finished.

Fisk: The physician says that your condition is... is grave. That your lungs are filling with liquid. In a few hours, you're likely to suffocate in your own blood. But you won't suffer alone. I'll be here. Because you were right. In prison, there's only room for one kingpin. Dutton: You still have scars to remember me by, I hope. Fisk: Wait... You're dead. Nobu: There is no such thing.

Donovan: I deeply regret that it's come to this, Mr. Fisk. I assure you my firm did everything we could... but the case against you was, quite simply, bulletproof. Fisk: How is the progress regarding my appeal, Mr. Donovan? Donovan: We're making progress, but I have to be honest. Given the magnitude of charges, we were lucky we could plead you out at all. Fisk: Vanessa, huh? Donovan: I've secured a percentage of your holdings offshore, as requested. Fisk: She wants to come see you. Donovan: She can't. She must stay where she's safe for the time being. Fisk: Of course. She'll have everything she needs. But with that said, you need to understand that a good number of your assets were seized by the government, Mr. Fisk. Your remaining capital is... limited. Donovan: How long will she be safe for? Fisk: Long enough. Donovan: Mr. Fisk, I'm doing everything I can to get you out, but we're talking about a process that could take months, maybe years. In the interim, we need you to keep your head down and avoid trouble while you're in here. The state will jump on any infraction to shoot down an early release... to keep you inside. It's the best move, Mr. Fisk. In fact, it's the only move. Fisk: Those you cannot teach to fly, teach to fall faster.

Dutton: Wilson Fisk. The boogeyman of crime. The man who cast a shadow in the dark. Fisk: You'll stop reading those eventually. It's best to accept that real life is what happens on the inside. Dutton: Maybe your life, Mr. Dutton, not mine. Fisk: We never met before, have we? Dutton: No, but your reputation precedes you. A life of running drugs buys you that much in New York City. You may have made a name for yourself on the outside... but I run the big box. I just wanna make that clear... in case you get any ideas about stepping up. Fisk: I have no intentions of doing that. Dutton: Cut the shit, fat man. I've known guys like you my whole life. I killed most of 'em. You ain't never seen a throne you didn't wanna sit in. So I'm here to make myself crystal clear. There's only room for one of us in this prison, and it ain't gonna be you. Not ever. Because I'm the kingpin of this bitch. Dutton: Catch you later. Stewart: Mind if I sit? Fisk: Fine. Stewart: I won't bother you. Just wanted to meet. You know, in here, guys like us need to stick together. Fisk: Guys like us? Stewart: I was a mortgage analyst on the outside. Seven figure salary, summer house in the Hamptons. Just made the wrong deal, crossed the wrong guy. It turned out that his brother was some bigwig in the Justice Department. Some luck, huh? Look, what I mean is... we're not like these savages in here. That's all. Smart to steer clear of that asshole. Fisk: It's not just the guys at his table that are on his side. He runs about 80% of the contraband in this place. Most of the guards are in his pocket, from what I can tell. Stewart: The two men you were speaking to. Fisk: Valdez brothers. Stewart: They your friends? Fisk: Slim pickings in here, but, yeah. Yeah, they don't talk much. Let's just say what they did to get in here was ghastly. Stewart: Do they have family? Fisk: A mother. She'll be alone for a while.

Donovan: I wish I had better news, Mr. Fisk, but the appeal... Fisk: I didn't ask you here for that. Donovan: Oh. Fisk: I need you to write down the following. The office of Caplan and Dayhill... they have a client, his name is Stewart Finney. He needs his legal retainer bolstered. Donovan: What? Fisk: Andrea Valdez. She's 62. She lives in Spanish Harlem. Needs her rent paid indefinitely. Donovan: What is this? Fisk: Untraceable, if you handle it correctly. Donovan: Mr. Fisk, I warned you about getting involved in the... Fisk: Get it done!

Guard: Fisk. Fisk: Anything on Dutton? Guard: He and his men haven't emerged from block A today. No way to get in. That wing's impenetrable. Fisk: For now. Guard: The paper's interesting, though. Check out the front page. The Punisher. Apparently, he gunned down the Irish in a big way. Fisk: Mmm, Nesbitt was a problematic leader. Guard: He took out the Dogs of Hell, too. Blew up their clubhouse. They charged him with 37 counts of murder. Fisk: Wow, perhaps his name suits him. Guard: I'd say. Rumor is some of the Cartel got meat hooks through their faces. Fisk: The Cartel? Guard: The Mexicans. Fisk: If I'm correct... Dutton didn't do business with the Cartel. On the 22nd, Dutton's lieutenant mentioned... a deal with the Aryans to move product in the Dogs' territory. A hostile takeover. Does Dutton have connections with the Irish? Guard: Some heroin deal gone south. That was a while back, though. Fisk: I know what I'm asking for will be difficult. Guard: I'm not worried about difficult. I'm not even worried about illegal. Your funds have almost been depleted. Building up your little protection crew wasn't cheap. Fisk: Nor should it be. Guard: Your cash is almost gone. If I do this, that's it. After that, anything you need for the rest of your stay, you'll be dipping into the reserves, into Vanessa's protection. Fisk: I won't need anything after this. Guard: This guard you've spoken to, do I want to know what you'll be asking him to do?

Fisk: I see you got my message. Frank: Shh, I've got you, Matthew. Fisk: Who's... who's there? Elektra: Elektra? Matt: Oh, slowly. You okay? Elektra: Where is he? Matt: Stick? He left. Remember? Elektra: No, not Stick. The boy. The one you killed. Matt: It's been taken care of. Elektra: Not "it." He. Matt: Well, he tried to kill you. Elektra: He was scared. He was just a kid. Matt: If you'd spared him, he would've sent his big brothers after us. I killed him in self-defense. Even your precious court of law would say that's legitimate... Elektra: It doesn't work that way. Matt: Well... it's a good thing I'm not on trial. Elektra: We need to tell the police. Matt: Tell them what? I killed a member of an ancient organization of ninjas that are digging a giant hole in midtown Manhattan? Perhaps we should. Maybe they need a laugh. Elektra: But you and I, we've seen it. The Hand is very real. And they know we're onto them. The battle has begun, Matthew. There's nothing we can do about it now but fight. Matt: Look... I wish I could tell you that I'm not going to pull my sword... but I will if I have to. Elektra: You said you wanted to be good. Matt: I do. Elektra: But you don't. I saw it ten years ago with Roscoe Sweeney... and I saw it again last night. Your adrenaline spiked, Elektra. You enjoy killing. Matt: And you may say you wanna be good for me, but that's not who you really are, is it? Elektra: The first time I took a life... I was 12 years old. I did it of my own volition. I wasn't saving another. I wasn't even protecting myself. I did it... because I needed to know that I could. Not that I could get away with it. Not that I could get used to it. Matt: And you enjoyed it. Elektra: You know, Stick taught us to never let anyone get close. Matt: I fell in love with you. Elektra: I loved you, too. That wasn't a lie. Matt: I fell in love with you, so I don't want to keep judging you for who you are. And this... this is who I am. Elektra: We have to stop corrupting each other. We can't do this anymore. Say something. Matt: The Hand will decimate your city. Elektra: Not if I stop them. Matt: You'll die. Elektra: Yeah, maybe. But this is a war I need to fight alone. Goodbye, Elektra.

Fisk: The circumstances are unfortunate, but each loss brings opportunity. I'm glad we have this chance to meet. Frank: Hmm. You have something you wanna say to me? Fisk: I've been following your case... as much as one could in this cage. I want you to know... what happened to your family that day... Frank: Don't you do that. You don't talk about my family. You got that? Just don't do it. Fisk: I consider it a tragedy. Frank: That right? You can save your bullshit sympathy, 'cause I don't buy it. Fisk: I understand why you'd think that. Frank: Look, you got something to say to me or not? Fisk: Yes. I've crossed paths with your attorneys... before. Needless to say, I'm not a... a huge fan. Pushing you towards a sentence in a mental health facility, after everything you've been through, that would have been a travesty. Frank: As opposed to what? Fisk: Closure. Since I've been incarcerated, I've developed an empathy towards those who suffer by the hand of the law. Frank: I think I've heard enough of your bullshit, okay? You said closure. What'd you mean? Fisk: There's a man, here, in the big box. He's a prisoner. He's been overheard... boasting about his involvement with several criminal factions. Frank: This man... he most definitely had a hand in the massacre in the park. Fisk: I want a name. Frank: He's in another cell block... Fisk: I didn't ask you that. Frank: Which he essentially owns, heavily guarded by guards and inmates alike. Fisk: I don't give a shit. I want a name. Frank: Dutton. He's not Irish. He's not Cartel. He's not a biker. He's something else entirely. I believe that he facilitated the deal... that led to your wife and children being gunned down in broad daylight. Frank: You put me in a position to get to him... and I'll find out the truth. Fisk: Consider it done.

Dutton: What the hell? Frank: Now, you make any noise, anything at all, I'm gonna open you up like a bag. I'll watch you bleed out all over this floor. Now, you nod if you understand me. Dutton: Okay. Frank: Shh. Stanton massacre. The carousel hit. I hear you were there. Dutton: What if I was? Frank: You're a goddamn lunatic. What the hell were you doing there? Dutton: Drug deal. I was brokering between three groups of assholes who barely spoke the same language. Frank: What happened? Dutton: What do you think happened? Frank: Tell me who started the shooting. Dutton: What? Frank: You tell me who pulled the trigger. Who made the order? Dutton: It went south. Frank: What do you mean, "It went south"? It happens. Dutton: What does that mean, "It went south"? What do you mean? Frank: It means we're not as dumb as they thought we were. We realized what it was. Dutton: What was it? Frank: It wasn't a massacre, asshole. It was a sting. Dutton: A what? Frank: My source warned me. The feds infiltrated one of the gangs. I'm not sure which. They found out how big the deal was. Massive exchange. A real game changer. But they weren't after any of us. They were after the man in charge, the man who organized the whole damn thing. Dutton: Who's that? Who is that? I want a name. Frank: I never met him. He never showed his face. All I know is he had a line on pure heroin. Shit shipped from the Middle East. They called him the Blacksmith. Dutton: The whole thing should've went by the numbers, but he got wise. He stayed away. And when they realized he wasn't gonna show, someone started shooting. That's all I know. I swear... to God. Frank: I heard about you. News travels fast around here. But there were almost 100 bangers that day, and every finger found a trigger. You know, this crusade of yours... it's never gonna end, right? Right? Dutton: Yeah... yeah, you're right. You're right. Frank: Open the door. Open the door. Dutton: What are you doing? Frank: Open the goddamn door. Frank: Hey. Hey. Mr. Castle... thank you. I couldn't have done it without you. Inmates: They got Dutton! Holy shit, man! There he is. There he is. You're a dead man. Let's go! Let's go! Let's go! Come on. You're dead! Guard: Inmate! Fall on your knees!

Elektra: Open up! Not strong enough. Hai. Mmm. Security: We found two guards unconscious in the Roxxon garage. Nobu: What were they protecting? Security: Stan Gibson, sir. Nobu: Find him. The process is almost complete. Daredevil: Tell your man to stand down. Don't shoot. Lower the gun. Lower the gun! Gibson: There are more men outside. Daredevil: Not conscious ones. Tell me about the Farm. What are you growing here? Nobu: I am not afraid to hurt you. Daredevil: I know you're not. But you are not the only devil who will walk these streets. Nobu: What's in the basement? Daredevil: The rising is coming. You are but one man, akuma-san. You cannot stop what we have started. Daredevil: What is that? Nobu: That's blood.

Brett: Christ almighty. Brett: What the hell happened here? Captive: Please. Captive: They need medical attention. Please. Please. Brett: Thompson, help them. Thompson: Got it. Captive: Daniel, look at me. Brett: Jesus Christ. Brett: Don't let any of 'em out your sight, okay? Thompson: Yeah, yeah. Thompson: Okay, guys, come over here. Um, I wanna make sure we cordon off— Brett: ETA on the ambulances. Dispatcher: They're two out, sir. Brett: I need five of 'em to 54 St. Mark's, right away. Daredevil: Mahoney. Brett: Let me guess. You're the one who found 'em. Daredevil: The cages, the medical tubing. They were being drained. Brett: For what? Daredevil: Doesn't matter. We need to find the people who did this to them. It would be a good start if you told me who that was. You see anyone down there? Brett: No. Daredevil: But you could start with the Yakuza. Brett: "Start with"? Daredevil: Yeah. Brett: Shit! You saying the Yakuza is mixed up with another group? Daredevil: I think so. Brett: That's scarier than all this cult-looking ritual shit put together. This group— they got a name? Daredevil: I'm working on it. Brett: Yeah, I'll bet you are. Listen, these victims, they need to be taken somewhere off the grid, somewhere they can't be found. Daredevil: No. What they need is medical attention. Brett: I know, and they'll get it, but— Whatever was being done to them, it may not be over. We need to get them somewhere safe. Daredevil: Yeah, that might not be a bad idea. All Saints is closest... Brett: No, take them to Metro-General. I know someone there we can trust. But no one can know you're bringing them in. Daredevil: I'm on it. And just know, someday I'ma tell you how to do your job. Brett: Thompson, I need a favor.

Claire: Got the last one. And he's burning up. I need a cooling blanket and ice packs. Nurse: We're out. Claire: Jesus. Uh— Vending machine. Next floor down. Get all the cold sodas you can. Nurse: Okay. Claire: Apply them on their wrists. We need to get the fever down. Brett: Thanks for this. Claire: Thank administration. They've taken six months to remodel this wing. Anything happens, you let me know. I'll keep a few PD here, and more downstairs. Brett: Okay. Claire: And do me a favor? Keep the details of this arrangement to yourself. Brett: Details? Claire: Our mutual friend. Brett: I have no idea what you're talking about. Claire: This ain't like any overdose I've ever seen. Nurse: Yeah, their systems are in free fall. Claire: Holy shit. Nurse: What? Claire: She's got no prints. Her fingertips were burnt off. Claire: Her, too. Nurse: IDing 'em is gonna be fun. Claire: What kind of junkies do this? Nurse: Yeah, I think this was done to them. Let's just get them stable. One headache at a time. Claire: You. And here I was hoping my day would get worse. Matt: Hi, Claire. Claire: Five patients, non-responsive, high fever, no fingerprints. You wanna tell me what kind of shit storm you just rained down on me? Matt: It's why I'm here. Claire: In here. Matt: What's the story? Claire: It's, um— it's complicated. Matt: Always is with you. Claire: Remember the last time you patched me up? Matt: When you were cut to shreds? Claire: Kinda hard to forget. Well, the same guy who did that to me, he's the one responsible for your five new patients. Nobu. Matt: You said he burned to death. Claire: Yeah. I was wrong. Matt: There's gotta be more to the story than that. Claire: For now I need you to know that every one of these people is still in real danger. Matt: Okay, I have checked their vitals. Claire: I know, they're hanging by a thread. Matt: No. Claire, I mean— even if you manage to save their lives, someone may still come to kill them. And the people who gave them aid? Claire: Most likely. Matt: Yes. Claire: Wow, Matt. I— I really have not missed you at all. Matt: But, look, Claire, nobody knows they're here. And I'm gonna offer you all the protection I can. Plus, you can still send them away. Claire: You know I can't do that. Matt: Thank you. It's why I came to you. Claire: Are you hurt? Matt: Yeah— a little. Claire: "A little"? Oh. Claire: That's— Bone bruise. A fractured rib, most likely. It's probably busted, knowing you. I'll say this about you, Matt Murdock. You are a lot of bad things. Boring is not one of them. Claire: Here. Matt: What is it? Claire: Two aspirin. Catholic morphine. Take it. Matt: I don't know. Dispatcher: All units, suspect Frank Castle. Believed to be armed and extremely dangerous. Brett: I should've known this day would get worse. I want this out across all five boroughs. And get some additional units to the courthouse and City Hall. Do it. Move! Matt: Son of a bitch. Claire: What is it? Matt: The Punisher. He just escaped.

Woman: Miss Page? Karen: Yeah. Agent Gallagher: Agent Gallagher. Follow me. I'll get you through security as quickly as possible. Karen: Thank you. Agent Gallagher: Excuse us. Excuse me. Pardon me. Karen: Sorry. Agent Gallagher: Wait here. Karen: Hey. Foggy: Guess I'm not the only one that got Reyes's invitation. Karen: Security is nuts. Foggy: Frank Castle's on the loose. I wouldn't take any chances either. Karen: No, not even Frank could have orchestrated an escape that quickly. How's that even possible? Foggy: Guessing that's what the District Attorney wants to ask us. Karen: This case just keeps serving up the shit burgers. Agent: Mr. Nelson, this way. Foggy: See you on the other side. Karen: Yeah. Man: Excuse me, sir. Do you need a hand? Matt: No, thank you. Thank you so much. Karen: I, uh, see Reyes dragged you in, too. Matt: Karen? Are you all right? Karen: Other than being hauled in as a suspect in the escape of a confessed murderer? Yeah, I'm great. Matt: Yeah, this whole case has been a disaster. I'm sorry I pulled you guys into it. Karen: Don't be sorry. Matt: How are you otherwise? Karen: Good. Yeah, I'm good. Matt: Good. Agent Gallagher: Miss Page? Karen: Come with me. Agent Gallagher: Yeah. Matt: Mr. Murdock, I'll be right back. Foggy: According to my buddy, Reyes is most likely about to grill us like fish. Karen: She has no cause. Matt: On paper, we're still Frank Castle's attorneys. Foggy: And I am so proud of that. Frank's out, but instead of going after him herself, Reyes is dragging us into the lion's den. What could we possibly know about his escape? Matt: Precisely dick. But if Reyes can find a way to blame us for all this, she will. Foggy: Karen, you spent the most time with him. He say anything? Anything at all that could help us right now? Nobu: Hey. Nobu: Is he close? Hirochi: Perhaps. It does not matter. We will continue until he breaks. Stick: Only thing gonna crack tonight is your skull— asshole! Daredevil: You okay? Ellison: Karen Page, what the hell are you still doing here? It's Christmas Eve. Shouldn't you be home celebrating with all that family that you can't stand, like everybody else? Oh, no, I'm sorry. Ellison: Happy Hanukkah. Karen: Scotch. Ellison: Mmm, you know, just— just in case. I'll expect 2,000 words in my inbox before Santa shows up. Karen: You got it, boss. Karen: Okay. Karen: "What is it, to be a hero? Look in the mirror and you'll know. Look into your own eyes and tell me you are not heroic... that you have not endured, or suffered or lost the things you care about most. Matt: I have something that I need you to see. Matt: I'm Daredevil.

Melvin: Yeah, I don't know about this. I made all this stuff to keep Betsy safe, not just give it away. Elektra: You'll get it back, Melvin. Without a scratch. Promise. Melvin: If you say so. Brett: So this is what it's come to, huh? The masked vigilante is the only one I can trust. Daredevil: What happened? Brett: I knew it was just a matter of time till you showed up again. Elektra: This is insane. Daredevil: Probably. Elektra: We're about to walk into a building full of highly trained assassins. Daredevil: I know. Elektra: And your plan is to what? Nobu: Impressive. But futile. Daredevil: Where are they? The people on your list. Nobu: Safe. For now. But that can change. Elektra: We're not letting you leave here alive. Nobu: You assume I came here to leave. Daredevil: What do you want? Nobu: Her. The Black Sky. You may have her heart, but we have her destiny. Elektra: My destiny is my own. Nobu: We shall see.

Elektra: Okay. Even if we survive— we may not see each other again. Daredevil: Wait, wait. Wait for one second. One second. So, what if— What if from now on, if— if we make it— wherever you run, I— I run with you? Elektra: You're not serious. Daredevil: I've never been more serious. Matt: This, Elektra, this is a part of me that I need. And you're the only one who gets it. Without this, I'm not alive. I'm not. Not really. And I know that now, thanks to you. I don't know what we are together, and if we have any chance in the future I don't... But I— I do know that I'm free with you. Like with no one else. Elektra: You hide from yourself. You don't let anyone in. Matt: You. I let you in. Think about it. What if this isn't the end? What if it's just the beginning? Elektra: No. They'll find us. Matt: No, we'll keep moving. We'll change identities. We'll, we'll hide. They'll never catch us. What do you say? Elektra: Uh, I say let's go to London. Yeah? Madrid. Tunisia. There are sexy places to hide. Matt: Hey, I've never been further north than 116th Street, so... Elektra: Because you love New York. Matt: And I'd give my life for it, but there's one thing in this world that makes me feel more alive. And that's you. Elektra: I'm the Black Sky, Matthew. Matt: Yeah, and I'm the Devil of Hell's Kitchen. Matt: The airport's just a cab fare away. All we gotta do is survive whatever's waiting for us behind that door. Elektra: Let's get out of here. Daredevil: Remember— they're trying to kill me, not you. Elektra: Over my dead body.
Matt: Father Lantom. Clinton Church.

Matt: How was the walk? Karen: I just needed some space. It's a lot... Matt: No, of course. I get it. Please, come in. Karen: Thank you. Karen: Can you see me? Matt: No. No, not "see" exactly. It's different. It's, um... I think it's better. Karen: "Different" how? "Better" how? Matt: Well, I can sense things about you. Karen: Okay. Like what? Matt: Oh, God. It's really hard to explain. Um... Try me. Karen: I know that you stopped on the way over here. At our favorite Indian place. Probably it was a trip down memory lane, 'cause you didn't eat but you did order a drink. See, I can smell the curry on your clothes, and I can... taste the Jameson's off your lips. I know that just telling you all that makes you uncomfortable... 'cause I can hear your heartbeat. Karen: This is humiliating. Matt: Karen, I should've told you. You have every right to be angry... Karen: Yeah. I should be. I should be really angry at you. But I watched you fight for me. Twice, actually. You know I dreamed about that? I played it over in my mind again and again, and I keep... How can I be this mad at someone who saved my life? Matt: Because he's your friend and you care for him and he broke your trust. Karen: Yeah, well, stop agreeing with me. It's making it worse. Matt: Can I get you a drink? Karen: And he knows I nodded. Karen: So, the whole cane thing, it's just... an act? Matt: Yep. Karen: Sorry. Why? Matt: Why didn't you trust me? What, did you think I would judge you? Karen: No. Matt: I didn't judge Frank. Why would I judge you? Karen: Well, maybe you should judge Frank. Castle's a killer. I'm not. Matt: You don't always know what motivates people. Karen: Uh, yeah, but I know when they lie to me. Their heartbeats tell me. Matt: Here's what I know. I will never lie to you again. That's a promise. All right? Ask me anything. Karen: Where do you keep it? Matt: In the closet. In the chest. Karen: Holy shit. Karen: What... what happens now? Matt: It's over. That's it. I'm gonna leave Daredevil behind. Karen: Really? You can just do that? Matt: Yeah. Karen: You know... you and Foggy had me almost convinced it was alcohol. It makes a lot of sense. You know, the secrecy, abandoning social and professional commitments. It... It certainly sounds like an addict. Matt: Well, it's not like that. Karen: Help me out, then, because I'm not you. I can't tell if you're lying to me or not. Matt: I don't need him to be a part of me anymore. And I don't want him to be. I want to believe you. Karen: I'm not so sure Daredevil is the problem. Matt: Ouch. Karen: Shit. Foggy: Karen? Hey, Karen, you here? Karen: Hey. You okay? Foggy: Hey. Yeah. Yeah, yeah, fine. Thanks for coming. Karen: Did the building manager let you in? Foggy: Um... I thought you said you were packing the place up. Karen: Yeah. Uh... Remember how I told you I was gonna talk to Matt's landlord about letting his place go? Foggy: Uh-huh. Karen: Surprise. Foggy: What, so when you asked me to help you move boxes... Karen: Uh, yeah, I lied. I mean, technically it was more of, like, a ruse. Foggy: Gotcha. You rused. Karen: Hmm. Foggy: Journalism has changed you, Page. Karen: So what am I doing here? Foggy: Oh! Uh... Right. Yeah. So... Wait! Are you living here? Karen: Oh! No. God, no. I'm just paying the bills, or some of them, until Matt gets back, but, um... Matt's being evicted. Foggy: Yeah, I need you to help me convince his landlord to give me an extension. Karen: Karen... Foggy: No, just, carrying two rents... I'm behind this month. That's all. Foggy: As much as it hurts me to say this, you're a reporter. Look at the facts. A building fell on Matt. A big one. And nobody's heard from him since. Matt's dead. Karen: That's the first time I've said that out loud. Foggy: I don't want to accept it, either. Especially since I'm the one who... you know... Karen: No. Foggy: ...brought him the Devil suit. Karen: Hey, don't... do that to yourself. Foggy: It doesn't even matter. Look, Matt wouldn't want you burning through cash, trying to hang on to his stuff. He's my best friend. He was my best friend. I know him. I knew him. He would want you to move on with your life. Karen: I... I can't. Foggy: Then it's time to come to terms.

Maggie: I've been a nun for 30 years. I know self-pity when I hear it. Matt: Okay, good. Maggie: Your father was famous around here. I saw him fight. I saw him go down many times. But he never stayed down.

Matt: Oh. Maggie: What in God's name have... Matt: Feel that? Maggie: Feel what? Matt: Three subway lines run beneath us. At any given time, there are six different trains vibrating the ground. That was the E train. Maggie: Was it now? Matt: You brought food. Maggie: I did. I brought you some... Matt: Beef ravioli from Nonna's. Nice. Maggie: Now you're just showing off. Maggie: He wants to know that he's still got it. Lantom: I am not comfortable with that idea. Maggie: Now you're uncomfortable? Heal the body, and the spirit will follow. Lantom: It's the other way around. Maggie: He needs this. It's the only damn thing that's gotten him out of bed. So please just do it. Matt: Thanks for making this happen. Lantom: Hands should be used for God's work. Matt: Yeah? That's why he made me this way? Lantom: No. That's why he made boxing. Matt: Gloves? Maggie: Helmet first. Matt: No, I can't. It'll throw me off. Maggie: Don't be an idiot. Matt: Sister, listen to me. For this to work, I have to feel and hear everything. Lantom: Now, remember the deal. Keep your mouth shut. Edmund: Beats the Hail Marys. Edmund: You want me to hit a blind guy? Matt: All right. Lantom: Cut! Time! You good? Matt: Yeah, I'm good. Edmund: Damn. He hits hard. Lantom: It's really something. To see it with my own eyes. Matt: No. Something feels off. It feels like I'm underwater. Lantom: Maybe we should stop. Matt: No, no, no. Ding-ding. Let's go again. Lantom: Matthew? Matthew! Maggie: You should see the other guy. For what it's worth... you were incredible. Matt: Thank you. Maggie: Sister, I... Matt: Did your head spin around? Maggie: Then wear it for me. Matt: You've been very kind to me. Maggie: I have, haven't I? Matt: And patient. Very, very patient. Maggie: Don't tell anyone. They'll think I've gone soft. Matt: No. I don't think there's any danger of that. Maggie: Let me look at you. Matt: I used to sew up my dad. Maggie: And your stitches are perfect. Well, there's plenty of practice around here. Matt: Everything okay? Maggie: Yeah. It's fine. I just have to get back upstairs. Maggie: I don't suppose there's any hope you'd come to Mass with me? Matt: Maybe next time. Maggie: I'll hold you to that.

Woman: Hey! Hey, get off of him! Hey! What are you doing? Dad! Woman: Help! Get off! Help! Oh, my God! Dad! Dad... Woman: Stay with me. We'll get you to the hospital. Come on! Man 1: Hey, asshole, this was none of your business. Come on. Man 2: We should kill this son of a bitch. Man 1: Nah, man. Leave him. Matt: Hold on. God forgive me. Man 1: Leave him. Let's get out of here.

location: FBI AGENT RAY NADEEM'S HOUSE - PARTY
scene_text: Ray'S Son: We seriously out of turkey? Ray: You didn't swing by the deli? Seema: I did, actually. I ran into a little payment snafu at the register. I wanted to make it through the party before I brought it up. Ray: Huh. Uh, which card did you use? Seema: The red Visa, right? Ray: Yeah, of course. Yeah. Seema: Huh. Ray'S Son: Hey, Dad. Ray: Hey! There's the birthday goon! Masi Savina wanted to know if you're ruining dinner. Ray'S Son: Excuse me? Ray: Is she trying to undermine my culinary talents again? Get over here. Let me show you how a master chef does his thing. Check this out. See what I'm doing here, Sami? This is a technique called "skimming." High degree of difficulty. Ta-da! Ray: Wanna do the honors? Sami: Yes. Seema: Are you positive you used the red Visa? Ray: I paid that one last week. That one should be good. Seema: I tried the red Visa, the blue Visa, the silver Mastercard... I even tried my library card. Ray: It's okay. Nothing we haven't handled before. Seema: Hmm. Nihar: If I could have the floor for a minute? If you haven't heard by now, despite Nihar shouting it from the rooftops... Nihar: ...my courageous sister-in-law is now 100% cancer-free. Nihar: We know that it hasn't been easy for you, with all the obstacles you've faced. Being denied insurance over and over again. Those asshole institutions running you over like a tank. Nihar: Anyway... tonight, we celebrate. This one's for you, Saanvi. Cheers. Cheers. Ray: We couldn't have done it without you, brother. Nihar: No, please don't. I'm serious, Ray. You two did the work. I just wrote a few checks. Ray: What are you doing out here, bug? Everyone's eaten. We're waiting to light the candles. Sami: I don't think I want any. Ray: No cake? He doesn't want any cake. There must be something seriously wrong with him. No, seriously, bug. What's up? Sami: I don't know why we had to have our family party today. I told you, Ricky Thomas is having friends over. I could be at his house, glow bowling in his basement right now. Ray: The Thomases have a bowling alley in their basement? Sami: Let me tell you something. Come the summer, you're the one who's gonna be throwing mad parties, because the pool is definitely happening this year. Ray: Really? Sami: You bet. I'm gonna be tossing your butt off the diving board by June. Now, what do you say we go inside, throw back some cake? Ray: Okay. Sami: Yeah? Seema: The pool, huh? Ray: No, don't. Seema: Listen, Nadia said one of her literacy tutors quit last week. Maybe I could pick up some evening hours at the center... Ray: Not another job. We've been down this road before. Seema: I know, Ray, but I can't see another way out. Ray: I'll fix this. I'll fix everything.

Hattley: I've got a nine o'clock with Salazar, so unless you got something quick... Ray: Salazar just got called downtown. Hattley: Well, make yourself at home. Ray: Thanks. Ray: My performance review. That's not until the end of the month, correct? I'd like it moved up. I'd like to do it now. Hattley: That's a tall order, Ray. Performance review isn't the kind of thing we shuffle around. Ray: Then how come mine's been deferred twice now? You're denying me the advancement opportunities that I have rightfully earned. No, not the Bureau. You. Now, why you'd do something like that to me, I don't have a clue. But maybe it's time I file a complaint with the EEO. Hattley: You're right. Your reviews have been deferred for reasons having nothing to do with scheduling or restructuring or whatever bullshit I fed you at the time. It's because I'm trying to protect you. Ray: Protect me? Hattley: Do you have any idea what your FICO score is? 640. Your FICO score is 640. Ray: So it's not stellar. You know, I... Hattley: You're buried in debt, and that makes you a recruitment target. It's Bureau policy not to promote someone with that level of vulnerability. Ray: My circumstances were exceptional, and you know that. My sister-in-law was sick and I... Hattley: I am sorry for that. Ray: Three and a half years. I haven't had a pay bump in three and a half years. Hattley: I know it's wrong. I know. You're a fine agent. But I can't make this happen for you. Not until you fix your finances. But look... while I got you here... your number's up. Ray: Nice. Nice timing. Hattley: It's a shit errand. I get it. We talk to this guy every month, and every month he gives us nothing. It's a nice drive, though.

Ray: Mr. Fisk, I'm Special Agent Ray Nadeem with the Federal Bureau of Investigation. The FBI would like your assistance with... Ray: Let's cut to the part where you tell me to eat shit, so we can stop wasting each other's time, huh? Fisk: Tell me, Special Agent Nadeem... do you have anyone in your life who you love so much, you'd do anything to protect them? Ray: Are you threatening me? Fisk: I have made many mistakes. But I accept the debt I'm paying because of them. But what I will not accept... is that the woman that I love should have to pay for them, too. I would do anything to protect her. Anything. Ray: I'm sorry. What is it you're saying? Fisk: I want to make a deal.

Maggie: ...bright idea to bring him in? Lantom: He's one of ours, Maggie. What other choice did I have? Maggie: Metro-General maybe? Call 911. Lantom: He's a vigilante. If he goes to a hospital, the police will arrest him. Maggie: This is Sister Maggie Grace at St. Agnes Orphanage... Lantom: It's Matthew. Jack Murdock's son. Maggie: I'm very sorry. I made a mistake. Get wire cutters. We need to get him out of this suit. Go to the kitchen and bring... we have. Lantom: How can I help? Maggie: You've done enough.
Matt: Where did you go, Elektra? We're gonna die here. Elektra: This is what living feels like.

Nun: Get Maggie. Tell her he's awake. Matt: Elektra... Nun: How do you feel? Maggie: Don't try to stand up. Matt: Where... where... Maggie: St. Agnes. The orphanage. Matt: How long? How long? Maggie: Lay down. Several weeks. Matt: Where is she? Maggie: Who? Matt: Elektra. I... Maggie: I don't know who that is. Maggie: Stay in the bed. You'll hurt yourself. Matt: My right ear... I can't... Maggie: Just stop this right now! Maggie: Damn it, Matthew! Matt: Now I can't see. I can't see.
Young Matt: I can't see! I can't see! I can't see!

Lantom: Matthew? Matt: Father. I didn't know you were there. Lantom: Must feel strange to be back here. The place where you grew up. Matt: I haven't thanked you yet, Father. Lantom: Figured we could count on the nuns for their discretion. The nuns know who you are, but Sister Maggie swore them to secrecy. After she swore at me. Lantom: If you want to take Communion... we could, uh... Or we could just talk. Matt: Elektra... was with me when the building collapsed. Lantom: Matthew, Elektra passed months ago. We had a funeral for her. Matt: No, shh... I remember. I know it sounds crazy. I'm telling you, she was there. I was... holding on to her when... Lantom: In any case, the building was surrounded when it collapsed. Nobody else was seen getting out. I am so sorry, Matthew. Lantom: How about I take your confession and we go ahead with the Eucharist? Matt: Not today, Father. Lantom: Mystical thinking is not my bag, Matthew. Hell, I'm probably the most rational crank in the whole diocese, but even I have to admit... it is a miracle you survived. Matt: Our conversations, they usually go this way. I come to you with questions. You tell me what you understand about God. Lantom: Nature of the gig, I guess. Matt: Give it a rest, shall we? Lantom: Sure. I'll be around. I'll, uh... When you're ready to talk... we'll talk.

Orphan: Is he dead? Matt: Boo. Orphan: Who are you? Matt: Same as you. I grew up here. Orphan: Damn! What happened to you? Matt: Life. Maggie: This room is off limits. And if you're well enough to be up, you're well enough to be in class. Both: Sorry, Sister. Maggie: Hello again, Matthew. Matt: They're scared of you, huh? Maggie: So were you when you were their age. I need to change your gauze. Preferably without you flailing around like an idiot. Matt: I guess I shouldn't be surprised by any of this. You were always pissed off. Maggie: Of course, back then, you were just a boy who lost his eyesight. And now, you're the Devil of Hell's Kitchen. Matt: You've heard of me. Maggie: I live in an orphanage, not under a rock. I just never imagined it'd be one of ours running around in that Halloween costume. The things I've heard you can do... You are blind, right? You weren't just faking it the whole time? Matt: Congratulations. You finally caught me. Maggie: It's not a fair question? Matt: Yeah, the accident blinded me. It just also, uh, sharpened my other senses. Maggie: Not to worry, Sister. Those days are behind me. I'm deaf in my right ear, and I can't even walk to the bathroom now. Matt: Yeah, well, you're pretty banged up. Your spine, your hip. Well, the days of doing backflips might be over, but... you'll get back on your feet. Maggie: Now that you're out of the woods... Matt: You want me to go. Maggie: It's not a convalescent home. Matt: I understand. Maggie: I'm sorry. Matt: I'll figure something out. Maggie: There must be at least one person I can call for you. Matt: No. There's no one. Karen: Yeah. No, I filed that story already. Yeah! No, look... Oh, that. No. Uh, part five still needs a quote. I put out a few lines. We'll get a bite soon. Yeah, okay. Yeah, I'll have it for you by the end of the day. All right. Yeah. Bye. Karen: Shit.
Karen: What am I doing here, Matt? Matt: I have something that I need you to see. Matt: I'm Daredevil.

Agent 1: FBI! Agent 2: FBI! Get on the floor! Agent 3: Get out of the bed! Agent 4: FBI! Don't move! Ray: Freeze! Agent 5: Where are you going? Ray: Off the bed! Hands up! Show me your hands! Cuff him! Agent 6: Hey. Give me your hands. Man: Take off these cuffs. I have the right to an attorney. You have no right here. Do you understand? You have no right. Agent 7: You got Mother Teresa. Agent 8: You actually bagged that asshole. Got his number one and number two also. And two judges, district police cap... A freakin' deputy mayor. This is gonna be a messy day for City Hall. Ray: Yeah. The Albanians had to be buying those guys off with more than tail. Burgos got their computers, so we're gonna find their money. Once we start tracking it, who knows how far this goes? Thank you, Wilson Fisk. He's a gift that's gonna keep on giving.
Ray: This deal will save lives because of Wilson Fisk. Now I need a shower. If we keep him talking, Fisk will give up others. This deal will save lives. Agent: Tell me you're not going for this.

Kids: Uncle Foggy! Foggy: Okay, easy, easy. Left pocket. Left pocket. You're gonna save them for after dinner, right? Foggy: Don't tell your mother! Or my mother. Woman: Hey! Foggy's here! All: Hey! Foggy! Theo: Hey there, Counselor. "How are your briefs holding up?" Foggy: What's up? Christ, that joke gets old. Theo: Gets old? Rosalind: Listen, Franklin, there's something I need to talk to you about. Foggy: Hi. Rosalind: Try a little. I put cinnamon in it. Foggy: Mmm! Delicious. So good. Rosalind: Is he worse? Foggy: Your father's arthritis gets a little worse every day. He's having trouble holding onto things, especially when he's tired. I see him with the saws and slicers. Rosalind: Ma, I'm sorry. Isn't there anything they can do for it? Foggy: There's no cure for getting old, Franklin. Your father needs to be on a beach, not slinging meat in Hell's Kitchen. Forty years is enough already. Rosalind: I know. You got yourself a life. A good life. But maybe it's time you came home. Foggy: I'm right here when you need me. Rosalind: Your brother loves this place, but Theo can't do it alone. Come help. Put those brains to work for your family, not every uptown shithead that comes into your office. Foggy: They're not all shitheads, Ma. Rosalind: I'm not telling you what to do. You're a grown man. Just think about it. That's all I'm sayin'. Foggy: Okay. I will. I promise. Rosalind: Good. I love you, kid. Rosalind: Hey! I can smell the candy from here, Ruthie! Come here.
