Where'd you get that? Where'd you get that? Where'd you get that? Foggy: Hey, Pop. Edward: Hey! Foggy: Do you want a glass? Edward: Damn sure didn't come to chat. Edward: The suits I understand, Foggy, but... why you drink this expensive crap is beyond me. Edward: You know how proud of you I am, Foggy? You're a big deal. Foggy: Which is what you always wanted. Edward: Did I? Edward: Ever since you could talk, you went around telling people that you owned the store. They'd play along with it, too. Remember? Foggy: Yeah. Edward: I got it, Pops. I got it. Edward: Yeah. Sláinte.
Guard: Your lawyer almost screwed up the whole deal. Fisk: Those terms guarantee my safety. Guard: Beyoncé has fewer demands. Guard: This way, convict.

Clerk: You want service, you gotta get in line. Clerk: Oh... Oh. Come on, come on. You got a ticket, you just picking up? Matt: Me? Clerk: Yeah. Matt: Oh, no, I just ran in 'cause your clothes smell so good. See, I got this real sensitive nose. I thought... Clerk: Yeah, we use a totally organic process, latest stuff. Matt: Oh, cool. You got a flyer? Clerk: Not in Braille. Matt: I... I got seeing friends. Clerk: Here, have a coupon. Matt: Thanks, I appreciate it. Glad I found you. Really makes my day. Clerk: All right. Man: God damn it. We must have blown a fuse. Thug: Hello! You! Matt: Yeah, I'd like to report an assault. I didn't see what happened, but there are a lot of guns here. Maybe some kind of robbery.

Foggy: I don't think I ever said it, but thank you, Theo, for taking over the shop. Theo: They wanted it to be you. Foggy: Yeah. For a long time, I kinda wanted it to be you, too. Theo: You never said anything. Foggy: What was there to say? You got a head for other things. You were always getting the prizes and scholarships and shit. Anyway, you can't make a sandwich to save your ass. Theo: Theo, if we need to figure out... Foggy: Knock it off. Go do what you're good at. You're livin' the dream. Theo: Am I? Foggy: You're shittin' me. Theo: I had this idea of how things were gonna go. Matt and I talked a lot about what we'd do. Open our own firm. Help people. Get rich. I was the get rich part. He was the help people part. When he was around, I knew who I was. Now... Theo: Matt was a good guy. Foggy: Sláinte. Theo: You can always come back here. Foggy: Yeah, great. Thanks. Karen: Hi. Sorry, I... Foggy: Perfect timing. Now everyone can stop worrying about my career choices and start worrying about me cheating on Marci. Much better. Karen: Can I to talk to you? Foggy: What's wrong? Karen: I think Matt's alive. Foggy: So the guy in the mask, he wasn't in a, you know, devil suit? Karen: No, but he was wearing a black mask. Foggy: So it could be anybody. Karen: It could also not be anybody. Hell's Kitchen is ground zero for vigilantes these days. Foggy: Believe me, I want it to be Matt, too. But he's... gone. Karen: No, no. Foggy: We need to get past that. Karen: There is no proof of that. And until there is... Foggy: You know how I know he's gone? Because if it was Matt, if he was really still alive, he would've reached out to us. You know how I know that you don't really believe that? You keep saying "gone" instead of "dead." Now, don't you want to take a minute and just be absolutely sure that's not your best friend out there somewhere? Karen: I wish it was my best friend. But it's not. He's dead. Foggy: Karen, come on. Stay. Theo: What? Foggy: You.

Neda: Your father... he's in a coma. Matt: He's alive. Neda: Why did you help us? Matt: The men who did this are in police custody for another crime. You head down to the 15th Precinct right now, you can identify them. Neda: You caught them? Matt: You should go. Neda: Thank God for you. Matt: He didn't help you. I did.

location: FBI TRANSPORT - EN ROUTE TO SAFE HOUSE
scene_text: Ray: You will be under the strict supervision of my team. You will not remove your ankle monitor. You will not pass beyond the boundaries shown to you. You will continue to have a strictly regulated schedule. That means eating, sleeping, shitting, whenever I say. Do you understand, Mr. Fisk? Fisk: I've spent much of my life alone. And for many years, I pretended that this was the source of my strength. I told myself I had free will. And in that time, I achieved a great deal. But I was not fulfilled. I was longing for a connection that I could imagine but I could not achieve. Searching and not finding. Until Vanessa. Until I discovered love. I thought I would explode with the sense of power and freedom that she brought me. That the world lay at my feet. But then that passed when I discovered the great lie at the heart of love. That what I took for true freedom was precisely the reverse. Fisk: You can build a prison of stone and steel, but you merely present the prisoner with a challenge. Fisk: Any truly determined man will find a way out. But love... Love is the perfect prison. Inescapable. So you see, Agent Nadeem... I am always in prison, wherever I go. And if these things help me protect Vanessa, then they are nothing to me. I will do whatever I must. Ray: Go left! Left! Agent: Nadeem! Nadeem! Agent: Prepare to fire! Agent 2: Grenade! Ray: Stay in the car! Man 2: Don't shoot! Don't shoot! We surrender! Dex: Convict. Don't move.

Paramedic 1: Put him in bay 4. Paramedic 2: Excuse me, sir. Paramedic 1: Sorry. Paramedic 3: Multiple GSWs. Paramedic 4: First one up... Agent 1: Goddamn Albanians killed everyone except Fisk. Agent 2: Somebody said he's en route to the safe house. Karen: It's a damn shitshow. The FBI just let Wilson Fisk out of prison.

Prisoner: Snitch! Fisk: No! No, don't! Fisk: No! No! No! No! Guard: All tier two COs, we have a 10-10 in progress in the weight room. All tier two COs, we have a fight in the weight room. Guard 1: Guard! Guard! Guard! Guard 2: You, up against the wall, right now! Against the wall!

Maggie: What did you do, Matthew? Where did you go last night? Matt: Hey. Don't pull that crap with me. Maggie: What happened? Matt: Go away. Maggie: I put in way too much work on you to quit now. Up. Move your ass. Maggie: So you get beat by a guy who wasn't even trying to hurt you, and your brilliant next move is to go out and pick another fight? Here. Take these. Maggie: A word of advice, Mr. Daredevil... give yourself time to heal, or you're gonna get yourself killed. Matt: You're probably right. Maggie: Is that what you wanted? I have a special gift, too. I'm impervious to bad attitude. So you can throw your self-pitying bullshit at me all day, Murdock, and I'll still be standing right here. Pissed off, maybe, but right here. You're gonna talk to me. Matt: Why did you become a nun? Maggie: I heard God's call. Matt: So you feel like being a nun is what you're meant to be? Maggie: Yes. Very much. Matt: What if you couldn't be one anymore? If it were taken from you? Maggie: Your point being that if we can't fulfill our calling, we might be better off as worm food? Matt: Answer the question. Maggie: I'll tell you what I wouldn't do. I wouldn't lose faith. I'd find some other purpose. If you can be anything else, it was never really your calling. Matt: Just tell me, honestly. If you could no longer be a nun, wouldn't you grieve? Maggie: Of course I would. Matt: Then please... go away. Maggie: I understand what it's like to feel lost, Matthew. It happened to me, too, once. A long time ago, when I was still a novitiate... I left the order for a while. Matt: Why? Maggie: I was considering a very different life. It was wonderful and terrifying. I struggled to know which life God wanted me to choose. I prayed. I looked for signs. In the end, I just had to do my best to figure it out. Matt: Well, there you go. That is the difference between us. I no longer care what God wants. Maggie: Oh, right. Almost forgot. You've seen his true face now.

location: FLASHBACK - ST. AGNES ORPHANAGE - FATHER LANTOM'S OFFICE
scene_text: Lantom: Those are some fancy moves, Matthew. Young Matt: Sister Dora turned me in, didn't she? Lantom: This has to stop. Young Matt: My Confirmation is in the spring. I'm supposed to be learning the catechism, and Sister D can't even defend original sin. Lantom: She is not a theologian. You already know more about it than she does, I'm sure. Young Matt: So I can skip catechism? Lantom: No. Come on. Sit. Lantom: How many fights have you been in this week? Young Matt: How many guys complained? Lantom: None. 'Cause no one wants to admit they got their butt kicked by a blind kid. Young Matt: So you can't prove that I did anything. Lantom: I don't want to, and I don't need to. It's not about proving anything, Matthew. Argumentation is a skill. Being argumentative is a sign. Young Matt: A sign like a prophecy? Lantom: A sign like you're angry, Matthew. That's a perfectly understandable reaction to your situation. But it's not sustainable. Young Matt: Or maybe it's a sign that Sister Dora should stick to teaching math. Lantom: You're good... at arguing and deflecting and denying you're angry to other people. But you're gonna have to deal with your anger, Matthew. Find a way to... harness it. Or it will destroy you. Young Matt: Well, if that's God's plan for me, then I guess that's how it's supposed to work out, isn't it? Lantom: You know, maybe you don't understand original sin, after all. God gave us free will, Matthew. Adam and Eve were not puppets, and neither are we. We make our own choices. That's one reason we pray, for help making good ones. You should try it sometime. Young Matt: I do pray. I pray all the time. I've been praying for years. God doesn't talk to me. Lantom: So that's what this is about? You feel God is... neglecting you? Matthew, the burning-bush business doesn't happen very often, even in the Bible. He's usually more subtle than that. You want to hear God, Matthew, you have to listen more carefully. Because he speaks in whispers.

Agent: Veggie sub. No meat. Ray: Thanks. Agent: You don't want it. Ray: Why not? Agent: When you see the way Ramsey and Arinori are kissing Hattley's ass, you're gonna lose your appetite. They're in her office right now. Ray: Doing what? Agent: Hattley gave you this raid. But now that it worked, well, somebody's got to run Fisk full time. Right?
Ramsey: There he is. Man of the hour. You see the client list yet? Holy shit. Ray: A moment, ma'am? Hattley: Sure, Ray.

Hattley: Congratulations. Pristine execution. Ray: Glad to hear it, boss. I got a big ask. Hattley: You want Fisk detail. I can't. He's my kill. I get to eat first. Ray: There's a goddamn buffet in that conference room. You can't fill up on that? Hattley: That's today. Now, what about tomorrow? Look, we play Fisk right, there's plenty for everyone for years. He can give us every criminal organization on the East Coast. Hattley: Hey, Pryor. Find out how Burgos is doing on the computers. Ray: Dozens of agents had their shot at Fisk. None of them got shit. But I did. Hattley: We got some big collars out of this, Ray. I'm gonna make sure D.C. knows about it. Ray: Why do I feel like there's a "but" coming? Hattley: Shut the door. Hattley: I put you on Fisk detail, your file is required reading. You'll be naked. There will be questions. Ray: I've got answers. Hattley: I've got a boss, too. And he's got a hard-on for agents in financial holes. Ray: I'm sorry. Hattley: No. No way. Ray: Easy, Ray. Hattley: No. You tell D.C. that none of this could have happened without the unexpected connection between me and Wilson Fisk. Because that's the truth. And then none of the other shit in my file will matter. Come on, Tammy. How am I supposed to get out from under? Hattley: Okay, he's yours. But you need to keep him talking, Ray. Ray: I got this. Hattley: He better last years. Because he goes dry, we're both burned.

Karen: Hey. Ellison: Hey. "Rostam Kazemi." Mean anything to you? Karen: Uh, yeah, he's a real estate developer. Ellison: Mmm-hmm. Karen: Actually, his daughter, Neda, is the mean one on the Heiresses of Manhattan. Not that I watch that kind of crap or anything, but... Ellison: No, of course not. Karen: Anyway, he and his daughter were attacked outside a restaurant last night. He's in a coma at Riverbank Hospital, think it might be a kidnapping attempt. Ellison: No, you know what? I think you should give TJ that story. He watches her show. He'd love it. Karen: Well, that's... That's great. That's nice. I'm giving it to you. Ellison: No, I'm in the middle of something here. Karen: Excuse me? Ellison: It's not done yet, but I'd like to stick with it if that's okay. Karen: What? Karen: Uh, yeah, here. Ellison: What am I looking at? Karen: Uh... They're reports of respiratory illnesses among residents of a particular city block. They've spiked. They're up, like, 40% from last year. Ellison: And which particular block would that be? Karen: 48th and 10th. Ellison: Midland Circle adjacent. Karen: Karen. Ellison: Come on. I know we've done a lot of pieces on this, but there are still questions about that night we don't have answers for. Karen: You think the answers are in here? Ellison: I don't know. Maybe. Just give me a couple days. It's not done yet. Karen: What is it about Midland Circle, Karen? I mean, it's not just a story, is it? Ellison: Look. The work you've done on this, reporting, the writing... it's excellent. It's great. It's some of the best you've ever done. I'm proud of it. I'm even maybe a little bit jealous. But it's done. Karen: It's not. Ellison: You've been over it, and over it and over it, and nothing new has turned up. It's done. So take the Kazemi story. Karen: I don't want it. Ellison: I'm not asking.
Fisk: Nadeem! Agent: Stay in the car! Man 1: Don't shoot! We surrender! Dex: Convict. Don't move.

Fisk: That's it. Let the Devil out. Felt good, didn't it? Too bad you still can't get at me. Not with the FBI protecting me. I'm going to kill everyone you love, and there's nothing you can do about it.

Ellison: Paper goes to bed in 10 minutes. You got 30 seconds. Karen: Okay. It's big. Ellison: Shit. Fisk. Karen: No, look... Ellison: God damn it. I explicitly told you not to do that. Karen: I didn't set out to. Ellison: Stop. Mason saw you at the hotel. I mean, I know Fisk is important to you. I know. I don't care. Okay? I assign the stories, and I gave this one to Mason. Karen: I wasn't there on that story. I was there on my story. Kazemis? Look, I think there's a connection. Ellison: What do you mean? Karen: Do you know who used to own the Presidential Hotel? Ellison: No. Karen: The Kazemis. Ellison: I don't have proof yet, but you know who I think owns it now? Karen: Wilson Fisk. Ellison: Tell me. Karen: Okay. Look, I got a lead. So the Presidential Hotel is owned by these nested shell companies. It's just one company who owns another and another... Anyway, I tracked them from here to the Caymans to Luxembourg. Ellison: And this connects to Fisk how? Karen: Because all of those companies, they're all represented here in the United States by one law firm. Donovan and Partners. Fisk's lawyers. Ellison: Okay, keep going. Karen: All right, here's what I've pieced together. Six months ago, one of these shell companies buys the Presidential Hotel from Kazemi. A week ago, he tells his family that he regrets the sale and announces his intention to buy the hotel back. And two days later, Kazemi gets attacked. Ellison: Yes. Yes, exactly. Now, I don't think that timing is coincidental. I just... I can feel Fisk is behind this. Right? I feel it in my bones. I need two days to get everything vetted, then I'll have a story that you can run. Karen: It's excellent. Outstanding work, Karen. Ellison: Thank you. Karen: Really. Ellison: Yeah. I'm giving it to Mason. I told you. Karen: What? No, I know, I'm biased. Of course! Of course I'm biased. Fisk tried to have me killed. He also killed Ben, which makes you as biased as me. If people see your name and know your connection to Fisk, it compromises this paper! Ellison: Fine. Give the byline to Mason. I don't give a shit about credit. What I give a shit about is Fisk getting out of prison. We have to do something... I have to do something about this. So don't tell me to back off, 'cause I won't. Karen: You know, it took Ben decades to become this much of a pain in my ass.

Maggie: Well, at least you're upright. Maggie: Do I even wanna know? Matt: Do you believe people can change? Maggie: I'm still holding out hope. Matt: I don't think we can. Not really. I think we come into this world who we are. And maybe we get a little nicer. Or a little angrier. But we can't change our fundamental nature. Maggie: Well, you'd actually have to try to know. Matt: I was talking about Wilson Fisk. Maggie: So your hearing's really back, then? Well, what do you know? Maybe the boss did hear my prayers. Matt: Yeah, or my curses. Maggie: Please don't start with Job again. Matt: You gotta admit it's interesting, though, isn't it? I finally get my full hearing back, and the first thing I hear is that Wilson Fisk is out of prison. Maggie: So you're suggesting that God set a dangerous mobster free just to spite you? Matt: Nah. Probably just a coincidence. Maggie: Because that would be incredibly narcissistic. Matt: Fisk claims to be helping the FBI. But they don't know him like I do. Maggie: Right. And according to you, people can't change. Matt: 'Cause he's claiming to have changed over a woman. Maggie: I see. Well, if there's anything that can redeem a lost soul, love would have to top the list. Matt: Oh, come on. Even a monster like Fisk? Maggie: You're talking to a nun, kiddo. Love and redemption are pretty much our sales pitch. Matt: Yeah. Well, I'm not buying. Maggie: So, what are you gonna do? Matt: I don't know. Maybe I'll stop him. For good this time. Maggie: Well, just be careful that you don't become the monster. Matt: Foggy. Foggy: This isn't real. Matt: It's real. Foggy: Hey, Foggy. How? Where have... We all thought you were dead. Matt: I'm sorry. Foggy: Does Karen know you're back yet? Matt: Take a seat. Foggy: I'm... I'm not back. Matt: Well, I'm 99% sure I'm not hallucinating. Foggy: I'm, uh... not back. Matt: Matt Murdock isn't gonna be a part of me anymore. Um... I'm leaving him behind. Foggy: What? Matt: The only reason I came here was to warn you and Karen... that Fisk is out and you're both in danger. Foggy: Dude... Matt: I've had a rough couple of months, Foggy. Questioning a lot of... The point of it all. And last night, everything became clear. I'm going after him, Foggy. I'm gonna find a way to bring Fisk down. But I can only do that if I know you and Karen are safe. Foggy: Dude, slow down. I'm still processing that you're, like, even sitting here. Matt: I know you're gonna want to get involved. You and Karen will try and fight Fisk in some way. I'm telling you, I need you to stay out of it and leave it to me. Foggy: No. Matt: "No"? Foggy: No. You don't get to show up like this and say something like that and expect me to be cool with it. Matt: You're my best friend, asshole. Foggy: I see I was wrong to become your friend. Matt: I... I put you in danger, and it was selfish of me. I can't change the past, but I can stop making the same mistake. We're done, buddy. It's, uh... It's over. Foggy: There's something seriously wrong with you. Matt: Yeah, I know. Foggy: Stay clear of Fisk. Tell Karen to do the same. And I'd appreciate it if you didn't tell her you saw me. Matt: Do you even hear yourself right now? Foggy: Goodbye, Foggy. Matt: Matt! Matt!
Hattley: Was it him? Ray: He took out six feds. He wasn't in a red suit, but, yeah, it was him. Hattley: So the Devil is back.

Ray: Move! Move! Officer: Get back! Back it up! Ray: I need to make a call. Agent: Lobby's secure. Straight to the nest! Move! Ray: SAC's inbound. What the hell happened? Dex: Ambush. They were everywhere. Ray: Do you have status on anyone? Dex: Two agents in surgery now. We lost five for this shitbag. Fisk: Donovan! Ray: Stay back. Donovan: We're his attorneys. Ray: Congratulations. Stay back. Fisk: Locate Vanessa. The Albanians, they tried to get me. They'll go for her, too. Donovan: My client is not implying that he knows how to reach a wanted fugitive. Fisk: And make sure she's safe! Ray: We're good. Get the medic. Dex: He's fine. Ray: For me, not him. Dex: Copy that. Shitbag's all yours. Ray: Dex... Hold on. Check in with the SAC. Dex: We're down too many agents. The debrief can wait. Ray: You know the deal. Follow the protocol and get back here ASAP. Ray: You will be confined to these quarters. You'll be monitored at all times. You are allowed no outside contact other than your lawyers. Armed guards will be stationed outside 24/7. You'll be safe here. Fisk: "Safe." You nearly had me killed. Ray: Good men died tonight. You will make their sacrifice worth something. Or you can shove our deal up your ass. Arinori: Hey, convict... your lawyers are here. Get dry. Get dressed. Fisk: Did you reach her? Donovan: I need these cameras shut off and a moment with my client. Fisk: Forget about the cameras. Agent: Kill the cameras till they leave. Fisk: Is Vanessa safe? Donovan: We don't know. She's missing.

Karen: Oh, God. I don't know, it's been... uh, three months since I had one. Lily: See, now, that's bad. Karen: Yeah. Lily: Yeah, it's been about a month for me. I've been elbows deep in, uh, research, but it feels like 100 years since I had a home-cooked meal. Ellison: This is all Uncle Mitchell. Lily: Please, stop. Left to my own devices, we'd be ordering Wo Hop every night. Karen: Nothing wrong with that. Ellison: This woman does it all. Not only does she run Proxy Magazine, she is an expert orderer. Lily: Stop it. Ellison: No, it's true. You're amazing. It's like a skill. Right? You know all the best dishes on every menu. You always order the right amount. Never too much, too little. It's perfect. Lily: He'd be lost without me. Ellison: I would. Jason: Disgusting. Karen: Are they always like this? Jason: When I was eight, they renewed their vows on Long Beach in front of the whole family. Karen: No. Jason: Aunt Lily hired one of those planes that write in the sky. Karen: Oh, my God. Did you really? Lily: I did. Karen: So, how did you two meet? Lily: Kind of like you guys, actually. We were set up by our college newspaper editor. Jason: Oh. Mitchell, did you not tell them? Jason: Uncle Mitchell... Karen: I am so sorry. I had no idea. I had no... I was... I had nothing to do with it. Ellison: You know what? Uh, we need... We need more wine. Karen: Really? Ellison: I get it. I'm sorry. Ellison: You know... I knew that if I had actually asked you, you'd have said no. Karen: Right. See, that's the part where it gets to be my choice. Ellison: I know you meant well, but this... Karen: You could use some happy. Ellison: I am happy. Karen: Look, I'm not, um... I'm not ready. Ellison: All right, well, if you want to leave, I'll understand. I'm sure Jason will, too. Jason: So, wait. You're telling me that you named your cat Ralph? Karen: Ellison. Jason: Oh. Hey! I have a PhD in Am Lit. He's my favorite author. "Life is to be lived, not controlled. Humanity is won by..." Karen: I know this one, actually... "Humanity is won by continuing to play in the face of certain defeat." Jason: Is that right? How do you know the quote? Karen: I was going to be an English major. Invisible Man would have been a big part of my curriculum, but that was another lifetime. Jason: You made out okay. A revered journalist with an acclaimed publication. Karen: Okay. Lily: Too much, honey. Karen: So, tell me, you ever worry little Ralph's plotting your demise? Jason: I take it you're a dog person. Karen: Absolutely. Jason: I don't know, I like the company. Shared a room with my brother growing up. The apartment felt empty till I got Ralph. How about you? Any, uh, siblings? Karen: Uh. More wine? Jason: Um... Yeah. No, I had a brother, too, but, um... but he died. Karen: I'm sorry. Jason: No, it's okay. Lily: Who wants dessert? Karen: That'd be great. Thank you. Ellison: Sorry. I'm sorry. Yeah. Ellison. Karen: Uh, sorry. Karen Page. Ellison: Who in the hell would let out Fisk? Karen: Don't say his name. Ellison: What? Why? Ellison: After Ben died, Lily was inconsolable. They were really close. And, you know, it turned out that somebody at my office had been working for him. We'd gotten to the point where an hour could go by, and I didn't have to call to reassure that I'm alive. Karen: I understand. Ellison: Good. Then you won't push back when I tell you, you are staying away from this story. Karen: I can't do that. Ellison: Yes, you can. And you will. Look, I get it. I have a history with... that man. Karen: Makes it a conflict of interest. Ellison: Exactly. But I also know him better than anyone else on our staff. Doesn't that give me a unique angle? Karen: It gives you a bias. Look, it's not up for discussion. Enjoy the pie.

Marci: Baby... What was it this time? Laughing Matt? Foggy: Body Matt. Marci: Foggy Bear, whatever happened to Matt, it's not your fault. You have nothing to feel guilty about. Foggy: Because I have this great life? Beautiful girlfriend, high-paying job, expensive suits... I always wanted a good suit. I have it all, but Matt's just... gone. Marci: Maybe you should talk to someone. Foggy: It won't bring him back. Marci: But it might help you. Foggy: I can't. Marci: Why not? Foggy: Sorry. Go back to your brief. Marci: Take a pill. There's some in the medicine cabinet. Foggy: No. No. No.

Crowd: Lock Fisk up! Lock Fisk up! Lock Fisk up! Lock Fisk up! Matt: Doesn't make any sense. Fisk: Of course it does. God is angry with you. Matt: What are you talking about? Fisk: You don't think God knows you tried to kill yourself? Matt: No. That has nothing to do with this. Fisk: God restored your hearing... just in time to hear my name chanted by the crowds. Just in time to learn, in the long run, I won, you lost. Does that sound like God's forgiveness? Matt: No. Fisk: It sounds like... hell. Crowd: Lock Fisk up! Lock Fisk up! Fisk: You'll never keep Karen safe. Matt: In the end, you'll kill her, too. Fisk: Stop it. Matt: Just like your father. Fisk: And Stick. Matt: I said stop. Fisk: And Elektra. Fisk: They all died because of you, Matthew.

Karen: I can't believe this. This is insane. Officer: You're that reporter. Karen: Sorry. Karen Page, Bulletin. Uh... Sorry, who's in charge here? Officer: That's the genius who got him out. Agent Nadeem. Karen: Thanks. Karen: Agent Nadeem. Ray: Soon as I'm done here. Seema: There's a vigil at the hospital. Just give Sami a hug for me. You, too. Karen: Hi. Karen Page of the New York Bulletin. Ray: I'm not authorized to speak to the press. You need to find Special Agent In Charge Hattley. Karen: But it is N-A-D-E-E-M, right? And you're the agent who released Wilson Fisk? Ray: Fisk has not been released. That's fake news. Ray: He's a cooperating witness, but he's very much a convicted prisoner and being treated as such. Karen: Being held in a $11 million penthouse? Ray: Seized by the US Government from some Wall Street prick convicted of fraud. Karen: Oh. Oh, I get it. Okay, so what's he having for dinner? Is it the filet mignon or the line-caught halibut? Ray: Press area is over there. Karen: One RICO count carries a 20-year sentence. Fisk was convicted on five. Want to explain to me how this is justice? Ray: Jennings, Garcia, Foster, Leighton, Torres. They lost their lives, and they were good agents, good people. Five families are getting the worst news of their lives right now because of Wilson Fisk. Ma'am, I understand your concerns about my job, but right now, I got to help those families. Excuse me.

Dr. Mercer: Mr. Poindexter. Dex: Just "Dex" is fine. Dr. Mercer: All right. Well, if you want me to call you "just Dex"... Dex: Just "Dex." Dr. Mercer: Well, very nice to meet you, just Dex. I'm Dr. Mercer. You can call me Eileen if you want. Dex: I'll call you "Dr. Mercer." Dr. Mercer: Okay. Have a seat. Dr. Mercer: I know these visits can feel like a chore. Dex: Not at all. I like routines. Keeps me focused. Dr. Mercer: Mmm-hmm. How are you doing, otherwise? Have you had any violent impulses since our last visit? Dex: Nope. I... I like the new job. Agents are cool. My supervisor, Ray, he's a good guy. Dr. Mercer: That's great. A lot of the folks I talk to can have trouble meshing with a new team. Dex: Well, they respect me. I help them out with drills and tactics. Most of them shoot like shit. Dr. Mercer: Well, that's great. And you've been out in the field lately, I understand? Dex: I have. Dr. Mercer: It's a big step. How do you feel about that? Dex: About what? Dr. Mercer: About being in high-stress situations. Dex: I don't know. I process it. Dr. Mercer: Do you have a support system? Dex: Well, I think she'd rather be called Julie. Dr. Mercer: Oh. Well, tell me, how does that work? Dex: She's a bartender. Professional listener, like you. She probably gets paid more. Dr. Mercer: Tell me about her. Dex: We get dinner most nights. Today's Tuesday? It's pizza night. Julie gets broccoli with sausage, extra cheese. I tell her about my day. The good, the bad. I know it's not healthy to hold this stuff in, so... I talk to her. I tell her everything. And... And she doesn't judge me or blame me. She's just... there for me. Dr. Mercer: She sounds like a good one. Dex: Yeah, she is. Dr. Mercer: All right. You are clear for duty. But I want you checking in with me daily for a while. Okay? Dex: Yes, sir. Dr. Mercer: You, uh... You go see your girl. It'll do you good.

Matt: Why did Fisk flip on the Albanians? Donovan: I don't know what you're talking about. You've got the wrong person. Matt: Fisk hated prison. The FBI got him out. Donovan: No, no. He could have turned on anyone. Why the Albanians? Matt: I'm just a lawyer. Donovan: What is Fisk really getting out of this? Is it the Albanians' territory? Matt: No. Donovan: Is it money? Matt: No. Donovan: Why don't you let me know when you wanna breathe? Donovan: Fisk's woman. The feds will drop all charges against her. Matt: No. Donovan: I swear! He's doing it all for her. Matt: And where is Vanessa? Agent 1: Where you wanna eat? Agent 2: How about the Chinese place? Donovan: Help! Help! Agent 3: Over there! Go! Let's go! Donovan: Help! Matt: He's an Albanian. Agent 4: There's an unidentified assailant in the parking deck, considered armed and dangerous. Agent 5: Anyone got a visual on him? Agent 6: Nothing yet. Moving to the south side of the garage. Agent 7: We're in stairwell H, heading down to parking level three. Agent 8: We need backup on parking level three. Repeat, we need backup on parking level three. Agent 9: Stop! FBI! Fbi Agent: They have families, asshole. Matt: Listen. I'm not here to... Agent 10: There he is! Stop! Stop! Agent 11: Stop! Fbi Agent: Come out with your hands up. Now. Fbi Agent: Stay down, man. Matt: Oh, God.

Guard: Up! Up! Up! Room check! Lim: Convict, stand and face the wall! Guard: Comb the area. We'll be conducting a mandatory sweep of the area. You're to cooperate with all instructions. You understand? Fisk: I understand. Lim: Check. Lim: I am searching your person to ensure you're not carrying anything that might be harmful to yourself or others. Do you understand? Fisk: I understand. Lim: Check. Turn around. Fisk: Are we finished here? Lim: All clear. Driver: Oh, these mornings are getting colder and colder. Piece of crap can't keep up for nothing. Where we off to, boss?

Karen: Gelsdorf... Karen: Hi. Yes. I know you said you couldn't meet until Friday morning, but I found something. I don't think it can wait till then. Yes, absolutely. Off the record. Karen: No, only somebody who works at the FDIC can help me. You will? Thank you so much. No... Yeah, tomorrow is perfect. Great. I think I figured out how Fisk got his money out of the country. Ellison: I can't even get a hello anymore. Karen: Sorry. Hey, how are you? Ellison: I am... confused. Uh, Mitchell Ellison, editor in chief of the New York Bulletin, pleased to meet you. And who might you be? Karen: I'm sorry. What? Ellison: Well, you couldn't be the Karen Page I've come to know and respect because that Karen Page takes the stories I give her without a fight. Karen: Look, I told you I would take the story, and I am. Ellison: And yet, the Rostam Kazemi piece that I asked you to write, which should have been filed an hour ago, has yet to materialize. Karen: I had other work to do. And I've been making some good headway on the Fisk piece. Ellison: We already published the Fisk piece. Karen: Well, there's follow-up. Ellison: There always is. Sit. Karen: Mitch... Ellison: Sit. Please. You know I'd do anything for you, right? I mean, shit, you helped me bag my first Pulitzer. Karen: You earned that Pulitzer. Ellison: Yeah, well... I wouldn't have if it weren't for you. So believe me when I say that what I'm about to do... I'm only doing it because I care. Karen: What are you about to do? Ellison: I'm taking you off of anything Wilson Fisk. Karen: What? Ellison: You heard me. Karen: Why? Ellison: Because you have become one of those reporters who has fallen into the trap of thinking they're more important than the story. And I'm trying to save you from that. Karen: "Save me"? Ellison: From becoming the story. I mean, that's what you want, isn't it? To break this thing wide open, be the reporter who exposed Wilson Fisk's big secret? I've seen it a million times. Reporter gets so obsessed with some story that they can't see straight. They start cutting corners. You're chasing. You're chasing, Karen. And that is when you make mistakes. Karen: I haven't made any mistakes. Ellison: Not yet. But you're headed down that road. I can see it. And I know you probably can't. But take a step back. Look in the mirror. You're exhausted. You look like shit. When was the last time you got a decent night's sleep? Karen: Last night. Ellison: Don't bullshit a bullshitter. Karen: I know what I'm doing. Ellison: I'm sure you think you do. But I am your boss. And I'm telling you, no more Fisk. You wanna know why I'm doing this? It's not to punish you. It's because you are a damn good reporter. And I don't want you to screw this up for yourself. You got talent, kid. Real talent. Don't waste it. Karen: So that's it? Ellison: That's it. Now get me that Kazemi piece.

Guard: Keep moving. Inmate 1: Fresh meat! Inmate 2: Hey, pretty boy! Inmate 3: Yo, homes, you lost? Guard: In here. Inmate: You the lawyer? Matt: Yeah. Inmate: Vic wants to see you. Matt: That's why I'm here. Inmate: You're in the wrong place. This ain't where we meet. Matt: Where, then? Inmate: The showers. After count. Someone will come get you. Matt: The showers? Inmate: You got a problem with that? Matt: No. No problem.

Dex: It would be inappropriate of me to comment on the ongoing investigation into the motorcade attack. It would also be inappropriate of me to tell you that there was a slight discrepancy between your official report and the forensic analysis of the shooting. Ray: Yeah, it would be inappropriate for you to tell me all this. Dex: Because of you, my wife still has her husband... and my son still has his father.

Foggy: Detective! Brett: The hell are you doing here? This is a union-only function. Foggy: You know what I love about our dynamic? We skip the pleasantries. No hellos. No how-you-beens. Straight to business. Brett: I'm about to get to the business of dragging your ass up outta here. Foggy: I wouldn't have intruded if it wasn't important. Brett: Let me guess. You need a favor. Foggy: See? Do you have this kind of shorthand with anyone else? Brett: Wilson Fisk. His cushy new situation is a federally-funded slap in the face to every officer in this room. Foggy: No shit. Not sure what that has to do with you crashing this party, though. Brett: I want to say a few words, express my solidarity. And it would play better if you gave me the floor. Just to say a few things. Foggy: It's been a long week, Foggy, okay? And you talking is only gonna drag it out. Now, it's time to go. In handcuffs or on your own. Brett: Say no more. Foggy: Hey, Brett, how's it going? Excuse me, esteemed constables. Guys, could I have... Officer 1: Hey, Counselor, I personally wanna thank you for springing my arson perp out of jail on a technicality. Foggy: Come on. There were mitigating circumstances, and you know it, Officer. His building was not up to code. Officer 1: Let me show you where to stick your mitigating circumstances. Brett: Hey, hey, hey, people, look, um... Nelson's all right. He helped the city put Fisk behind bars. Give him a minute. One minute. Foggy: Officers, I don't mean to disappoint. But I'm not here to talk only about Wilson Fisk. With his name on everyone's lips, he's getting far more publicity than any cop killer deserves. His name deserves to be buried... buried in the same hard earth where he put your fallen brothers. I'm here to talk about Blake Tower... our honorable district attorney. Here's a man charged with ensuring the safety of this city, just as you are. And yet, he stands idly by while the feds whisk that monster out of prison and into the warm lap of luxury. Someone smarter than me... Officer 2: That's a pretty freakin' low bar, isn't it? Foggy: That man said, "The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing." Blake Tower is a good man doing nothing. Which is why I'm running my own write-in campaign for district attorney, to oust Blake Tower and to put Wilson Fisk into the deepest prison hole allowable under the Eighth Amendment. And I would love nothing more than to do that with the endorsement of each of you and your illustrious union. Officer 3: All right, where do I sign up?

Man 1: Hey, baby. Hey, baby. Hey, what's up, yo? Man 1: Look at shorty comin'. Hey, hey, let me get your name. Woman: Let's go around. Man 2: What we getting into? Man 3: What's up, y'all? Let me get your names. Man 1: Come on! What we getting into tonight? Man 2: Where you going, Ma? We got all night! See, that ass is walking away, bro. Man 3: Yo, that's all you, bro. That's all you, bro. Man 1: Now, this is a real lady. Man 2: Come here. You coming to say hi? We could have some fun tonight. Yeah, you like fun? Karen: Get out of my way. Man 1: You got bite. Come on, play with us. Karen: Let's play a game. Man 2: What do you wanna play? Karen: The one where I play scared little girl? 'Cause it seems you like scaring girls. Man 3: It's all good. We was just having fun. Karen: Let's have fun. Huh? Who goes first? You? Me? Man 1: Lady, we were just being friendly. Karen: Then this is just a friendly reminder that games like that can get your head blown off. Why are you still here?

Dex: Trouble at home? Ray: Um, no, I... Actually, that's none of my business. Dex: No, no. Um... I could use some help, advice. I don't know. You've taken fire before, right? Ray: Enough. Dex: You have kids at the time? Ray: Your boy having trouble with the shooting? Dex: Yeah. Yeah, he's, uh, not sleeping, you know... watching the news. Stuff like that. I mean, I think the best thing to do is talk to him like a man. Tell him that the job I do is dangerous, but I... Ray: My advice... don't. Dex: I tried that with my daughter. It freaked her out so bad, she wouldn't let me leave the house in the morning. She lay across the door and cried until I called in and took the day. Treat your son like a CI. Ray: Make my kid my snitch? Dex: Snitch lives in a scary world they don't control, and they depend on you to keep 'em safe. Sound familiar? Ray: Yeah, but lying to my son... Dex: My dad was a trucker. He mostly hauled chemical tankers. He'd bring 'em to the house overnight before heading out sometimes. And I'd have nightmares, thinking about what could happen. But when my dad found out, he showed me a diamond-shaped decal on the back with the colors and numbers. He told me the numbers tell you how high the level of danger is. He only hauled level four, safest stuff. Once I knew that, it didn't seem so scary anymore. Ray: Level four is the most lethal code. Dex: But I didn't know that. And I didn't worry when he drove off every morning in a rolling fire bomb. The lies that keep us safe are the ones worth telling. Dex: Coming?

Gelsdorf: Ms. Page? What are you doing here? Karen: I know we had an appointment for tomorrow, but what we have to talk about can't wait till then. Gelsdorf: This is my home. My family is upstairs. Karen: I know. I'm sorry. Gelsdorf: You're lucky I'm willing to talk to you, period. If my bosses at the FDIC found out I was talking... Karen: Red Lion National Bank. Gelsdorf: And how the hell did you get my address? Did Ellison put you up... Karen: No. Ellison doesn't know that I'm here. He doesn't know that I reached out to you. I know that looks bad... Gelsdorf: And if you did, you wouldn't be standing here. Karen: The sooner you tell me about Red Lion, the sooner I go. Gelsdorf: Wilson Fisk is laundering his money through that bank. We're talking millions of dollars. Gelsdorf'S Wife: Honey, who's at the door? Gelsdorf: Someone from work. Karen: The FDIC has to be monitoring a bank involved... Gelsdorf: We're done here. Karen: Hey! No, I just... I need proof. Give me a contact at the bank. Gelsdorf: I'll be having words with Ellison in the morning. Karen: Give me a name, you will never see me again. Gelsdorf'S Wife: Honey, what's going on? Gelsdorf: There's only one name worth checking into, and... good luck squeezing anything out of him. Karen: Who? Gelsdorf: Felix Manning. Karen: Thank you. Gelsdorf: Thank me by getting the hell off my property. Karen: Sorry.

Agent: I thought you were relieved for the day. Dex: Is everyone gone? Agent: Yeah. Dex: Good. Yeah, that's good. Why don't you go downstairs, grab a cup of coffee? My treat. Agent: Yeah. That's a good idea. I'll just... Yeah. Dex: Do you remember these men? Fisk: They were among the Albanians who attacked the motorcade. Winn: Did you see these men die? Fisk: Yes, I did. Winn: And did you see who shot them? Fisk: There was only one FBI agent left standing. Special Agent Poindexter. Winn: The moment he shot them, can you describe, for the record, what you saw? Fisk: They were armed. Special Agent Poindexter gave them a chance to surrender, but then their weapons came up to shoot him. He killed them both in self-defense. Winn: Thank you for your time, Mr. Fisk. Dex: What's your game? Fisk: Game? Dex: I don't need any favors from you, convict. Fisk: Favors, no. But sympathy... Papers, protests... the mockery. I can carry this burden of humiliation, but you? You're a dedicated federal agent. Dex: You don't know anything about me. Fisk: Neither does the Bulletin. The press is labeling the attack on my life as an FBI disaster. And now they're investigating you for doing your job. They're questioning you for your exceptionalism. You saved my life! And the lives of honorable federal agents. Did they report that? No. Instead, they vilify... and demean your act of courage. The world is changing. The real heroes are ridiculed and dismissed. And for that, I offer my sympathy.
Matt: Where are we? Where... Wait... Hey, hold up. Stop the car. Man: No problem. We'll get you home. Matt: Who are you? Hey! Hey! No, no, no. No.

Foggy: Matt shows up alive, then tells me I'm never gonna see him again. Only I, Foggy Nelson, can be ghosted by a ghost. Marci: It's locked. Like it was the last time you checked it. Foggy: We need to get another dead bolt installed. A single dead bolt and a measly chain? Might as well be a beaded curtain. Marci: Foggy, relax. Foggy: Relax? Are you even listening to me? Wilson Fisk wants my scalp. And for all we know, he wants yours, too. It's not like you've done him any favors. And of course Matt wants me to stick to the sidelines while he deals with Fisk. Only Matt Murdock is fit for the real action. Just because I'm not... Marci: What? Foggy: Nothing. I don't even know what I'm saying anymore. Marci: Foggy, breathe. Matt was gone. Now he's back. Fisk is out, and I have no idea where that leaves me. Foggy: Screw the sidelines. We go on the offense. Marci: Offense? With Fisk? He has the law and the FBI on his side. And it's not like we've heard a statement from the DA condemning his release. No, no, nothing to jeopardize Blake Tower's reelection. God forbid he grow a pair. Foggy: Oh, that could work. Marci: Blake Tower growing a pair? Not gonna happen. Foggy: No, think about it. The best way to protect yourself from Fisk is to make noise, is to be out in the open. Marci: Oh, like a public execution. Foggy: Like a public call to action. If Blake Tower won't do anything to stop Fisk, then run against him for district attorney. Marci: If you're already a target, you might as well be the first person to take a swing. Foggy: No, I'm serious. The more public, the more you're protected. Marci: There's no way I can win. Foggy: Well, of course not. Marci: Thank you for the confidence. Foggy: Anyways, we're light-years past the deadline. Marci: Then run as a write-in. You base your candidacy on a single issue. Putting Fisk back behind bars. You'd bag a few votes. I mean, not enough to win, but you'd get the issue out there. Plus, you'd make a few friends in the NYPD, and... that's not the worst thing for a defense attorney. Foggy: Or you could keep checking the locks. Marci: I won't let anything happen to you. Foggy: Oh, baby. Foggy: Then we better start working on that swing. After coffee. Marci: You're buying. Foggy: Have you seen my wallet?
Driver: This is good? Matt: Yeah, here's fine. Hey, you paying with card? 'Cause, you know, cash is better. Matt: Wait for me. Driver: Oh, yeah. Yeah, I can do that.

Matt: Hi. Good morning. Guard: Purpose for your visit? Matt: I have an appointment with my client. I called earlier. I should be on the visitor list. Guard: ID. Matt: I can't find my wallet. Did I leave it at home, or drop it in the cab... Guard: Without picture ID, I can't... Matt: Just give me one second. Guard: Sir, please step aside while... Matt: This is my New York Bar number. Now, it's not picture ID, I know, but it did take seven years and cost me $200,000 in student loans. Does it, uh, buy me anything? Guard: Name? Matt: Nelson. Franklin Nelson.
Man: How you doin'? Ray: Good. Man: You're holding up? Ray: Mm-hmm.

Michael: Matt! I thought Foggy... Matt: What's up, Michael? Michael: Oh, man. It's good to see you. Matt: It's good to see you, too. Even if it is in this shithole. Michael: I'm sure you're wondering... I'm sorry, I shouldn't have said shithole. I'm trying not to curse. What's the point of me getting out of here in 18 months with a degree in psychology, top of my class... if I still swear like a goddamn sailor? Did it again. Matt: Well, sorry. Saint Matthew. Michael: No, come on, I'm no saint. You and Foggy got 10 years knocked off my sentence. If that's not divine intervention, huh? Michael: Where is Foggy? I've never seen you two apart. Matt: We're not, uh... We're not working together anymore. Michael: Aw, man, that sucks. Matt: Yeah. Listen, I don't want anyone, even Foggy, to know that I was here, so... Michael: Yeah, I can do that. Matt: Appreciate it. Michael: So, what's the big mystery? Matt: Yeah, so, look, you, um... worked with the Albanians, right? Michael: A long time ago. Low-level stuff. Mostly just running. Matt: Mm-hmm. But they're offering you protection in here? Michael: What do you want with the Albanians? Matt: I want an introduction. Michael: If somebody needs a defense lawyer, I'll make sure to pass your name along. Glowing review. But, you know, folks in here, they're murdering bastards. Matt: I want an introduction to Vic Jusufi. Michael: Nobody gets in with Vic. Matt: You can't make it happen? Man: ...and the extra two years added? Michael: What do you want with him, anyway? Matt: Wilson Fisk could've turned on any crime organization. I want to know why the Albanians. What did they have on Fisk? Michael: Just, uh... let this go. Matt: No, I can't do that. Fisk stays out, innocent people die. Michael: I don't know shit. Matt: Michael, you can help me. Michael: No. Matt: Come on. Michael: You're gonna get me killed. Michael: Get this guy away from me! I don't know him! Get him away! Get him away! Guard: That's enough! Michael: Assault by an inmate... I said nothing. On my mother! My mother! Guard 2: Sir? Matt: It's all right. It's just a misunderstanding. Guard: Mr. Nelson, you need to get checked out by the nurse. Matt: It's fine. I'm fine. Guard: Then you can say that on an incident report. Liability reasons. Can't let you leave until you sign one. Matt: Yeah, all right. Guard 2: Follow me. Man: He's right in there.

Seema: Hi, boys. Ray: Hi. Seema: Hey. I brought clothes, mouthwash, and some leftover chole. Ray: Thanks. Seema: Hey, I'm sorry. It's gonna be like this all week. Ray: You promise me you'll eat? Your face looks thin. Seema: Fine. Okay, I'll eat. Ray: I love you. We gotta go. Seema: What "we"? Is Sami here? Ray: He's in the car, killing aliens on my phone. Seema: I'd love to see him. Bring him up. Ray: You're working, and I don't want to be late. Seema: Late? Late for what? Ray: Late for my sister's. Sami is gonna stay there for a couple of days. Seema: Sami has a bed. Ray: One that he can't sleep in. Seema: What do you mean? What's going on? Ray: He stays up all night, waiting for you to come home. He's been watching the news. He's... He's scared something is going to happen to you. Seema: Look at me. I'm fine. Ray: Are you? 'Cause Sami isn't the only one who's scared. Let him stay with Nav and the kids. Get his mind off all of this. Seema: No. I'll talk to him when I come home. Look... nothing bad is gonna happen to me. Ray: I was at the hospital. I talked to the other spouses waiting outside the ER. None of those agents thought anything bad was going to happen to them, either. Seema: I know how much this promotion means, but nothing is worth... Ray: We can talk about this later. Seema: Sami is going to my sister's. Make sure you eat.

Guard 1: Face the wall. Let's go. Turn around. Against the wall. Against the wall. Now. Foreheads to the wall. Let's go, gentlemen. Spread your legs. Guard 2: Wait in here. Nurse should be by. Matt: Thanks.

Donovan: There is no corpse. There's no corpse. Fisk: I heard you. Remind Felix Manning that I do not tolerate loose ends. Donovan: Yes, Mr. Fisk. But the body was probably just swept away in the current. Even if Murdock somehow escaped from the cab, how does a blind man swim to shore? Fisk: This look like a blind man to you? Donovan: We investigated him thoroughly. His associates. Medical and school records all check out. All confirm that Matt Murdock lost his sight at age nine. Fisk: Yes. Nevertheless... a man capable of that could have survived. And he threatened to come between Vanessa and I. Donovan: It's time for the government to honor our deal. Thanks to my client, the Albanian Syndicate has been completely wiped out. Their counterfeiting ring, their Dark Web child pornography. And the Jalisco connection Mr. Fisk divulged last week gave the DEA an early and very white Christmas. And in exchange for his ongoing cooperation, the DOJ will not be filing charges against Vanessa Marianna. Mr. Fisk is also entitled to the return of certain personal belongings, supervised movement within the hotel. Ray: He'll get everything he was offered. In time. Donovan: That time is now, Special Agent Nadeem. Unless you'd like my client to stop talking. Fisk: FBI has sacrificed a great deal for me. And I will continue to cooperate and trust you'll honor your word. There's a criminal I've employed. A facilitator. On my behalf, he's laundered and hid money, bribed law enforcement and court officials, orchestrated perjured testimony, manufactured evidence. Ray: Who is he? Fisk: A lawyer. Matthew Murdock.

Bartender: Can I get you started with something to drink? Dex: Looks like you need a little more time. I'll grab you a water. Julie: This is gonna sound random, but did you used to work at the Brooklyn Suicide Hotline? Dex: Yeah. Yeah, I did. That... was a tough job. Julie: It was. You probably don't remember me. I'm Julie. Dex: Dex. Yeah, of course I remember you. Julie: Small world, huh? Dex: I haven't seen you in here before. Julie: It's... it's my first day, actually. I got offered double the pay to leave my last job if I could start here immediately. Not that I'm complaining. What about you? Are you staying at the hotel? Dex: No. I live here. In New York, not in the hotel. Dex: The FBI has an office upstairs. We're guarding Wilson Fisk. Julie: A G-man. Woman: Excuse me, miss! Hello? Julie: I need to go help that table so they don't fire me on my first day. Dex: What time do you get off? Julie: In about an hour. Dex: Do you wanna hang out after? Catch up? Julie: Uh... Yeah. That... That'd be great. Dex: Hmm.

Theo: I got your coppa, your prosciutto, your mocetta, your sweet soppressata. All you can eat. Free! For anybody who promises to vote for Foggy Nelson, my less handsome brother. Foggy: You can't do that, Theo. It violates election law. It's an illegal inducement to vote. Theo: I don't see Mrs. Wobschall calling the cops. Mrs. Callahan: May I borrow a pen? Foggy: Is that an actual ballot, Mrs. Callahan? Mrs. Callahan: I just voted for you. Absentee. When Wilson Fisk set off those explosives in Hell's Kitchen, I lost my husband. Everything that matters, gone. Except my vote. I'm counting on you, Foggy. You get that son of a bitch. Foggy: I will. I promise. Thank you, everyone. And I'll be here till close to answer any questions. Ray: Yeah, I got a few. Like, what's the secret ingredient in your world-famous Nelson's sub? Foggy: A soft robiola. Ray: Perfect. Uh, team at work is gonna love that. Uh... Give me six. Foggy: Uh, Theo can help you at the counter. Ray: Is there anything else? Foggy: Yeah. When's the last time you saw Matt Murdock? Ray: Who are you? Foggy: Crashing my campaign event, trying to intimidate me, dropping the names of my friends... I'm not backing off my criticism of the feds' love affair with Fisk! Ray: You seem like a decent guy, Mr. Nelson. You care about people. About doing the right thing. I'm guessing that's why you ditched Matt Murdock as your law partner in the first place. Am I correct? Foggy: You really think I'm gonna answer a question that leading? Ray: To be clear: did you dissolve your partnership because Mr. Murdock took on Wilson Fisk as a client? Foggy: If you're referring to a single case where we represented a client who allegedly worked for Fisk even though we didn't know that at the time... the answer's no. It had nothing to do with it. Nelson and Murdock represented a lot of clients, for whom all work was completely ethical and legal and protected by attorney-client privilege. Ray: When's the last time you saw Matt Murdock? Foggy: Two nights ago. Ray: Where? Foggy: A bar in Hell's Kitchen. Ray: And what did you discuss? Foggy: That we hadn't seen each other in a while. Ray: Did he tell you where he was going? Foggy: No. Ray: Where you could find him? Foggy: No. Ray: Did he tell you anything? Foggy: That he was sorry. Ray: About what? Foggy: That our friendship isn't what it used to be. Ray: So you didn't knowingly give him your bar ID? Foggy: What? Foggy: Of course not. Why would I? Ray: So he could enter a prison, falsely using your identity, and make contact with an Albanian gang linked to the murder of nine federal agents. Foggy: I... I didn't give him my ID. Nor was I aware of anything that he was planning. But with all due respect, I think you have Matt Murdock all wrong. Ray: Yeah, well, uh... I don't think I do. I think Matt Murdock is hiding a double life. Lawyer by day and criminal by night. And you and Ms. Page both know all about it. It makes you uncomfortable. And complicit. And that's why you're no longer law partners or friends. Because once he's finally caught, you know you're on the hook as an accessory to his crimes. Or, if you're lucky, simply aiding and abetting. Foggy: Remind me, Special Agent Nadeem, what's Matt being charged with? Ray: Nothing so far. Foggy: Great. Then the only thing I'm aiding and abetting is your exit. Don't forget to vote.

Julie: Every day? Julie: FDR Drive's my favorite route, too. There's nothing in the world like a winter run on the East River. Between your workout habits and new gig, it's... it's almost like you're stalking me. Dex: Damn. The secret's out. Julie: So... why aren't you in social work anymore? Dex: Uh... Tried to pursue my dream as a dancer. It actually was going pretty well until I tore my ACL, again. Julie: I'm sorry. That must've been really hard. But you were brave to go for it in the first place. Dex: I, um... I didn't have a backup plan. My parents made the mistake of telling me I could be anything I wanted. Julie: Must've been nice to hear, even if it didn't work out. Dex: My parents were never really that involved. Julie: Sounds like you didn't need the message anyhow. You did great all on your own. Julie: So, what's it like working for Wilson Fisk? Dex: I don't work for him. I work for the federal government. Julie: Must be scary to be up close and personal with someone so dangerous. Dex: It is what it is. Julie: Do you think a killer like that deserves a second chance? Dex: You worked at the hotline for three years. I think you of all people would believe everyone deserves a second chance. Julie: How did you know I worked there for three years? You were only there for one. Dex: You mentioned it earlier. You quit to do ballet. Julie: Did I also mention ballet earlier? Specifically? Dex: I guess I... I just assumed. Julie: Anyway, um... It's late. I should get home. Dex: You're ditching me? Julie: No, not at all. I... I just have to go feed my dog. Dex: You don't have a dog. Julie: How do you know that? Dex: Julie, you're misreading this. Let me pay for dinner. We'll go for a walk in the park. I'll explain. Julie: Dinner's on me. Dex: Julie. You're very special to me. Julie: Let go of me, Dex. Please. Dex: I said let go!

Karen: Just being at Matt's apartment, and his bloody clothes... And I just... It threw me. Nadeem's smart. I probably gave him everything he needs to figure it out. Foggy: Wait. You told the FBI that Matt is Daredevil? Karen: No, no. Of course not. Karen: They know he's hiding something. It's not what they think, but this is bad. This is really bad. Infinitely bad. We could all go to jail. Foggy: Foggy... Karen: I should've never let Matt tell you his secret. This is my fault. I'm not gonna let you pay for our shitty mistakes. If it comes to it, I'll plead in exchange for your immunity. Foggy: Foggy... You always see the good in people. But you put us on such high pedestals, you can't see who we really are. I didn't tell the FBI Matt is Daredevil. I did something worse. Karen: Karen, breathe. I'm in trouble. Foggy: Tell me what happened. Karen: I'm gonna need attorney-client privilege before I can. Foggy: Okay, um, give me five bucks. Foggy: Good enough. I'm officially your lawyer. Karen: Do you remember the... the Healy trial? And there was that... that guy from... from CGI who offered us a stupid amount of money to take his case? Foggy: Yeah, how could I forget that creep? Karen: His name's James Wesley. He worked for Fisk. He disappeared shortly after that, and they think Matt had something to do with it. Foggy: That's crazy. Matt had nothing to do with that. Karen: I know. But if they keep investigating, they're gonna find out that I did. Foggy: What? Karen: I killed him. Dex: Shit. Shit.
Mercer: It's good to see you, Dex. How was your week? Young Dex: I'm scared, Dr. Mercer. Mercer: Scared? What's making you scared?

Ray: Alpha Team on approach. Ray: FBI. Get back in your apartment and close the door. Ray: Stack up. Breach. Fbi Agent: FBI! Clear! Agent: Murdock's been home. Recently. Agent: Command post, we're clear. Suspect's not here. Woman: NYPD has been advised. Citywide BOLO. Suspect Matthew Murdock to be considered armed and dangerous.
Agent: Alpha Team on approach. Agent: FBI. Get back in your apartment and close the door. Agent: Stack up. Breach. Fbi Agent: FBI! Agent Fremont: Clear! Agent: Murdock's been home. Recently.

location: STREET - OUTSIDE RED LION NATIONAL BANK
scene_text: Woman: It was so nice to see you again. Take care. Karen: Felix Manning? You haven't returned my calls. Karen Page, from the Bulletin. Before I go to print, I'm obligated to offer you a chance to comment on your involvement in laundering money for Wilson Fisk. Karen: Look, if you talk to me off the record, help me connect some dots, I promise I will keep your name out of it. But that is only if you talk to me. Karen: You're a fixer, Mr. Manning. You're a freelancer. Other clients, a lot to lose. Once this story breaks, Fisk is gonna hang you out to dry. If I were you, I would start looking out for myself. Manning: Karen Page. Daughter of Paxton and Penelope. Kings Road, Fagan Corners, Vermont. You had the back room. My guess, Dad wanted his little girl to be safe. Sadly, he should've been more worried about his little boy. Drug addicts really do destroy families, don't they? Manning: Off the record, you're incorrect. About what I do for a living. I don't fix problems. Manning: I make them disappear.

Fbi Agent: Karen Page? Karen: Who are you? Fbi Agent: Don't move. FBI. Karen: Uh... I have a weapon in my purse. And a concealed carry permit. Fbi Agent: Keep your hands exactly where they are and follow my instructions. Now turn around. Karen: Okay. Okay. Karen: Okay. Okay. Karen: What do you want from me? What happened? Why'd you bring me here? Foggy: I asked him to. Karen: Is Matt okay? Foggy: You wanna tell me what's going on? Ray: Ms. Page, I get that you ask questions for a living, but, for now, I'll be the one asking.

Ray: When's the last time you heard from Matt Murdock? Karen: Um... Months. Ray: You haven't seen or spoken to him in months? Karen: Uh, no. Ray: He give you any indication when he'd be back? Karen: Uh, no. Ray: Or whether he'd be back at all? Karen: No. Ray: Then why have you been paying his bills? Karen: He's a friend. Someone had to do it while he was away. Ray: So your friend, a blind man who you haven't spoken to in months, just ups and disappears, and you don't file a missing persons report? Karen: I figured he'd come back when he was ready. Ray: Can you think of any reason why Matt Murdock would go on the run? Karen: No. Ray: You were a secretary for Nelson and Murdock. Karen: Mmm-mmm. Office manager. Ray: And when did the firm first start working for Wilson Fisk? Karen: Um... We never worked for Wilson Fisk. Ray: Is that your signature? Ray: Do you remember depositing this retainer check for a company called CGI? Karen: Yes, I do. Um... Look, Matt and Foggy took on one case for them. That's all. Ray: According to my source, CGI was a front for Fisk. Karen: Well, we didn't know that at the time. Ray: But you do now. So you see how your last answer wasn't technically accurate? Karen: Okay, we never knowingly worked for Fisk. They hired us through someone else. Ray: Who? Karen: Some executive. Hang on. Ray: Was it this guy? James Wesley. You remember him? Karen: Uh, yeah. I think that was him. Why? Ray: Just trying to put the pieces together. Karen: Okay. Uh... Well, here are some other pieces for you to put together. Um... Felix Manning. Red Lion National Bank. Vancorp. Any of that ring any bells? Ray: I don't follow. Karen: Well, instead of letting Fisk use you and the FBI to retaliate against innocent lawyers who put him in prison, why don't you ask him if he hired a fixer named Felix Manning to launder money through Red Lion? Ask him if he's the true owner of a shell company called Vancorp. Ray: Why would I do that? Karen: Because it just bought the Presidential Hotel. Ray: Where are you getting this from? Karen: I ask questions for a living. I just ask better ones than you do. Like, has your so-called prisoner just bought the prison you're keeping him in? Ray: Has he bought? So this is what? Just a theory? Ray: You have any proof? Karen: Fisk is using you, Agent Nadeem. That's what he does. Ray: Is that a no? Karen: Am I under arrest? Ray: Not at this time. Karen: Then I'm done answering the wrong questions.
Donovan: Is this everything? Manning: Everything Felix's investigators were able to dig up on short notice. Donovan: Uh... This will take some time. Manning: I brought an audiobook.

Man: Dex, ready to go? Game starts in 20. Traffic's a nightmare. We gotta hustle. What's the deal? You don't even got your uniform on. You all right, buddy? Trouble in paradise? Does the headmaster know you're drilling a hole in his pile of bricks? Coach Bradley: He doesn't like it. He gives you a hard time, you send him my way. It's damn fine practice. Coach Bradley: Hey, I got you a little something. I was gonna wait until after the game... 100% leather. That's steerhide in the pocket and cowhide in the palm, so it's nice and soft. Try it on. Coach Bradley: An all-star pitcher deserves some all-star gear. Come on, let's go break it in. Dex: Wait. Real quick, can I show you my new wind-up? Coach Bradley: All right, showboat. Let's see it. Coach Bradley: You're in the zone, Dex. Keep throwing those heaters. Umpire: Strike! Strike! Strike! Strike! Strike! Strike! Coach Bradley: All right, kiddo. Pack it in. Let's give that arm of yours a rest. Young Dex: You're pulling me? Coach Bradley: I'm gonna let Kanon finish it out. Young Dex: But... but no one's gotten a hit off me. Coach Bradley: I know. You're killin' it out here. No question. But I gotta give other kids some field time. Young Dex: You can't do this. It's not fair! You gotta let me keep going. Coach Bradley: Keep it together, okay? Take a few deep breaths. Big gulps of air. Young Dex: I need... I need to keep going. Young Dex: If I pitch a perfect game, then they might... Coach Bradley: Dex... you could pitch a billion perfect games. It won't bring your parents back. Okay. Hit the pine. Grab a Popsicle. We'll talk later.

Mercer: Well, this has been nice so far, hasn't it? Talking like this. Now that we've gotten to know each other a little bit, I wonder if we could talk about Coach Bradley? What happened at the field? How did it make you feel? Sad? Maybe a little scared? Young Dex: I wasn't sad. Mercer: Why not, do you think? Young Dex: He was a jerk. Mercer: How so? How was Coach Bradley a jerk? Young Dex: He never let me do what I wanted. Didn't know shit about pitching. Mercer: He was your coach for a long time. Was he always such a jerk to you? What about last year when he named you MVP? Was he a jerk then? Young Dex: No. He used to be awesome. Mercer: Dex, tell me... And be honest. We like honesty around here. When you hit Coach Bradley... was that an accident? Young Dex: Whatever you say stays between us. Mercer: That's right. There are rules about that. Not even your parents... Young Dex: My parents are dead. Mercer: I'm sorry. I meant your social worker. That's right. There are rules. What you tell me stays between us. So... was it an accident? Young Dex: No. Mercer: Can you tell me what you were trying to do? Young Dex: I was trying to kill him.

location: FLASHBACK - KAREN'S APARTMENT - AFTER KILLING WESLEY
scene_text: Foggy: Karen, the gun. Where is it? Karen: Bottom of the Hudson. Foggy: Did you touch the body? Karen: He said he was gonna kill you. You and Matt and my family. He said I would die knowing I got you all killed. Foggy: Karen, that's awful, but, please, you have to focus. Did you touch the body? Karen: No. I don't think so. Foggy: What about your clothes? Get blood on them? Karen: I threw them away. Foggy: Foggy, can you not talk to me like a lawyer and just... just talk to me? I want you to tell me that I'm a bad person. Karen: I can't say that. Foggy: Why... why not? Karen: Because you're not. Foggy: Then why are you looking at me like that? Karen: Because my friend... my amazing, kind, brilliant friend... went through something terrible. And I didn't know. Foggy: When I got the gun, I could've called the cops. I could've run. Karen: You were afraid for your life. It was self-defense. Foggy: Seven times. Karen: What? Foggy: I shot him... seven times... because I wanted him dead. Matt: Hey, Karen. You need to pay me back for your rent.

Karen: Sister Maggie? Maggie: Can I help you? Karen: Uh, yes. Uh, one of the nuns said I should speak with you. Um... I'm looking for Matt Murdock. I'm sure he swore you to secrecy, but... he came to see me this morning. Asked for my help. Uh, is he here? Maggie: No, he's not. Karen: Okay. I'm sorry. Sorry to bother you. Maggie: "And some bloody their fists trying to keep the Kitchen safe." That was from your article, right? The one about heroes? Karen: Yeah. Maggie: Matt showed it to me. He was very proud. Karen: Yeah, well, he shouldn't be. All it did was get him into trouble. Maggie: I'll tell him you stopped by. Karen: Actually, can you... Can you not mention it? Maggie: Of course. Karen: Thank you.

Karen: You're making a mistake. Jasper: No, if I talk, Fisk kills my son! Karen: Look at this place. I grew up here. We had a good life before the neighborhood went down and I got myself put away. I left my son without a father. And this is what he does with his life. If I go back inside, it won't be long until he's sharin' a cell with me or worse. Karen: If Fisk stays out of prison, a lot of innocent people are gonna die. So you can either tell my paper the truth and we let you and your son run far away— or you can go back to prison and I print the story like you talked anyway. Jasper: You would lie and get us both killed? Karen: Your choice. Ray: Special Agent Nadeem. Foggy: Mr. Nelson. I'm glad to see you've reconsidered. The sandwich you ordered last night. Ray: I'm here to represent Matt Murdock, as his attorney. Foggy: So when I asked if you knew where Murdock was... Ray: I didn't lie. Matt contacted me today. My client's ready to submit to questioning. Foggy: That's fantastic. So, uh... where is he? Ray: I'll provide him to you tonight. After you hear the statement of a second witness who will convince you of my client's innocence. Foggy: It sounds like I'm being jerked around, counselor. Ray: His name is Jasper Evans. And you're really gonna wanna hear what he has to say.

Maggie: Hallelujah. So you can dress like a normal human being. Matt: Clean socks. Maggie: Thank you. Matt: Well, it warms my heart to see you going out to do something other than beat someone up. Maggie: How do you know? Could just be adding style to my beatings. Matt: Did you... Did you just make a joke? Maggie: You look ready to smile, which I'm sure in your case means... Well, I don't know what that could mean, as I've never actually seen one. Maggie: This have something to do with the blond who came to visit me today? Matt: Karen. Yeah. Yeah, I'm meeting her. Maggie: Wow. She's lovely. Matt: She is. Maggie: She knows you're Daredevil. Matt: She does. Maggie: And she stuck around? Sounds like a keeper. Matt: We're just friends. Maggie: Well, it's nice to hear you use the F-word. Maggie: And to see you reconnecting. Matt: Wait, I'm... She's just helping me one last time. Maggie: It's not a criticism, Matthew. Calling you an idiot... for believing that friends make you weaker rather than stronger? That would be a criticism. Matt: Thank you for clarifying that. Maggie: Anyway, where are you off to? Matt: Gotta turn myself in to the FBI. Maggie: You must be joking. Matt: You need a suit for that? Maggie: I've been falsely accused. Gotta clear my name. Matt: You mean Matt Murdock's name. If you're leaving him behind, why does it matter? Maggie: My life is complicated enough without being a wanted fugitive. And there are... other people involved. Matt: Other people? You mean your friends?

Hattley: So you've heard? Congratulations, Ray. Ray: What? Hattley: You were right. Your work with Fisk trumped your credit issues. The EAD approved your promotion. Ray: Wow, I, uh... Wow. Hattley: That's not why you're here? Ray: Murdock's lawyer just promised to surrender him tonight. Hattley: That's great. Ray: But only after we hear from a witness he claims can exonerate Murdock and prove that Fisk has been playing us. Hattley: He's bullshitting. Ray: Yeah, well, he claims his witness is Jasper Evans. Hattley: Why do I know that name? Ray: He's the guy that shanked Fisk. Hattley: That proves Murdock's attorney is bullshitting. Evans isn't giving any statements. He's in the hole. Ray: Actually, he's not. I just got off the phone with the warden. Evans is missing. Hattley: What do you mean he's missing? Ray: I mean, they've searched the prison top to bottom and he's not there. Hattley: Jesus. If Murdock's attorney has him... you don't think he's right about what Evans can prove? Ray: How can he be? Fisk's intel checks out, and we're watching him 24/7. We'd know if he was playing us. Hattley: Right. Ray: So it's a bluff. Hattley: It's a bluff. Julie: Suicide Prevention, this is Julie... Tell me, Dex, are you thinking about taking your own life right now? How are you going to do it, Dex? Do you have a gun? Mercer: Learn to stay calm. Julie: Is it in your hand? Mercer: It wasn't your fault. Julie: The world doesn't want you. I don't want you. Mercer: It wasn't your fault. Learn to stay calm. Julie: Do you have a gun? You know where to press it. Mercer: You see how alone you are? Julie: You know where to press it. Dex: Hello? Fisk: When I was in prison, my mother passed away. Among her effects was a shoebox with my name on it. A keepsake box of sorts. It was full of happy relics from my life. The gifts that I made her when I was young. The odd news clipping. And the hammer. The instrument of my father's death. Fisk: I thought that she had thrown it away. But she was proud of what I had done, of who I was. She accepted me, without shame. And that's what I want for you. Someone to accept you, without shame. I do. And I've sent you a gift, an opportunity to become your true self. And if you accept this... unlike everyone in your life, I will never abandon you. The decision is yours. Deliveryman: A car is waiting, sir, if you care to come with me.

Matt: I wanted to put some money in it, but I'm a little bit behind on my rent. Foggy: Are you sure you wanna do this? Matt: You confident this FBI agent can be trusted? Foggy: Nadeem's a ball breaker, but he seems genuinely interested in the truth. Matt: Yeah. I trust him. Foggy: Then, yeah, I'm sure. Ellison: So, I got your message. Why am I missing my wife's office party? Karen: This is Jasper Evans. He's here to go on record. He's the inmate who shanked Wilson Fisk in prison. Jasper: Fisk made me do it.

Agent: We just got the call. Murdock's at the Bulletin. Hattley: What about Jasper Evans? Agent: Nelson didn't say, but doing this at the newspaper means they want it as public as possible. Hattley: Get Murdock and find out what the hell is going on.

Ellison: The publisher and the lawyers want it all on tape. Karen: Just tell the truth, you'll be outta here soon. Just, uh, give me a minute. Karen: I know you told me lay off Fisk, but... Ellison: All right, look... Karen: We owe this to Ben. Ellison: Stop, stop, stop. I owe you... an apology. Someone has gotta shine a light on this. And, well, I'm grateful that you were brave enough to make me do it, so... thank you. Karen: Lead on. Matt: What is it? Karen: Do you hear something? Matt: Screaming. Karen: Please state your name. Jasper: My name is Jasper Evans. Karen: Good. Now, can you tell us how you know Wilson Fisk?

Ray: What the hell's going on? Matt: Foggy, find Karen. Get her outta here. Foggy: Oh, shit. This is not happening. Man 1: Great, another power outage. Man 2: Genny's kicked in. At least our work is saved. Woman: Probably another fire drill no one told us about. Man 3: That's weird. The phones are out, too. Employee: Hey, you can't be here! Ellison: Karen? What is it? What's wrong? Mercer: We prepared for this. Julie: Let go of me, Dex. I said let go! Fisk: Fashioned yourself into something the world will tolerate! Mercer: It's just you. Dex: People like you. Like us. The real you. Foggy: Karen! Karen: Jesus. Who are you? Dex: I'm Daredevil. Jasper: Stop or I'll... Ahh! Ellison: The hell are you do... Dex: Hello, Karen. It's nice to see you again. Officer: Did anyone see what happened? Check 'em. You two, with me! Karen: Oh, my God. Oh, my God. Matt? Jesus Christ. Karen: Foggy? Matt: No, no, no. He's okay. He's okay. Karen: Jesus, are you? Matt: Did he kill Jasper? Karen: Yeah. Yeah. Matt: I don't, uh... Ray: FBI, don't move! Agents down! Agents down! FBI! FBI, nobody move! Officer: What the hell happened? Who did this? Karen: It was Daredevil.

Matt: I've been staying where I grew up. Karen: There's a reason I stayed away, Karen. Matt: Yeah, if you say it was to protect me, I'm seriously gonna throw up. Karen: I can't protect you. Not from Fisk. Can't even protect myself. Matt: Sure you don't want coffee? Karen: If you wanna yell at me... go right ahead. Karen: Did I ever tell you about my old neighbor, when I was growing up? Mr. Larssen. Well, he was this nice Norwegian guy. He let his wife do his talking. But on the days when it'd get really cold— you know, and stuff would freeze, and you'd need help moving your car or, uh... unstick a door, Mr. Larssen was always there. Karen: So, one winter, his wife hit a patch of black ice. The whole town turned out for her funeral. And Mr. Larssen sat there through the sermon... and then he gathered up his casseroles and went back to work on the farm, like it was just another day. He never said a word about it. Karen: And I thought I'd go over there and be a good neighbor... see if he wanted to talk about what happened. And you know what he said? "What for?" Karen: You know what? You came to Foggy because you needed something from him. What do you need from me, Matt? Matt: Fisk staged the attack on himself in prison. That's how he, uh, tricked the FBI into moving him to a hotel. Got some lifer named Jasper Evans to shank him and then arranged for him to walk out of prison. On the books, Evans is in solitary. In reality, he's been set free. Karen: Can you prove that? Matt: Yeah, if I can find him. Get him to talk to you. Bulletin publishes the details. Fisk is exposed. And the FBI will be forced to send him back to prison. Matt: So, yeah, you're right. I came to you 'cause I needed something. Your help. What do you say? You wanna help me? Karen: No. And I'm serious about the rent.

Julie: You probably don't remember me. I'm Julie. Dex: Do you wanna hang out after? Julie: How did you know I worked there for three years? You were only there for one. Julie: Let go of me, Dex. I said let go! Mercer: Your internal compass isn't broken, Dex. It just works better with a North Star to guide you. Young Dex: What if I can't find one? Mercer: Then you'll rely on our structure. A tidy physical space. A disciplined vocation...

Ellison: This paper takes its sourcing seriously. We don't publish unverified innuendo, you know? Gossip... Ah, Ms. Page. Yeah, I'm not boring you, am I? Ellison: Anyway, in other news, our illustrious publisher, in his infinite wisdom, has decided to change our health care coverage, yet again. You should be getting your enrollment packages sometime in the next week. I've already had a look at it. My advice to you is, try not to get sick. Uh, any questions?

Karen: It's total bullshit. I can't believe Matt would even ask. Foggy: But I still think you should help him. Karen: Oh, come on. Foggy: Just hear me out.
