You agree to write the article on one condition. Matt turns himself in to the FBI. Karen: What? No. Foggy: They're only up in our chili because they're looking for Matt. Once they have him... Karen: But he can't. He'll never agree to it. Foggy: There's no reason to think the FBI knows anything about Matt's other life. But if he can give 'em that witness, Matt's in the clear. So we all are. I could reach out as Matt's attorney and negotiate his surrender. Karen: Okay, but I'm not ready to forgive him. Foggy: I get it. You know, you shouldn't be either. I mean, he... he stole your identity, he made you a target. Foggy: Has Matt been a shitty friend lately? Without a doubt. But, deep down, I think it's hurting him as much as it's hurting us. Karen: How do you figure? Foggy: Because he could've gone to any reporter, Karen, but he came to you. Maybe Matt's finally coming to his senses. But even if he isn't, the way he's been treating us lately is on him. Us turning our backs would be on us. Foggy: People have bailed on Matt his whole life, and I'm not gonna be one of 'em. You do what you want, but... that's not the kind of friend I wanna be. Karen: It's like you argue for a living or something. Foggy: Was it too much? It felt like too much. Karen: Matt said he was staying at the place where he grew up. Do you know where that is?

Dex: Don't you look pretty today. Julie: You know you're two hours early, right? Dex: Yeah, the, uh, the neighbors kept me up. Julie: Again? Shit. You gotta move. Or get them into couples therapy. Julie: If those were my neighbors, I'd go over there and give them a piece of my mind. Julie: Do you think a killer like that deserves a second chance? Mercer: Your internal compass isn't broken, Dex. It just works better with a North Star to guide you. Julie: Let go of me, Dex. I said let go! Mercer: Then you'll rely on our structure. A tidy physical space. A disciplined... Julie: Do you wanna hang out after? Dex: Yeah. Julie: Where'd you go? Dex: It's feeding time. Julie: You know, I, uh... I got it. Dex: You sure? You're not even on the clock yet. Julie: Yeah, I could use a decent cup of coffee. You mind going downstairs and grabbing me one? And I'll feed the animal. Dex: He's all yours.

Dex: I don't know what strings you had to pull to get that waitress a job, but it was a waste of your time. Yeah, they train us in counterintel at Quantico. You really think I'm gonna fall for some bush-league honey trap? Dex: You got it in your head that she means something to me. But she doesn't. She doesn't mean shit to me. So what? You... You have me tailed for a few days, you think you know me? Think you got me dialed? You don't, all right? You don't know anything about me. Dex: Say something! Fisk: When I was a boy... I... beat my father's skull in with a hammer. I was 12 years old. Young for my age, in fact. Terribly inexperienced. I'd never been to a dance with a girl or... stayed up past midnight. Never been out of the city or even taken the subway on my own. Fisk: Yet there I was... twelve years old... standing over my father's body... watching him die by my hand. That feeling. That moment. I sense it's something you're familiar with. Fisk: You... were taught to hide beneath many fictions. You fashioned yourself into something the world would tolerate. A soldier doing his patriotic duty. A sniper in the FBI. The watchful companion of a nice young woman. Dex: You destroyed what we had. Fisk: If it were honest and true, no one could've destroyed it. Dex: I should've let you die. Fisk: Stay back. Fisk: Julie never would've understood you. And society won't either. It punishes people like you. Like us.

Fisk: Julie never would've understood you. The real you. She never would've understood the real you. And society won't either. It punishes people like you. Like us. Alvarez: It's all over the papers. Dex? Dex? Dex! Dex: What? Alvarez: They're throwing you under the bus. I'm sorry, Dex. It isn't right.

Fisk: The painting that's intended for this wall is something I am specially attached to. Lee: Of course. Rabbit in a Snowstorm. Yes, the agreement. It said I was to get all my belongings restored to me. Donovan: Precisely. And we might be able to use this violation of terms to lobby the feds for something else. Fisk: The painting! That's what I'm interested in. Donovan: I can assure you we're doing everything in our power, but... there's a challenge to your ownership claim. Fisk: It comes home. Do you understand? Guard: Lawyer's out! Cameras back on! Agent: Wellers, we have a situation. Report to the CP. Wellers: Shit. Agent: Inside. Shut the door. Fisk: Show them to me. Woman: All units on the citywide, NYPD... Doyle: Shit. Are you hearing this? What happened at the Bulletin? We should be there, not stuck here with this asshole. Wellers: He go to bed? Doyle: Turned in early. Nice and cozy, while the world explodes.

Marci: Foggy? Foggy, baby, are you okay? Because I don't think you're okay. Foggy: Oh. I'm... I'm fine. I think I know what Fisk is up to. Paxton: Hello? Karen: Hi, Dad. It's me. Paxton: Karen? Good Lord. I heard something on the news. That wasn't where you work, was it? Karen: Yeah. Yeah, it was. I'm okay, though. I was thinking that maybe I could come home for a little while. Paxton: I don't know. I'm afraid the timing is not great. Karen: Yeah. Of course. I get it. Paxton: But you can call anytime, all right? Karen: Dad... I was just trying to do the right thing. It just... It went all wrong. Paxton: That's what you do, Karen. Good night. Ray: I'm not asking for prisoner files. All I want is footage from the security cameras. Copies. I'll even pay for them. We're supposed to be on the same side here. All I want to do is see exactly what happened when Fisk got shanked. Well, you have him call me as soon as he gets in. Understand? I'll... asshole.

All: Surprise! Ray: Wow. Seema: Congratulations on your promotion, nuuri. Ray: Thanks, everyone. Hey, bud. Come here. Sorry I'm late. Seema: Ray, you make every single person in this room so proud. Proud of the man you are and who you strive to be. For the example you set for our son. For the husband and friend we adore. And for being the man who hogs more blankets at night than is humanly possible. Seema: But even with that, you've always been the person to warm my heart. Congratulations on your well-deserved promotion. Man: Cheers. Woman: Congratulations. Seema: I love you. Ray: I love you. Sami: Eww. Ray: Way to kill the moment, buddy. Sami: Mom, we're out of soda. Seema: There's plenty in the fridge downstairs. Ray: I'll get it. Seema: I need a moment with you first. Ray: What? Seema: I told you, everything is fine. Ray: You lied to me. Seema: I called you, afraid for your life, and you lied. I have to hear from Annie Wellers what really happened? That that murderer attacked you and that you shot him? Ray: Seems... Seema: I have to hear it from her? Ray: I didn't want you to worry. Seema: Well, I am worried. I'm worried what this job is doing to you, to us. Ray: What's that supposed to mean? Seema: I will always have your back. To them. To everyone. But I'm not an idiot. Ray: I didn't say you are. Seema: When you lie to my face, you do. Ray: You're right. I'm just trying to keep everything together. I don't want to screw any of this up. I worked so hard for this, for us. How... How can I fix this? Seema: You can start with telling me the truth. And by getting more drinks. Ray: Who are you? Matt: I'm Daredevil. The real one. Ray: You don't look like... Matt: I buried the red suit. The man who attacked the Bulletin, he resurrected it. Ray: You do, however, match the description of a guy who's been tuning up FBI agents. Matt: Which is the last thing I ever wanted, but you people haven't left me any choice. If you'd just wake the hell up instead of playing right into Fisk's hands. He's using you, and I think you know it. Now, I heard you confront that psycho at the Bulletin. I heard you try to stop him, and he almost killed you, too. So let me ask you this, Agent Nadeem... Who do you think is the danger here? Me... or him? Sami: Dad, Mom wants to know where you are. Ray: Don't come down, Sami. I dropped a beer, there's glass. Tell your mom I need a couple of minutes to clean it up. Sami: Okay. Ray: Let's say I believe the guy that just broke into my house. Let's just say that. What do you got? Matt: The man who attacked the Bulletin dressed as Daredevil... he's in the FBI. Ray: Keep talking.

News Anchor: And now the news, Mrs. Shelby. ...rushed to nearby hospitals in critical condition. But what we do know is that, according to several eyewitnesses, the brutal attack on the Bulletin staff has been carried out by none other than Daredevil. The word from the witnesses we've spoken with is that Daredevil, Hell's Kitchen's renowned vigilante, is the perpetrator. ...they don't know the whereabouts of Daredevil or whether... This brutal act hits Hell's Kitchen after a period of relative calm in the city, with the FBI arresting many of New York's...

Matt: You're missing the point. He didn't just find someone to wear my suit. Someone as fast and skilled as I've ever seen, and I couldn't take him. He found someone to kill me. Lantom: Matthew... Matt: I was stupid enough to think that I had Fisk cornered. He knew I'd find the witness, and I just brought the sheep to slaughter. Jasper Evans is dead. He's dead and he leaves a son behind, and that's on me! I was so sure that I finally was out in front of this bastard. And Fisk, he knew I thought that. He was waiting for me. Lantom: Matthew... Matt: Foggy and Karen both could've been killed. And there would have been nothing I could have done to stop it. Nothing. Lantom: You're losing blood. I need to stitch you up. Matt: I listened to you. I listened to you, and they almost died. God damn it. I'm such an idiot. Lantom: No. I'm the idiot. I told you to involve your friends, and I made things worse. I'm used to putting on a brave face when people bring their troubles to the church. And I find that they don't just bring their troubles, they bring their answers, too, if you let them talk enough. But... what you're dealing with is so far beyond my experience that... Well... all I can hope to do is help keep your wounds stitched and your head clear, so you can be safe. And I'll be more careful about giving advice to the Devil. And, occasionally, possibly, I'll try to keep my mouth shut. Matt: Could I get that in writing? Look, I know you were just trying to help. Now, can I please see to those wounds? Matt: Can I ask you something? Lantom: Yeah. Lantom: What if you stopped this fight, took time to heal... and let other people like you go after Fisk? Matt: This isn't their fight. Fisk is my problem. Lantom: Sorry. Matt: It's okay. The problem is, he's always five steps ahead of me. I don't know if I can beat him. And I don't know if I can beat the man he sent to kill me. Lantom: You won't know for certain till you find him. Matt: I thought you were gonna keep your thoughts to yourself. Lantom: You really want me to do that? Matt: No. Lantom: If he was wearing a copy of your Devil suit... Well, he didn't get it at Sears. How good a copy was it? Matt: It was perfect.

Dex: Hello, Karen. It's nice to see you again. Ray: Was there anyone else in the room named Karen? Or on the whole Bulletin staff? Foggy: I'm advising my client not to answer any questions that treat her like an asshole. Ray: There was not. He was talking to you. Why don't we watch it again? See... Karen: No. He was talking to me. That's true. Ray: Okay. Good. Karen: But I've never met him before. Ray: Well, according to your own newspaper, you've met Daredevil at least twice. Karen: That psycho's not Daredevil. Ray: I got a pretty good look at him, too. Karen: Could have fooled me. Ray: Do you think every fat guy with a white beard and red suit is Santa Claus? Foggy: If he comes down my chimney and leaves presents under the tree. Karen: Exactly. If he acted like Santa. This guy doesn't act like Daredevil. Ray: Based on your two encounters? Karen: Dig a little deeper. Why don't you read everything? He doesn't kill people, ever. It's not Daredevil. Ray: So you keep saying. Did you ever look into Felix Manning? Red Lion Bank? Any of the leads that I dropped in your lap? Karen: They're on my to-do list. Foggy: This is bullshit. Ray: He dropped your name, Ms. Page. Used your gun to murder someone. And in this entire shitshow, you're the one person he didn't lay a finger on. So I'm sorry that you think that this is bullshit, but something doesn't add up. So we're gonna keep going over this until it does. Karen: It's not gonna add up until you start asking the right questions. Ray: How about this one? Where's Matt Murdock? Foggy: Yet another fine example of a question that's besides the friggin' point! Ray: You were supposed to deliver him, Mr. Nelson. But there are zero Matt Murdocks in my custody. Zero Jasper Evans left alive. Think that's random? He kills the one guy with dirt on Fisk. You know that already? Is that why you don't wanna go there? Karen: Karen... Foggy: What? Karen: That psycho in a suit did Agent Nadeem a huge favor. Now there's no one left to tell the world what a fool Fisk is making of the FBI. Ray: Did you know Daredevil was gonna attack the Bulletin? Is that why you brought your gun last night? Foggy: Okay. We're done here.

Foggy: Are you okay? Karen: No, I'm definitely not okay. Karen: None of the people who own those phones are okay, either. Foggy: Come on. Let's go. Karen: No... I don't get it. You... You almost died. That doesn't leave a mark? Foggy: I don't have time to think about that. Right now, Agent Nadeem's got all my attention. If he digs into Jasper Evans, he'll know we're telling the truth about Fisk. Then he'll dig into the rest of it. I hope. Karen: I did this. Foggy: Wilson Fisk did this. Karen: Evans wouldn't have come to the Bulletin if I hadn't threatened his son. Foggy: This isn't on you. And this isn't the time to give up the fight. We need to find Matt... Karen: No. Um... I'm gonna go to the hospital. Foggy: Are you hurt? Karen: I'm the only one who wasn't. Foggy: Marci. I should take this. She's worried. Hey, babe. Yeah, I'm okay. I'm fine. I know. I'm sorry, it's just been crazy. The time has... Ray: Seema, I'm fine. Really, I... Seems, I wasn't even there. I got there after it was all over. That's right. I'll be home tonight, okay? Ray: Oh, shit. That's tonight? No. No, no. Don't cancel. Um... It'll be good to see the family. And good for Sami, you know? And let him know everything really is all right. I love you, too.

Matt: Where is he? Betsy: Damn, it's cold out here. Melvin: You got your hat? I could get your hat. Betsy: No, Melvin, it's okay. I'm in the office today. Melvin: Okay. I made you cheese and pickles. Betsy: Thanks, love. Melvin: You got your gun? Betsy: Of course. Right here. Melvin: What's going on? You've been acting strange all morning. Melvin: I... worry about you. Betsy: Because I hang out with paroled cons like you? Melvin: 'Cause they're not like me. Betsy: I can take care of myself, big man. You be good today. I'll make asopao for dinner. Melvin: Okay. Love you.

Matt: Betsy's your parole officer. Melvin: Please don't tell anyone. It's against the rules. Matt: I don't care what you do with Betsy, Melvin. You know why I'm here. Melvin: Fisk made me make the suit. Matt: Did that man hurt you? Melvin: I'm sorry. Matt: Who was he? Melvin: He didn't tell me his name. But I can make you a new one... to protect you against him. It'd be a fair fight. Matt: I don't want the suit anymore. Melvin: You don't like it? Matt: I've outgrown what it stood for. Melvin: When you made my suit, there were molds, measurements. At the workshop, maybe there's something. Matt: I've been to the workshop. It's been burned down. Melvin: I was forced to throw everything away. I didn't want to. I'm sorry. Matt: Who forced you? Melvin: I can't tell you. I'm sorry. Matt: Melvin, you know how this goes. You know what I need from you. Melvin: I thought making him his own suit would get Fisk out of your lives and mine. He didn't need me to remake yours. He just wanted it. Matt: I need to see the FBI agent. Melvin: If I help you, Betsy dies. Matt: She's already dead. The second Fisk gets what he wants from you, he'll kill you both. Melvin: He promised. Matt: He promised me, too. And look what he's doing to me. Melvin: I won't help you. Not if it means she gets hurt. Matt: I need that name, Melvin. Melvin: Please don't make me do this. Matt: Is he coming? Tell me who wore the suit! I will find him. I will put an end to this. Melvin: I can't. Fisk will know. And he'll hurt Betsy. Matt: If you really loved her, you'd cut her loose. This life doesn't work with Betsys. Melvin: I can't let you leave! Melvin: Someone's coming. Matt: I'm not supposed to be here. Melvin: It's the FBI, Melvin. Why would Fisk send... Matt: They're supposed to find you with the suit. Melvin: Oh, God. Matt: He's framing me for being Daredevil. Oh, God. Melvin, come on, he's tricking you. Melvin: Please. Betsy's all I have. Matt: Once Fisk has me, he will kill you both. Melvin: Oh, man. Matt: You gotta help me, or Betsy's dead. Who did you make the suit for? Melvin: He never told me his name... but he was an FBI agent. Matt: How do you know that? Melvin: He was talking about it with the man who brought him. Agent 1: Breach. Breach. Breach. Agent 2: FBI! Don't move! Go! Go! Go! Agent 2: Stop fighting, or we'll shoot! Agent 3: Hands behind your head. Melvin: Please! I gotta get to her! Agent 3: On your knees. On your knees! Melvin: Betsy! He'll hurt Betsy!

Agent: He asleep? Wellers: Been in bed all night. Ray: I need to talk to him. Wellers: You want company? Ray: No. I got it. Manning: Potter's in custody. Should we alter his situation or his girlfriend's? Fisk: No. He's irrelevant now. Where is Poindexter? Manning: Laying low, as ordered. Although, I'm concerned about his mental stability. Fisk: Yeah. I've demanded a lot from him. You keep an eye on him. But let him be for now. Fisk: We need to talk. Ray: You're working late. Shouldn't you be with your family? Seema, isn't it? Fisk: Say her name again and see what happens. Ray: What can I help you with? Fisk: Help me. You know, you remind me of someone I knew growing up. Jack Kem. Yeah, but everyone knew him as Jiggy. You know, Jiggy lived in a two-family house all by himself. It was practically a mansion to me. But Jiggy was a helper, too. He was always helping out folks on the block. Annie the single mom needs a new car. Jiggy's got it. The Hoffmans are desperate for rent. No problem. Ten-year-old me thought this guy was a hero. But it turned out Jiggy had hidden ten kilos of heroin in the trunk of Annie's sedan. Another five in the Hoffman baby's room. Guess who the cops arrested when they tracked down that powder? Fisk: I've seen your kind of help before. Ray: Have a little faith in me, Special Agent Nadeem. I'm a better man than Jiggy. This... All of this... This was my price, which I was plain about at the start of our relationship. And you have paid it. Fisk: I need to know. Right now. You let Jasper Evans out of prison to pay him back for shanking you? Ray: Your desperation diminishes you, Special Agent. Good night. Fisk: "The Hero of Hell's Kitchen Feeds a Simpleton to the Feds." Won't that make a hell of a headline for tomorrow's Bulletin? Matt: Melvin made his choice. Fisk: Yet you did hesitate before you left. Were you waiting for a messenger from the Lord to stop you, like he stopped Abraham from killing his son? Were you disappointed no messenger arrived... or relieved that you didn't have to risk your life for a weak-minded criminal? You're not strong enough to beat the man I sent for you. You're not smart enough to beat me. You couldn't do it alone. You couldn't do it with your friends. Your father never knew when to lay down. He was too proud. You will die the same way. Betsy: Please, Betsy, don't do me like this. I wasn't the one who violated parole. You did this to yourself. Matt: Betsy. Matt: Don't. I'm not here to hurt you. I'm here about Melvin. Betsy: Melvin Potter? Matt: He's been arrested. Betsy: Bullshit. Matt: He's not gonna tell anyone about your relationship, but that's not what you need to worry about. You need to worry about Wilson Fisk. Betsy: Oh, shit. Damn it, Melvin. Matt: Fisk doesn't leave loose ends. He will kill you. Don't go home. Don't go back to work. Leave town. Betsy: What about Melvin? Is he okay? Matt: You can't help Melvin. He made his bed when he went back to work for Fisk. Betsy: You're a cold piece of work, aren't you? Melvin told me about the Devil of Hell's Kitchen. He thought you were a hero. I told him assholes like you and Fisk are cut from the same cloth and both of you would take advantage of Melvin because he has a good heart and a trusting way! Matt: You've been warned, Betsy. You want to live? Run.

Matt: Who are you? Dex: I'm Daredevil. Man: Hey, you can't be here! Dex: Hello, Karen. It's nice to see you again. I'm Daredevil. Mercer: Your internal compass isn't broken, Dex. It just works better with a North Star to guide you. Young Dex: What if I can't find one? Mercer: Then you'll rely on our structure. A tidy physical space. A disciplined vocation. You will build your life on pillars of order.

Foggy: What? What? Karen: Foggy? Foggy: Think of it as a compliment. That they actually thought I would try to kill him? Karen: I had to tell them something. Foggy: No, Foggy, you didn't. You ruined it. I had him. Karen: Had him? Fisk would snap you like a twig. Foggy: At least they'd have it on video. Karen: Was that really your plan? God damn it, Karen. Don't turn into Matt on me. Foggy: Look, I didn't want him to kill me. Just come after me. Karen: Oh, good. Foggy: Well, I got the idea from you. Karen: Me? Foggy: All that talk about Tower and catching him off guard, and I thought, "Yeah, just get Fisk to stop thinking and reacting emotionally instead." I figured you were thinking something like that. Karen: Not a bad plan, actually. Except for the part where you have to hope the FBI comes in before that monster beats you to death. Foggy: Well, it doesn't matter now, does it? Foggy: How did you even know I was here? Karen: I know you. When you didn't come— I thought of some possibilities and this was my nightmare scenario. So I pretty much counted on it. Foggy: At least I took my shot. Karen: You took a shot. Tomorrow, there's gonna be an army shooting back.

Agent: The report, for your insurance. Ray: Thank you. Fisk: Come with me. Ray: Yeah, yeah, another late one. I know, babe, but they're filing charges against the Albanians tomorrow, and I never reviewed my account. Yeah, I'm not gonna make it home tonight. Kiss Sami for me. I love you, too. Ray: Boss. Nadeem. Sorry to wake you. We need to talk.

location: PRESIDENTIAL HOTEL - FISK'S SECRET ART ROOM
scene_text: Fisk: After you. Dex: This was here the whole time? Fisk: Yes. We, um— I have a problem. Dex: Nadeem knows. Fisk: I know he does. We will take care of the problem. Fisk: Dex— rage cannot stay inside. It needs to go somewhere or it becomes a poison. It will kill you from within. I find that when this rage cannot stay buried in me for one more second— that a primal scream is the only satisfying release. Dex: Yes. Yeah. Young Dex: I like making things happen without anybody knowing it's me who did it. Mercer: Let's do our exercise. Close your eyes.

Matt: He didn't have any parents. Young Dex: I'm digging a hole. Matt: Spent a lot of time fighting. Young Dex: Buried my anger in the ground. Mercer: Good. Matt: Angry. Mercer: Now cover it with dirt. Young Dex: Okay. But, Dr. Mercer? Mercer: Go ahead and say it. Young Dex: I want to open the box. Lantom: I promised to keep my mouth shut. But you want to say it sounds familiar. Matt: Does it? Lantom: I didn't have anyone either, but I'm nothing like him. The tapes make it sound like he was a killer at a young age. The guy's a psychopath. And I had a chance today. A shot to catch him off guard, and I blew it. Lantom: You did what you thought was right. You kept your word to Agent Nadeem. Matt: Yeah. And how many people will die because of it? I don't know if I have the strength to get through this. Maggie: He's so stubborn. Full of fury and foolish pride. Please watch over him. Keep him from making the same damned mistake that took you from us. Our son is too much like you, Jack. Matt: Mom? Maggie: Mom. No.

Matt: If you'd just wake the hell up instead of playing right into Fisk's hands. Lim: Morning. Agent: Morning, boss. Matt: He's using you and I think you know it. So let me ask you this, Agent Nadeem— Who do you think is the danger here? The man who attacked the Bulletin dressed as Daredevil— he's in the FBI. Dex: Hello, Karen. It's nice to see you again.

Man: Hey! Julie! Dex: Dex, stay away from me. Julie: Please, just hear me out. I'm doing this in public so you'll feel safe. I'll stay right here. I'm not coming any closer. Dex: Okay. I am so, so sorry about how things ended the other night. I'm sorry for scaring you. I just wanted to explain myself. When we worked together at the suicide hotline, I saw the way you were with other people. Patient, compassionate, and I— I really need that right now. My life is out of control. I have no family, and I'm about to lose my job— Please. I just want to talk. Anywhere you choose. And if you say no, I'll understand and I'll never bother you again.

Matt: Agent Nadeem. Ray: You're late. Matt: I was early, but I needed to be sure about you. Ray: What's his name? Matt: Yeah, well, I need to be sure about you, too. You have a history of hurting people. I'm not handing you a federal agent if you're gonna kill him. Ray: I don't do that. Matt: The agents you beat up the other day? One of them is still in the hospital. All of them just doing their jobs. Ray: If they'd arrested me, there'd be no one to take down Fisk. Matt: If you're right about him, taking Fisk down is our job. Ray: Oh, really? Because we both know where he's sleeping these days. But I understand. If there's one thing we agree on, Nadeem, it's the greater good. Like house incarceration in exchange for good intel. Sometimes you and I have to hurt one person to save another. So what's his name? Matt: I need your word that you won't touch him. Ray: My word can't mean anything to you. Matt: But I need to hear you give it. Ray: Well, I need him to testify against Fisk, so you got it. Matt: We're gonna slip into his place. Look for any evidence that ties him to the Bulletin attack or to Fisk. If we find any, we leave it where it is. And we set off his fire alarm on our way out. The fire department arrives, and you circumvent a search warrant. But if we don't find anything, the guy goes on with his life. Ray: Spit it out. Who is he? Matt: Special Agent Ben Poindexter. Dex: A small decaf and whatever she's having. Julie: I've got mine. Thanks. Richie: My regular, Richie. Richie: All right. Dex: So, I don't know how to say this without it sounding like an insult. I was never actually into you. Or not the way you might have been thinking, anyway. I didn't know how to talk to you. Julie: Okay. Dex: I wasn't— I wasn't stalking you. Although, I completely see how it could have come across that way. I just— I wanted to be more like you. Julie: Do you realize how creepy that still sounds? Dex: You are so good. And kind. And— You save lives as your job. The FBI, the army before that— they helped keep me on the straight and narrow path. But now, without that, it's all— I'm drowning in deep water, and I don't know whether I'm swimming for the surface or the bottom. Julie: Dex, you need air. Breathe. Dex: See, that's— that's what I'm talking about. You help people right themselves. I've seen you do it a hundred times. All I'm asking, just treat me like someone on the other end of the line. Julie: What happened at the FBI? Dex: The bureau needed a scapegoat. Julie: You know, what you really need is a good therapist. Dex: I had one. She died. Julie: Oh, I— I'm so sorry. Julie: Okay. I'll help you, Dex. But, please, do not make me regret this. Dex: I promise. Promise I will not. Julie: Excuse me. Foggy: Hi. Whoa! Did you get any sleep at all? Karen: Yeah. No. Foggy: You need coffee. Karen: Yeah. You ever have one of those days where you're just, like— You break it down, step by step? Just, uh— "Put your feet on the floor, Karen. Just get to the sink." Foggy: Sure. Generally speaking, I don't call myself Karen, but— Actually, no, I don't do any of that. Karen: How are you not at the bottom of a bottle right now? Foggy: Because I have a theory. Karen: Jeez. Must be a hell of a theory. Foggy: Fisk is giving up criminals involved in corruption. He's planning to step into the void and become the sole source of government protection for all criminals in Hell's Kitchen, maybe the city. Karen: And that theory makes you want to not drink? Foggy: Yes, because I also have a plan. Karen: No. No, no, Foggy, you don't have a plan. Do you know what happens when you make a plan? Fisk has already thought of it, and he's made it part of his plan. Foggy: Except he has no idea that I'm onto him. He couldn't. I discovered this while looking into Marci's briefs. More ways than one. Karen: Foggy. Foggy: Sorry. The point is she was prepping for a deposition of a corrupt IRS official who was providing fraud and money laundering services for the Albanians— Karen: No, stop. I can't. Foggy: Just one more article, Karen. That's all it'll take. Karen: All right. What's this? Foggy: The terms of Fisk's house incarceration. If he violates any of these, zappo. He's back in prison. Karen: "Zappo"? Is that a thing? Foggy: Number three is the key. "Committing or conspiring to commit a felony." Karen: No, no, wait. What about number six here? All this stuff about being charged with a crime that predates the agreement? Foggy: Number six is not the plan. Karen: We have a good number six. I mean, Fisk killed his father. That's murder. There's no statute of limitations. And his mother told Ben Urich about it. Foggy: A dead woman told a dead guy something. That's not proof. It won't stick. Karen: Yeah. You know what will? Publicizing my theory. So the FBI sees that Fisk has violated his agreement, they're forced to put him back in prison? Foggy: And they can't ignore it if we splash it across the front page. And by "we," I mean you. Karen: The Bulletin won't just let a journalist make unsubstantiated claims. That's not news. Foggy: But it is news if a candidate running for district attorney makes unsubstantiated claims. In a public forum. Debating the incumbent DA. Karen: You're gonna debate Blake Tower? Foggy: At the Hell's Kitchen Club. Well, it's supposed to be prepared remarks. Karen: Huh. Foggy: They're endorsing him. I'm not actually on the agenda, but Nelson's Meats is a member of the club, so— Karen: You're just gonna confront him, out of the blue? Foggy: Why not? I'll catch him when he's not expecting it. Throw this stuff at him— Karen: Yeah, you get him worked up, emotional. Provoke him. It could work. Foggy: Yup. So, you'll cover the meeting? Karen: Yeah, I would. I just, um— I lost my job. Foggy: So— What? Ellison loves you like family. What did you do? Karen: I refused to give him Daredevil's identity. Foggy: Yikes. Okay, well, Ellison wants Fisk as badly as we do. Just tell him our plan. Watch how fast he gives you your job back. Then we'll hook up at the dinner later. You're my plus one. I got you the salmon.

Julie: Hey. Did the landlord let you in? Julie: Dex. Thanks for coming. Dex: You made it pretty clear I had to. Julie: What's this about? Julie: I have someone here who wants to talk to you. Follow me. Julie: Dex, this is my old friend Andrea Morales. She's an attorney. The guys took up a collection to pay for Andy's services. Now if you're up for it, she's going to sue the bureau for wrongful suspension on your behalf. Dex: She can do that? Morales: I can. And having reviewed the details of your case, I fully believe that I should. She's on a retainer. Starting now. And I'm not cheap. The guys must really like you, Agent Poindexter. Dex: You've had my back through all this? I don't know how to thank you. Ray: The guy that saved our lives doesn't ever have to thank us for anything. Well, figure out the next steps, and, uh— I can't wait to have you back on the team. Morales: I've prepared the argument.

Ray: You find anything? Matt: I don't know. Too much to look through. Ray: We're running out of time. Matt: He keeps his apartment obsessively clean. A place for everything, everything in its place. His shoes all face the same direction. The hangers are an inch and a half apart. Ray: Okay. So the guy's fastidious. Matt: He's not fastidious. He's methodical. Compulsive. Ray: So he's a psychopath. Matt: He's something. Fisk knows it and is using it. Ray: Well, if we can't find anything here— Matt: Wait. This is different. A box of things that don't match the rest. Sentimental stuff. Ray: A dead woman? Matt: Dr. Eileen Mercer. Died six months ago. Heart attack. She was his therapist. These are therapy tapes. Hundreds of them, going back decades. Ray: Is there one dated around the Bulletin attack? Matt: Yeah. Right here. Mercer: How was your week? Dex: I did a bad thing. Mercer: Tell me about it. Ray: Hold on. Play that back. Matt: What? Ray: Just play it. Dex: I did a bad thing. Ray: That's him. That's him at the Bulletin. Same voice. Matt: Let's get out of here. Pull the alarm. Let the fire department find this. Ray: No. These are privileged. Even with a warrant, we can't use them. Matt: So we take them. Ray: That's illegal. Matt: You've already broken in. Ray: But I haven't stolen anything. Not yet. Matt: Nadeem, we can't just leave them here. Ray: We made a deal. Matt: And Fisk will get away with everything. Ray: I'm not gonna send an innocent man to prison based on stolen evidence. Matt: He is not innocent! Ray: Then we find another way to prove it.

Tower: Thank you. Thank you all very much. I appreciate your faith in my tenure as district attorney, and I'm honored to accept the club's endorsement for my reelection. Now, I have some prepared remarks— Foggy: Mr. Tower, before you begin, I have a question for you. Tower: Mr. Nelson, this is not a debate. It's a speech. Foggy: I understand, but the members of this club deserve to know where you stand on Wilson Fisk. Tower: I stand exactly where I did when I prosecuted him. Foggy: So you're opposed to his release? Tower: Of course I am. But it's a federal matter. It's out of my hands. Foggy: Is it? Because Fisk is using the government as his private army to reclaim his position at the center of this city's criminal underworld. Tower: This is fantasy. Foggy: No, it's a harsh reality. There are government officials who are controlled by various criminals. What Wilson Fisk has done is take all those criminals and turn them over to the FBI. And keep all those corrupt officials for himself. He's planning to turn himself into a one-stop shop for bribery and protection. It's all right here. Tower: Mr. Nelson. As district attorney, you can't just pander to a crowd. You have to prove your case. Foggy: I can. Tower: No, you can't. My turn. At your fancy law firm, what they teach is, "Create a fiction." What story does a jury need to hear? Not what facts. I have been prosecuting for 13 years, and I can tell you this is not how criminal law works. Moving speeches impress a crowd, but they don't stand up in criminal court. Foggy: I don't have your experience, Mr. Tower. It's true. But then again, I'm not jaded from doing the same thing for too many years, either. I'm still passionate about what the law can do. And that's a very powerful tool to work with. Because when you get beyond the cold facts and really get worked up about what you're doing, you can— Holy shit. Tower: I can't hear you. You can do what, Mr. Nelson? Freeze up in front of a jury? Karen: We'll be watching. Foggy: You gotta be kidding me.

Fisk: Ms. Page. I must admit, I'm surprised you're here. Karen: I suppose this qualifies as hard time? Fisk: Yes, I'm sure all of this is offensive to you, given our personal history. Karen: You mean the times you tried to have me killed? Fisk: Crimes for which I'm still paying. Yes. It's offensive. Fisk: Tea? Karen: No, thank you. I'm not here for tea. Fisk: Sit down. You came for words, at least. Karen: Yeah. Let's— Let's have some words. Fisk: You are not writing an article about my mother. Karen: I'm not? Fisk: I could. Karen: To what end, Ms. Page? My distress? Fisk: Hmm. Doesn't actually sound that bad, now that you say it. Karen: I do not welcome intrusions into my privacy. Fisk: Yet you invited me in? Karen: You worked for Ben Urich, didn't you? I believe he mentored you. Fisk: Yes, before he was murdered. Karen: A final lesson. One you seem not to have understood. Fisk: Is that a threat? Karen: It's an observation. Fisk: Well, you're right. I'm not here to talk about your mother. I'd rather talk about what she told Ben. Actually, really, rather, what she told us. See, I don't think you know, but I was with him. It probably wasn't fair. Two trained journalists working on a feeble old woman like that. It's easy to push her. Get her to say things she doesn't want to. Fisk: Your point? Karen: She remembered a lot about your childhood. They say the oldest memories stick around the longest. She remembered a lot of little things. A lot of embarrassing things. Seems like there were a lot of those, weren't there, Willie? Fisk: I'm sure your readers at the Bulletin will be as entertained as you are. Karen: No, we would never print those. We just pass them around the office. How is it around your office? I heard about your misfortune. Fisk: Before it even happened, I'm sure. Karen: No, the story that we will print is her very detailed description of your father. And how you murdered him. Karen: A hammer. At that age? Is there any part of you that isn't broken, I wonder? Fisk: You asked me why I let you in. The reason is, Ms. Page, I have a few questions of my own. You are a respected journalist, but at one time you were merely a secretary at a law firm. To Matt Murdock, yes? Karen: Office manager. Fisk: Intimately involved in his affairs, huh? Karen: His business affairs. Fisk: Of course. Tell me, so at what point did you learn about Mr. Murdock's secret life? Karen: Yeah. Thank you. Thank you, Ms. Page. Karen: Okay. Okay. You want secrets? I can tell you a secret, Wilson. Okay if I call you that? I feel like we know each other well enough by now. Fisk: As you wish, Karen. Karen: Great. James Wesley. What was it like for you when he disappeared? Really, it's those first 24 hours that are the worst, aren't they? When you call and you call and you call, and there's just no answer. It becomes an obsession. The calling. The never-ending loop of a ghost's voice mail in your ear. You worry. You wonder. You swear, "God damn it, if he's still living, I'm gonna kill him myself." Is that what it was like for you? Did you rage at him? 'Cause you thought he betrayed you? Because I wonder what would be worse for you. His duplicity or his death? Karen: He died quickly. If you were wondering. Didn't suffer much. You see, Wilson, Matt Murdock isn't the person you should be worried about. I killed Wesley. I shot him seven times. Because the clip ran out. He deserved more. Wellers: Don't move!
Lantom: That's $80.00. Unless you want to go double or nothing. Man: You hustling me, grandpa? Lantom: You tell me.

Foggy: I don't have your experience, Mr. Tower. It's true. But then again, I'm not jaded from doing the same thing for too many years, either. I'm still passionate about what the law can do. Theo: Maybe a haircut next time, though. Rosalind: He's making quite the name for himself. Edward: Theo, you gotta see this movie your brother's in. Rosalind: Let me fix you a plate, sweetie. Come here. Theo: Hold on, Ma. I need a couple minutes with Foggy. I'll be quick. Rosalind: Don't worry about her, Foggy. She'll be fine. Aunt Anna: So, Marci, have you considered freezing your eggs? It's never too late. Edward: Anna!

Theo: This better be important. All that stuff you said about Fisk on the video, you gotta take it back. Foggy: What are you talking about? Theo: You have to make a different video, man. Issue a statement or whatever. Say you were drunk. Foggy: Au contraire, mon frère. That's the last thing I gotta do. I gotta exploit this opportunity to expose everything Fisk is doing. Theo: No, no, no. Foggy, listen to me. You need to apologize. Foggy: What happened? Did someone come after you, Theo? Theo: Fog, it's real bad. About a year ago, some of our suppliers stopped taking our orders. Just stopped. No reason I could understand. We couldn't change their minds for the love of money. After a few months, the shop was in a tight spot financially, right? And we didn't have the collateral to get a loan... Foggy: Why didn't you come to me? I could have helped. Theo: I didn't have to, because of what happened next. Out of the blue, I get this call from a bank I never heard of offering to help us out. Red Lion Bank. Foggy: Shit. Theo: You know these guys? Foggy: Just keep going. Theo: So, the loan officer there, he coaches me on how to move the numbers around. Make our assets look healthier, you know. And bam! The loan comes through without a hitch. I don't give it another thought. Life goes on. I mean, we've been through a lot around here. Foggy: And the old suppliers came back. Theo: Yeah. Yeah, they did, now you mention it. Foggy: And then someone came to talk to you? Theo: This afternoon, yeah. This old English dude comes to see me. He knew all about the creative accounting on the loan app. He said unless I could convince you to walk back everything you said about Fisk... he'd have Red Lion call the loan. Foggy: Of course. Theo: Foggy, that application... if anyone looks too carefully at it... Foggy: You're going to jail. Theo: Not just me. Mom and Dad signed it, too.

Hattley: We have a new teammate today. Take a seat, Ray. Ray: I don't believe it. Fisk's got something on all of you? Arinori: Arinori? Hattley: Better we don't talk about it. And in here, we don't even say his name. That's one of the rules, Ray. We only refer to him by his code name. Ray: What code name? Hattley: Kingpin. Hattley: Another roundup, gentlemen. And we're going to hit them fast and hard. Kingpin wants this one to make a point.

Agent 1: FBI! Don't move! Man: Shit. It's the feds! Agent 2: Down on the ground, now! Stay where you are. Man: No. Dex: John Hammer, you're coming with us. Dex: Good morning, Mr. Starr. Ray: I got this one. Please come quietly.

Dex: Shift change, guys. Alvarez: We just came on an hour ago. Dex: Hattley's orders. I think she's punishing me for getting off suspension so fast. And thanks for bringing me along for the ride. Alvarez: She's the boss. Ramsey: See you later.

Ray: So what was it? Money? I've known you for ten years, for Chrissakes. Hattley: Shut your goddamn mouth. Ray: Or what? You'll frame me for another murder? Hattley: Keep your head forward. There's no mics in here, but you know they're watching. Ray: You murdered Winn. How do you live with that? Hattley: I killed him to save your life. That's right. This is on you. I didn't tell you to break into Dex's apartment. I would've stopped you, and you wouldn't be here. But here you are. Ray: I can't believe you want this. We made this happen. We can find a way to end it. Hattley: There's no way out, Ray. Fisk's had you marked for more than a year. Ray: What do you mean, had me marked? Hattley: Why do you think your sister-in-law lost health coverage? He made you desperate for this job, you did everything you could to get him this penthouse, get him everything he asked for. Like I said, there's no way out. We're out of our league here. Ray: You could've gone to Homeland Security or the NYPD. Not take me down with you. Not murder an agent. You make a report. You get your family somewhere safe. Jesus. Hattley: That's not an option with Fisk. I used to have two children, Ray. They made it look like a hit-and-run. I got a divorce. Maybe that keeps him a little safer. But there's still Allie, so... Think about Seema and Sami. And do what Fisk tells you.

Agent: Where is Mrs. Shelby? Dex: She's on her way, sir. Fisk: No. Nadeem. Fisk: Let's go. Matt: Yeah? Ray: Fisk has left the hotel. Matt: How is that possible? Ray: I don't think Dex was the only FBI agent he turned. But he's taking Fisk to meet with other crime bosses. Some kind of sit-down. Matt: Where? Ray: I'm texting you the address. But if you catch Fisk in the act... Matt: This is our chance to take him down. Thank you, Nadeem. Fisk: We'll meet you inside, Nadeem. Dex: What do you want me to do? Fisk: Be ready. Daredevil will know it's a trap, but he'll come anyway. Automated Voice: Red Fish Blue Restaurant, 10th Street and 4th Avenue. Jack: You're not fallin' for that, are you? That guy, he ain't in your corner. Not anymore. Matt: That doesn't matter. Jack: It's been a long time since you used Muay Thai ropes, Matty. Matt: That guy in my suit kicked my ass. I can't beat him from a distance. I gotta draw him in close and do more damage. Jack: You're too mad to think straight. And it's gonna get you killed. Matty, come on. Your mother didn't only leave you. She left me, too. Matt: You looking for sympathy? 'Cause that's not happening. Jack: She left us because we're cursed. Jack: Because she knew we got the devil inside. Matt: So it's my fault? Jack: Would you be honest with yourself? You put on that mask because it lets you feel all right with who you really are. It lets you hurt people and makes you feel like it's for something important... something good, maybe even for God. But that ain't the truth, and we both know it. Fisk: You and your father are cut from the same cloth. A corrupt boxer who takes as much satisfaction in inflicting pain as he does money for taking dives. And his son, who's trying to convince himself he's any better than his criminal father. You were born from nothing. You remain nothing.

location: RED FISH BLUE RESTAURANT - INTERROGATION ROOM
scene_text: Starr: Arrest me, or I'm leaving. Agent: Stay where you are. Hammer: We have a right to counsel. Zyl: This some bullshit. Carter: What are we waiting for? Hammer: We'll know when it happens. Zyl: You know something about what's going on? Hammer: Well, they pick us up all quiet like. No press, no perp walk. Take us here instead of downtown. The feds want something. Zyl: Fisk? Starr: What the hell is this? Fisk: It's an opportunity, Mr. Starr. Fisk: I've brought you here to offer you my protection. From investigations and prosecutions by the federal government. Hammer: Bullshit. This is a sting. Carter: Hey, jury, if you can hear this on tape, I'm totally innocent. I don't even know these people. Zyl: How much? What's the vig? Hammer: Twenty percent. Fisk: For Chrissake. Of everything. Starr: I don't know how you keep that suit white with all the bullshit you pack into it. I know what this is. We all know what this is. You want us to confess to something that buys you another month in that hotel suite you conned yourself into. No. You can count me out. Fisk: The tax is now 25 percent. Zyl: I gotta hand it to you, Fisk. You know how to put on a show. Just one question. Where do I drop the cash? Ray: If you tipped him... Matt: I said exactly what you told me to say. You were there. Ray: Let's go. Doyle: Moving to Stairwell C. Weapons out.

Matt: Are you gonna kill me? Shelby: No. Not you. Matt: Fisk? Shelby: Oh, thank God. Matt: When will he be back? Shelby: Minutes. Matt: Thank you. Ramsey: Karen Page located at the Clinton Church. Keep all NYPD units clear of that location until otherwise advised. Copy? Matt: What does Fisk want with Karen? Shelby: He wants her killed.

Matt: Did you know, Father? Lantom: Matthew? What are you doing here? Matt: Did you know she was my mother? Lantom: Yeah. Matt: You knew. Lantom: I couldn't tell you. Even when I wanted to. Matt: Don't hide behind your collar, Father. Man: Wait. You're a priest? Lantom: Take your money and go. Lantom: I'm not hiding, Matthew. I'm right here. Matt: You... of all people... All those times I looked to you for guidance. You saw me struggling... and you chose to hide the one thing that could have changed everything for me. Please, Father, help me understand why you would do that. Lantom: I prayed for Maggie to find it in herself to tell you years ago. Matt: She couldn't find it in herself to walk nine blocks to visit me as a kid. Or to comfort me when my father was murdered and I thought that... I knew that I was alone in this world. Lantom: You were never alone... Matt: Yes, I was! And you let me believe it. Lantom: Yes. Yes, we did. Matt: Why? Lantom: What did Maggie say? Matt: I'm asking you. Lantom: Maggie's a good person, Matthew. Flawed, like us all. And tortured over decisions she's made. But she dedicated her life to making amends. Matt: You still haven't answered the question. Lantom: Growing up without your parents, Matthew, you don't grow to see them as people. You need to understand that... to understand her.

Girl 1: We should go. This was a stupid idea. Girl 2: Definitely. Young Maggie: No, we're here. Let's just give it a minute. Girl 1: Three weeks from now, we're not going anywhere anymore. Girl 2: True. Young Maggie: Just a minute. Jack: Hey. Young Maggie: Me? Jack: Yeah, you. Can you give me a hand up here? Young Maggie: No, I can't. Jack: Yeah, you got to. Come on, it's only gonna take me seconds to put this asshole down. Three minutes, tops. Girl 1: Okay, now is a good time to leave. Girl 2: Yes, it is. Let's go. Young Maggie: What do you need me to do? Jack: Nothing much. Just gotta give me some water, maybe wipe off my face, like that. Come on. Maggie, obedience, poverty... Young Maggie: Chastity. Jack: You ever done this before? You got brothers or something? Young Maggie: No. Never seen a fight before, either. Jack: Shit. Then why'd you pick me to come up here? Young Maggie: I just figured a nun wouldn't put something in my bottle. Jack: It's gonna be all right. You just gotta put my mouth guard in my teeth at the start of the rounds. Maybe give me some water between rounds, too. Young Maggie: I thought you said you only needed 30 seconds. Jack: Yeah. Well, it's just a backup plan. You never know. Jack: Water. Yeah, come on. I only got a minute. Can you get that? Maggie: Get that? Jack: Yeah. Maggie: Oh, yeah. Maggie'S Mother: Maggie, what is wrong with you? Maggie? Maggie. Maggie.

Lantom: Damn, I don't know what I should've done. I guess that's not really true. Matt: You know, when I heard Maggie call me her son, my thought was... my first thought... was how stupid I'd been. That it had been right in front of me for so long. And then I remembered that it had been in front of you for even longer. From... From the beginning. We've talked so much about truth... you and I. Of my truth, God's truth. Now it seems like all those conversations were just a goddamned lie. Shame on you.

Hattley: We couldn't do this at the office? We had to come all the way out here? Winn: Once I explain everything to you and the SAC, you'll understand, sir. Hattley: Shit, I better. Ray: Sorry about this, boss. Winn: Come in, guys. Girl: Mom? Allison: Where did you put them? Hattley: Give me a sec? Allison: Like you'd understand. Hattley: I understand, Allison. I just don't care. Now, move it. Allison: Make sure your dad signs those papers. Hattley: I know. I know. Bye, Mom. Hattley: At least she talks to you. I can't pry my girls away from their phones. Winn: You say that like it's a bad thing. Hattley: Sorry about the mess. My contractor promised he would be done months ago. How do you take it? Winn: Black is fine, thanks. Ray: Uh, none for me. Thanks. Winn: Interview with Special Agent Rahul Nadeem and Special Agent in Charge Tammy Hattley, conducted by Supervisory Special Agent Winn, FBI Office of Professional Responsibility. Winn: Okay, Ray. You've got our attention. What's this about? Ray: There's no good way for me to say this. But I believe Wilson Fisk is currently engaged in a criminal conspiracy and has manipulated the bureau into becoming his unwitting accomplice. I also have reason to believe that Fisk has corrupted an agent on his detail. Hattley: Who? Ray: Dex. Winn: You're referring to Special Agent Ben Poindexter? Ray: Yes, sir. And as crazy as it sounds, I think Poindexter may have perpetrated the attack at the Bulletin. Hattley: What the hell are you talking about? Why would you think that? Ray: Because while I was pursuing those suspicions yesterday... Dex shot me. Winn: Jesus Christ. Ray: Sir, OPR needs to start an internal investigation into Fisk, into Poindexter, into all of it. And for the record... this was on my watch. I personally ran Fisk's detail. SAC Hattley did everything by the book, and this shouldn't fall on her. I take full responsibility. Winn: Ray, I'm sorry, but I'm placing you on administrative leave, effective immediately. Ray: I understand. And will cooperate fully. Hattley: So... what do we do next? Winn: First, we call you an ambulance. Ray: No! Ray! Put down the gun! Please! Dex: Damn you, Ray. You bring this into my house? My home? Sit down. Sit. Dex: Your prints, your weapon, the recording. Do I need to explain to you what this means? Answer my question, please. Do you understand your situation now? Hattley: Ray? Dex: You get this? Ray: Yeah, boss. I understand. Hattley: I'm not your boss anymore. Wilson Fisk is.

Foggy: You don't have to run. Hiding is an option. Karen: I'm not so sure it is, Foggy. Not after what I said to Fisk. Foggy: Where will you go? Karen: I don't know. But I wouldn't bother paying the rent like we did for Matt. Foggy: Come on. You'll be back. Karen: Foggy, Fisk is never gonna stop hunting me. Foggy: Then don't run or hide. Do what I did. Make yourself so public he can't touch you. Karen: Yeah, well, it's not gonna matter, Foggy. Foggy: My DA campaign's kept me out of his crosshairs so far. Karen: Yeah, well, you didn't confess to killing his BFF, so... Foggy: Valid point. But maybe... Karen: Look, Foggy. I'm running. Karen: Right after I tell Matt I completely betrayed him. Foggy: Come on. You didn't betray him. Karen: Fisk knows that Matt is Daredevil because of me. Foggy: He can't actually know that for sure. You didn't say anything. Karen: No, you weren't there. He, uh... The way he looked at me... He knows. Karen: Just, uh, destroy these for me? Foggy: No, Foggy... Karen: Please take it. Foggy: Thank you. I should go. We're gonna get through this. I don't know how, but we will. Watch your back. Please.

Maggie: Change can be scary, Marcus. Even when it's for the good. Marcus: No, it's not. Maggie: Oh... You know, the Dockerys are a wonderful family, and now you get to be a part of it. But you will always be a part of our family, too. Maggie: Maggie. Lantom: What is it, Paul? Lantom: Matthew knows. Maggie: Oh...
Jack: I guess you know everything now, Matty. Young Matt: Everything I need to. Jack: Meh. Doesn't change a goddamn thing.

Seema: Ray? Ray: Yeah? Seema: You have a visitor from work. Sami: My hand's not big enough. Dex: Sure it is. Look. Just keep your fingers like that, hugging the seam, and just snap your wrist when you release it. Sami: And that makes it curve? Dex: Like crazy. Ray: There he is. Morning, Ray. Sami: Dad, he's teaching me how to throw a curveball. Seema: You want eggs? Dex: Uh, no, thanks. Ray: Go get ready for school, Sami. Sami: But, Dad... Ray: School first, kid. Sami: Okay. This is cool. Thanks, Mr. Poindexter. Dex: Call me Dex. Your dad and me go way back. Ray: So, Dex, what brings you to my house? Dex: Well, you've been bragging about Seema's cooking for so long, I figured I'd come up with an excuse to finally come try it. Ray: You could have called. I would have made sure there was enough to go around. Dex: You guys are so sweet to each other. Ray: What do you want, Dex? Dex: Kingpin sent me here to make sure you understand the consequences of not doing what you're told. For you. For your family. Ray: Get out of my house. Dex: I know you think you're the good guy. That you're doing the right thing, but... you're not. You crossed a line, Ray. And you can't come back. Dex: I'll get it. Delivery Woman: Delivery for Nadeem? Dex: Yeah, that's me. Delivery Woman: Sign here, please. Dex: Thanks. Dex: This must be for you. Dex: Message from Kingpin. He says you did this. And if you don't fall in line, your family's next.
